suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected process execution under FortiSandbox service context (e.g., fortisandbox user/service account). Baseline normal processes and flag deviations, especially shell interpreters (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, /bin/bash) launched from FortiSandbox processes with unusual parent-child chains.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Service Exposure Hunt (Asset Inventory)
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends 'standard asset-exposure hunt' for CVE-2026-25089 using template approach, but pipeline generated no asset discovery use case despite guidance provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query for exposed FortiSandbox service ports/endpoints in your environment using vulnerability scanner data, network flow data, or CDR logs. Cross-reference with patch inventory to identify systems running vulnerable versions (pre-2026-07-19 patches). Prioritize external-facing instances as T1190 exploitation requires public accessibility.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiSandbox CVE-2026-25089 Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'match against your vulnerability scanner' for CVE-2026-25089, but no IOC or use case was generated for this primary detection method.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest CVE-2026-25089 CVE feed into vulnerability management platform. Alert on any detection of Fortinet FortiSandbox or Fortinet FortiSandbox Cloud instances in your asset inventory. Flag as critical priority due to CISA KEV active exploitation status and federal due date 2026-07-19. Cross-reference with patch deployment logs to identify unpatched systems.

suggestion.title: Failed Authentication Attempts to FortiSandbox APIs
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'unauthenticated attacker' exploiting the service — no use case for detecting initial reconnaissance or failed auth patterns from reconnaissance attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiSandbox API/web interface logs for patterns of unauthenticated access attempts, parameter fuzzing, or requests with unusual User-Agent strings. Since exploitation is unauthenticated, baseline normal API traffic and alert on sources making requests without valid credentials or suspicious header manipulation.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Unauthenticated HTTP Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests.' Pipeline generated zero detection for this vector despite it being the attack mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to FortiSandbox admin endpoints (known ports: 8008, 8443, 443) originating from external IPs without prior authentication context. Correlate with subsequent process creation events on the FortiSandbox host showing shell command execution (cmd.exe, /bin/bash, /bin/sh) spawned from HTTP handler processes (e.g., tomcat, nginx).

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Child Process Spawning from HTTP Handler
suggestion.rationale: The vulnerability explicitly enables 'execute unauthorized commands.' Pipeline missed detection of the execution phase—monitoring for shell processes spawned by FortiSandbox handlers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on FortiSandbox daemon or web handler process (java, python, nginx, tomcat) spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, /bin/bash, or /bin/sh as a child process, especially if preceded by inbound HTTP POST requests to non-standard URIs or requests with command-like payloads in headers or body.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-25089 Patch Remediation Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Federal patch due: 2026-07-19.' Pipeline omitted the critical compliance and asset-tracking UC tied to the patch deadline and CISA mandate.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track all Fortinet FortiSandbox (on-prem, Cloud, PaaS) instances in your environment via asset inventory and vulnerability scanner findings for CVE-2026-25089. Cross-reference patch dates against the federal deadline (2026-07-19); flag any unpatched or unconfirmed instances after the deadline for immediate escalation and remediation.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Product Instance Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies three affected products (FortiSandbox, FortiSandbox Cloud, FortiSandbox PaaS). Pipeline produced no asset-discovery or enumeration UC to identify exposed instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all Fortinet FortiSandbox endpoints accessible from external or untrusted networks via port scanning, DNS discovery (*.forticloud.com, *.fortisandbox.com domains), and cloud provider APIs. Flag any publicly routable or internet-facing admin interfaces (default ports: 8008, 8443) and correlate against a baseline of approved external services.

suggestion.title: Suspicious HTTP Payload Patterns to FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'specifically crafted HTTP requests' as the delivery vector. No detection rule was generated to identify the exploitation payloads themselves.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to FortiSandbox endpoints for patterns indicative of command injection (shell metacharacters: pipe, semicolon, backtick, $(), command substitution patterns, escape sequences) in request headers (User-Agent, Referer, Cookie) or POST body. Flag requests without valid session tokens or authentication headers combined with suspicious payload patterns.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability affects 'public-facing' FortiSandbox and is actively exploited by unauthenticated attackers. Pipeline generated no asset-exposure hunt despite referencing template at ../_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify FortiSandbox instances (CloudProbe, management console, PaaS endpoints) listening on internet-facing ports. Check for CVE-2026-25089 presence in vulnerability scanner output. Cross-reference against patch inventory for systems not yet patched by deadline 2026-07-19.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Request to FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically notes exploitation via 'specifically crafted HTTP requests.' This HTTP pattern should be a distinct detection UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to FortiSandbox endpoints for unusual URI patterns, suspicious parameter encoding, or shell metacharacters in request body/headers. CISA KEV entry implies specific attack vectors are actively weaponized.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Execution from FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers can 'execute unauthorized commands' via the vulnerability. Pipeline failed to generate command-execution detection despite this being the exploitation outcome.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process spawning from FortiSandbox daemon/service processes (fortisandbox-daemon, sandboxd, etc.) with unexpected parent-child relationships. Look for shell execution (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, /bin/bash, /bin/sh) or suspicious command-line arguments originating from FortiSandbox process context.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Network Egress from FortiSandbox Process
suggestion.rationale: Injected commands may establish C2 or lateral movement. Article does not specify payload behavior, but command execution primitives warrant network-behavioral detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline FortiSandbox network behavior and alert on deviations: new outbound connections to non-Fortinet infrastructure, unusual protocols, or connections to known malicious IP ranges.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Container/Sandbox Escape Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions FortiSandbox Cloud and PaaS variants, implying containerized deployments. OS command injection in containerized contexts may indicate escape attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious syscalls from FortiSandbox container processes (ptrace, mount, namespace creation, cgroup manipulation). Alert on any process attempting to interact with host kernel or escape sandbox boundaries.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiSandbox CVE-2026-25089 Vulnerability Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies CVE-2026-25089 as CISA KEV (actively exploited in wild) and explicitly directs to 'asset-exposure hunt' with template substitution. Pipeline generated zero use cases. Federal patch due 2026-07-19.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner logs for Fortinet FortiSandbox, FortiSandbox Cloud, or FortiSandbox PaaS instances with CVE-2026-25089 or missing patches dated after 2026-07-19. Correlate inventory with external-facing asset database to identify exposed instances requiring immediate remediation.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Unauthenticated Command Injection Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests' — direct exploitation pathway with no auth required.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web service process associated with FortiSandbox for child process creation (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, /bin/bash). Correlate with HTTP request logs to FortiSandbox endpoints, flagging requests with encoded payloads or shell metacharacters (pipe, semicolon, backtick). Alert on process lineage: web service → shell command execution.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiSandbox External Network Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes unauthenticated remote exploitation via HTTP — implies internet-facing infrastructure. Standard CISA KEV remediation includes inventory and exposure assessment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query network logs for inbound connections to Fortinet FortiSandbox management/API ports (default 80, 443, 8080, 8443) from untrusted networks. Baseline historical external traffic; flag any FortiSandbox instances receiving internet-routable traffic outside security boundary.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated HTTP Access to FortiSandbox Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests' — establishes HTTP-based initial access without authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP POST/GET requests to FortiSandbox administrative or API endpoints from external networks without corresponding authentication events. Flag request patterns immediately preceding process execution or unusual HTTP status codes.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Service Child Process Spawning
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'OS command injection vulnerability' — direct implication is arbitrary command execution via child processes spawned from the vulnerable service.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected child processes spawned by FortiSandbox service (parent: sandbox.exe or fgsandbox) with suspicious command lines (cmd.exe, powershell, bash, sh with unusual arguments). Cross-correlate with unauthenticated HTTP access in preceding 5 minutes.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner Detection for CVE-2026-25089
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV designation indicates active exploitation in the wild. Reconnaissance scans for this CVE should trigger asset-exposure hunts given federal remediation deadline of 2026-07-19.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for third-party vulnerability scanner hits specifically targeting FortiSandbox version detection or public IP enumeration queries listing Fortinet products. Cross-check with internal inventory to confirm exposure status.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Payload Patterns in HTTP Requests to FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'specifically crafted HTTP requests' as the attack vector — payload inspection is necessary to detect injection attempts before execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect HTTP request bodies to FortiSandbox endpoints for command injection metacharacters and patterns: $(cmd), backtick substitution, pipe (|), semicolon (;), ampersand (&), output redirect (>, <), newlines, and URL-encoded variants in parameter values.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Network Egress After Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Successful OS command injection enables secondary actions; C2 or data exfiltration traffic typically originates from the compromised FortiSandbox host.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound DNS and HTTP/S traffic from FortiSandbox host to external destinations not in whitelist of known update/telemetry servers. Prioritize alerts if initiated within minutes of unauthenticated HTTP access attempts.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Public Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' applies and references template substitution. CISA KEV status means active in-the-wild exploitation against exposed instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for FortiSandbox (all variants: on-prem, Cloud, PaaS) instances exposed on internet-facing borders. Cross-check against patch management for CVE-2026-25089 remediation status. High priority: patch lag is the silent killer per article body.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox HTTP Command Injection Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests' — explicit payload pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiSandbox access logs for HTTP requests containing OS command syntax (backticks, $(), semicolons, pipes, |&) in query/POST parameters. Flag unauthenticated requests reaching FortiSandbox API endpoints. Correlate with CVE-2026-25089 exploit PoC signatures if available.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Authentication Bypass Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'unauthenticated attacker' can reach admin-level command execution — evidence of auth bypass chaining with RCE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests bypassing FortiSandbox authentication controls: missing/invalid session tokens accessing restricted endpoints, anonymous access to /admin or /cli interfaces, repeated 403→200 transitions in single session.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Unauthorized Command Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article core finding: 'execute unauthorized commands' — process/command audit logs are source of truth for active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On vulnerable FortiSandbox instances, hunt for sudden command execution from system processes with no corresponding admin-initiated requests. Look for reverse shells, data exfil commands, lateral movement probes initiated outside normal administration windows.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-25089 Exploitation Signature Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status guarantees active wild exploitation; network signatures should be available from threat feeds within days of publication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Deploy CVE-2026-25089 exploit signatures to edge networks. Monitor for HTTP POST/GET to FortiSandbox endpoints with known PoC payloads (check Exploit-DB, GitHub, vendor advisories post-2026-07-16). Federal due date 2026-07-19 creates 3-day exploitation window rush.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiSandbox Remote Code Execution Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article states RCE capability via OS command injection; post-exploitation activities (data theft, persistence, lateral movement) are common sequelae.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-compromise: monitor FortiSandbox for unexpected outbound connections, scheduled task creation, credential dumping utilities, or ransomware-staging activities. Correlate temporal cluster of suspicious commands on vulnerable assets with external IP reputation feeds.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Public-Facing Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated attacker' can exploit via 'HTTP requests' against FortiSandbox instances. Standard asset-exposure hunt is the canonical first response to any unauthenticated RCE per threat profile.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify publicly-exposed Fortinet FortiSandbox, FortiSandbox Cloud, and FortiSandbox PaaS instances via DNS resolution, port scanning, and service fingerprinting. Correlate CVE-2026-25089 vulnerability scanner results with network exposure to prioritize remediation against federal deadline (2026-07-19).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-25089 Vulnerability Scanner Detections
suggestion.rationale: Article is CISA KEV entry: 'observed exploited in the wild.' Any scanner hit is actionable urgency regardless of reported patch status. Federal civilian agencies required to remediate by 2026-07-19.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for CVE-2026-25089 detections across all FortiSandbox product variants. Escalate immediately; CISA KEV status means exploitation observed in wild, patch lag is 'silent killer' per threat profile.

suggestion.title: HTTP Command Injection Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack delivery mechanism: 'specifically crafted HTTP requests.' Must detect payloads attempting OS command injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests targeting FortiSandbox endpoints for command injection markers (backticks, $(), semicolons, pipes, shell metacharacters) in URL parameters and POST bodies. Validate against FortiSandbox WAF/IPS sensor logs for correlation.

suggestion.title: Process Execution from FortiSandbox Application Context
suggestion.rationale: Article outcome: 'execute unauthorized commands.' Successful exploitation spawns processes under FortiSandbox app identity, anomalous to baseline service behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On systems running vulnerable FortiSandbox versions, monitor for unexpected child process creation (shells, command interpreters, curl, wget) initiated by FortiSandbox processes. Establish baseline of legitimate administrative commands; alert on deviations, especially preceded by external unauthenticated HTTP traffic.

suggestion.title: Outbound Command-and-Control from Compromised FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: Successfully exploited command-injection can pivot to lateral movement or C2. Monitor for attacker-directed outbound network activity from FortiSandbox appliances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from FortiSandbox instances to non-standard destinations, anomalous ports, or known attacker infrastructure. Baseline should reflect only expected Fortinet management, update, and sandbox-legitimate cloud traffic.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Service Failure or Abnormal Restart Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Command injection exploitation may crash or destabilize service. Application logs can reveal forensic trace of attack attempts even if direct payload is not logged.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiSandbox application and OS logs for unexpected restarts, crashes, segfaults, or error spikes correlated with external HTTP traffic anomalies or CVE-2026-25089 scanner alerts within 0–60 minute window.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Externally Accessible FortiSandbox Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker requires 'unauthenticated' access via 'specifically crafted HTTP requests' to an exposed FortiSandbox endpoint. CISA KEV status means exploitation is active in the wild. Template-driven asset-exposure hunt referenced in article body is the canonical detection for this threat.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for inbound HTTP/HTTPS traffic to FortiSandbox management/API endpoints (default ports 10888, 10889) from external sources or suspicious originating IPs. Correlate with Fortinet asset inventory to identify instances that should not be internet-facing. Presence of traffic from non-whitelisted external IPs to these ports indicates potential exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Command Injection: Suspicious HTTP Request Payloads to FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability' exploited via 'specifically crafted HTTP requests.' No specific payload syntax is disclosed, but command injection typically uses shell metacharacters (`;`, `|`, `&&`, backticks, `$()`, etc.) in request parameters, headers, or body.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to FortiSandbox endpoints for common command injection indicators: shell metacharacters in query parameters, POST body, or headers; URL-encoded command separators; base64-encoded command strings; or requests matching known exploit POC signatures. Pair with authentication checks to ensure requests are unauthenticated.

suggestion.title: Process Execution: Unexpected Command Spawning from FortiSandbox Service
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'allows an unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands.' Successful exploitation results in command execution on the FortiSandbox host. Monitor endpoint telemetry for anomalous process spawning from FortiSandbox processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unexpected child processes spawned by FortiSandbox service accounts (e.g., `fsdb`, `admin` service user). Legitimate FortiSandbox operations spawn a known set of child processes; anomalies (reverse shells, credential dumping, lateral movement tooling) indicate exploitation. Cross-correlate with firewall/proxy logs to establish timing and HTTP trigger.

suggestion.title: Authentication Bypass: Unauthenticated Admin Function Access
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'unauthenticated attacker' can reach endpoints that should require authentication. This represents authentication bypass (T1078 adjacent). Detection should flag successful access to admin/privileged endpoints without valid authentication tokens.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiSandbox access logs for HTTP 200/302 responses to admin console, API, or config endpoints that occur without prior successful authentication (no auth cookie, token, or credential submission). Baseline legitimate admin source IPs; flag access from untrusted or external sources to these endpoints.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement: Command Execution to Adjacent Systems from FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: OS command injection on FortiSandbox allows attacker to execute arbitrary commands *on the FortiSandbox host*. If FortiSandbox has network access to internal systems, adversary can pivot laterally. Article does not detail scope but appliance position (sandbox, network visibility) implies lateral movement risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After identifying FortiSandbox compromise (via command injection detections above), hunt for suspicious outbound network connections from FortiSandbox to internal systems or external C2. Look for tunneling, port scanning, credential dumping tools, or lateral movement frameworks executed from the FortiSandbox process context.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-25089 Patch Inventory & Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies federal patch due date (2026-07-19) and emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer'; explicitly references asset-exposure hunt template. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this being the canonical detection for a CISA KEV.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for CVE-2026-25089 matches on Fortinet FortiSandbox instances. Cross-reference patch status and network exposure (internet-facing vs. internal). Flag any unpatched instances and track patch lag history against federal deadline.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox: HTTP Command Injection Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker exploits via 'specifically crafted HTTP requests' executing OS commands. No payload-level detection use case generated despite clear attack vector and exploitation methodology described.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to FortiSandbox endpoints for command injection patterns: shell metacharacters (backticks, $(), |, ;, &), environment variable expansion, command substitution syntax. Correlate with HTTP 200/502 responses and unexpected process spawning.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox: Unauthorized Process Execution from Service Account
suggestion.rationale: OS command injection vulnerability enables arbitrary command execution. Article specifies 'execute unauthorized commands'—process-telemetry detection should capture resulting RCE, but pipeline omitted execution phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor child processes spawned by FortiSandbox services (especially Java/web processes). Alert on unexpected system binaries (sh, cmd.exe, powershell), reverse-shell tools (nc, socat), or data exfiltration commands (curl, wget) with FortiSandbox service account lineage.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox: Unauthenticated HTTP Access to Vulnerable Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'unauthenticated attacker' as precondition. No authentication-bypass or anonymity detection use case generated despite this being the critical access-control failure enabling exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to FortiSandbox administrative or API endpoints lacking valid authentication tokens/sessions. Alert on requests from external IP ranges or high-velocity reconnaissance patterns (parameter fuzzing, endpoint enumeration).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-58644 SharePoint RCE Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'CISA Adds Exploited SharePoint RCE Zero-Day CVE-2026-58644 to KEV.' Exploit is confirmed active and tracked. Pipeline output: zero use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SharePoint servers (w3wp.exe, iisreset.exe) for HTTP POST/OPTIONS requests to known vulnerable endpoints (e.g., /_vti_bin/*, /sites/*, /_api/*) with suspicious payloads or anomalous parameter encoding. Correlate with 4xx/5xx error spikes followed by successful process creation from w3wp context.

suggestion.title: w3wp.exe Child Process Execution from SharePoint
suggestion.rationale: RCE exploitation results in arbitrary code execution within SharePoint worker process. Article establishes RCE impact but pipeline surfaced no execution-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag child processes spawned by w3wp.exe (typically processes do not spawn children) running cmd.exe, powershell.exe, certutil.exe, or whoami.exe. Unusually, baseline SharePoint should show zero or near-zero child process creation from w3wp; any activity is suspicious.

suggestion.title: SharePoint Server Lateral Movement – Admin Share Access
suggestion.rationale: Article describes active RCE exploitation but no detection for post-exploitation lateral movement or privilege escalation typical after SharePoint compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect net.exe, nltest.exe, or PsExec execution spawned from compromised SharePoint server. Monitor for SMB (port 445) connections from SharePoint host to internal domain controllers or sensitive file shares. Correlate with credential access patterns (sekurlsa, mimikatz artifacts).

suggestion.title: Suspicious ASPX or DLL Creation in SharePoint Web Paths
suggestion.rationale: RCE attackers typically drop webshells or DLLs into web-accessible directories for persistence. Article mentions RCE but no detection for post-exploitation persistence mechanisms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor creation or modification of .aspx, .asp, .jsp, .dll files in SharePoint paths (/_layouts, /sites, /bin, /App_Code, default.aspx parent directories). Flag files created by w3wp.exe or unexpected service accounts. Correlate timing with known exploitation windows (CISA alert date).

suggestion.title: SharePoint Suspicious Outbound C2 or Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Compromised SharePoint servers frequently contact external C2 or exfiltrate data. Article does not detail post-exploitation C2 activity, but RCE severity implies this is a probable secondary attack phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound HTTPS/HTTP from w3wp.exe or related SharePoint processes to external IPs or suspicious domains. Flag DNS queries from SharePoint server for unusual domains (not in baseline). Detect abnormal volume of data transfer or connections to known malware C2 infrastructure.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-58644 – Vendor Advisory and Patch Detection Gap
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates CISA KEV listing. Pipeline should have flagged the vulnerability IOC itself plus created detection for systems NOT patched or systems executing traffic patterns matching known PoC code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory all SharePoint servers by version and patch level. Flag any running versions known vulnerable to CVE-2026-58644 without corresponding security updates. Correlate with network telemetry showing exploitation attempts (above rules) against unpatched systems.

suggestion.title: Successful login as 'admin' followed by file/terminal abuse within Pheditor
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'any deployment using the default credentials grants an attacker full access to the file editor, file upload, and terminal features.' Detects post-auth exploitation. Requires log-access to Pheditor session/auth events or host-side monitoring of access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP POST to pheditor.php?action=login with password=admin (or auth-log success for 'admin' user) + subsequent file operations (write to web-root, terminal command execution) within 5 minutes. Successful auth + immediate RCE behavior is high-confidence exploitation.

suggestion.title: Pheditor.php deployed to web-accessible directory without access controls
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates Pheditor ships and is deployed; 'There is no mechanism to force a password change on first login' implies deployment as-is. Detect initial staging/deployment as a precursor hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for pheditor.php creation in web-root directories (/var/www/html, /srv/www, C:\inetpub\wwwroot, etc.). Especially suspicious if deployed without a .htaccess or nginx config restricting access, or if deployment pre-dates any managed change logs.

suggestion.title: Password-change enforcement bypass or skipped (Pheditor initial-login flow)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly notes 'There is no mechanism to force a password change on first login.' This is the vulnerability's core: lack of security hygiene enforcement. Detect when admin user skips or bypasses password reset prompts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If Pheditor logs or session tracking is available, detect 'admin' user logins that proceed directly to terminal/file operations without completing forced password-change flow, or session tokens that remain valid past expected credential-reset timestamps.

suggestion.title: Web-server process file I/O to web-root combined with suspicious process spawn
suggestion.rationale: Article describes both 'file upload' and 'terminal features.' Combine file-write (UC_6_3 standalone) with process-spawn (UC_6_2 standalone) to detect full exploitation chain in a single burst.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Within a 10-second window: PHP/web-process writes a .php file to web-root AND same process or child forks a shell (sh, bash, cmd.exe). Higher fidelity than either hunt alone; reduces FPs from routine updates.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-55579 / Pheditor asset inventory and exposure assessment
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline output showed zero IOC extraction. CVE-2026-55579 should be mapped to all known Pheditor versions/deployments in asset inventory. Prerequisite for risk prioritization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan asset database and software inventory tools for Pheditor installations or project artifacts matching CVE-2026-55579 affected versions. Cross-reference with public-facing service scans (shodan, censys, internal port-scans) to identify internet-exposed instances.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Processes from Game Application Parents
suggestion.rationale: Article headline 'Game Cheat Spyware' indicates malware delivered as or bundled with game cheating tools. Legitimate game launchers do not spawn shell/interpreter processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when game-related executables (steam.exe, launcher.exe, anticheat*.exe, gameupdate*.exe) spawn cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash.exe, or Python/Perl interpreters. Monitor for unusual network connection from child processes within 30 seconds of parent launch.

suggestion.title: Rapid File Encryption and Ransom Note Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article references '24-Hour Ransomware' — unusual ransomware that deploys and demands payment within 24 hours. Detection should focus on compression of attack timeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate mass file encryption (volume shadow copy deletion + >1000 unique file extensions modified in <5 minutes) with ransom note file creation (.txt, .html, .bmp) in system root or user Desktop. Alert if timeline from first encrypted file to ransom note display is <15 minutes.

suggestion.title: Chrome Sync Profile Abuse and Lateral Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article headline 'Chrome Sync Stalking' indicates attackers abusing Chrome's cloud sync feature for reconnaissance or espionage. Normal users do not authenticate sync to multiple external accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Chrome profile creation or re-authentication flows (chrome.exe --profile-directory, google.com/accounts/signin). Alert on sync.google.com traffic originating from internal networks; flag when Chrome browser accesses sensitive file paths (Documents, Downloads) immediately before or after sync re-auth event.

suggestion.title: Malware Distribution via Gaming Platforms
suggestion.rationale: Game cheat malware is typically distributed via trojanized download sites or social engineering. Article headline 'Game Cheat Spyware' implies a distribution mechanism requiring detection at entry point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect downloads from gaming/cheat-themed domains (regex: cheat|hack|mod|bypass|undetected in URL) that deliver executable files. Correlate with suspicious domain registration (WHOIS age <30 days) or free CDN hosting. Flag subsequent network beaconing from downloaded binary.

suggestion.title: Spyware Data Exfiltration via Game Process
suggestion.rationale: Article reference to 'Game Cheat Spyware' indicates payload includes reconnaissance/data theft capability bundled with cheat functionality.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor game launcher processes for access to sensitive file paths (browser cookies, credential stores, Documents folder) not normally required for game execution. Alert on unexpected registry reads targeting HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion or user profile paths combined with outbound HTTP/HTTPS to non-gaming C2 infrastructure.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-25089 Vulnerable Version Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names affected products (FortiSandbox, FortiSandbox Cloud, FortiSandbox PaaS) and federal patch due date. Standard asset-exposure hunt requirement.

suggestion.title: npm Preinstall Script Execution from Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly references 'malicious preinstall binary' — npm's preinstall lifecycle hook runs arbitrary code before package extraction. This is the core delivery mechanism and should trigger process spawning detections linked to package managers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child processes spawned by npm/yarn/pnpm package manager contexts where parent command includes 'install'. Establish baseline of legitimate preinstall scripts and alert on deviations. Correlate with suspicious network or file I/O from preinstall execution.

suggestion.title: Malicious npm Package Registry Installation
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attack vector: 'jscrambler npm package publishes' indicates compromise at registry or naming level. Detection must identify installation of known-malicious packages and suspicious package names.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm/yarn package-lock.json and node_modules directory additions for known-malicious package names. Alert on installations from public npm registry of packages matching known malicious hashes or signatures. Establish threat-intel feeds of compromised package names and versions.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Process Spawning from npm Preinstall Execution Context
suggestion.rationale: Preinstall scripts are expected to perform build/setup tasks only. Article implies this binary performs malicious actions beyond legitimate package prep—unusual spawning (network, credential access, lateral movement) should flag malicious preinstall injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish whitelist of expected child processes from known preinstall scripts. Alert on fork/exec of cmd.exe, powershell.exe, curl, wget, or network tools from npm preinstall context. Monitor for file access to sensitive dirs (%APPDATA%, %ProgramFiles%) from preinstall.

suggestion.title: Binary Download and Execution During npm Package Install
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'publishes malicious preinstall binary'—likely fetches or embeds binary during install. Detection should catch suspicious file download/execution chains tied to package installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for binary downloads (exe, dll, elf) initiated during npm install phase. Correlate HTTP requests originating from npm preinstall context with subsequent process execution. Alert on binaries written to temp directories and immediately executed.

suggestion.title: npm Registry or Package Metadata Tampering Detection
suggestion.rationale: Attack succeeded because registry was either compromised or account was hijacked. Detection should identify package version downgrades, metadata mismatches, or unexpected version pushes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm registry API calls for unusual package publish/update activity from compromised account IPs. Alert on package.json version constraints that install unexpected versions. Cross-reference installed package hashes against known-good registry manifests.

Alert on any vulnerable instance Internet-routable or accessible from untrusted network segments. Escalate based on days-to-patch deadline (2026-07-19) vs. current date.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Exposure Hunt

suggestion.title: Suspicious HTTP Payloads to FortiSandbox

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST/GET requests to FortiSandbox API endpoints (e.g., /fnsysreport, /feapi) containing shell metacharacters (backticks, $(), pipes, semicolons, && operators) or URL-encoded command sequences. Flag requests with unusual Content-Length or polyglot payloads.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Process Execution on FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: Article core impact: 'execute unauthorized commands' on appliance; pipeline failed to map post-exploitation detection despite explicit command-execution language.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiSandbox OS process logs for child processes spawned by httpd/web-server processes. Alert on non-whitelist commands (bash, sh, curl, wget, nc, perl, python) executed with SYSTEM/root context in response to HTTP API calls.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-25089 Vulnerability Scanner Match

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any vulnerability scanner positives for CVE-2026-25089 against Fortinet FortiSandbox, FortiSandbox Cloud, or FortiSandbox PaaS instances. Correlate with asset inventory to verify patch status against 2026-07-19 federal due date.

suggestion.title: Authentication Bypass Attempts to FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is explicitly 'unauthenticated'; pipeline should have generated detection for access-control bypass given the authentication-exempt nature of exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiSandbox authentication logs for successful API/admin access from sources with no prior authentication session or invalid/missing credentials. Baseline normal admin IP ranges; flag access from new/untrusted sources, especially if followed by process execution events.

suggestion.title: Detect Command Injection in Siemens ROX II CLI
suggestion.rationale: Keywords explicitly state 'command injection' as attack vector. Article describes 'three chained zero-day vulnerabilities' leading to 'terminal' access; command injection is the likely entry point in the exploit sequence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Siemens ROX II CLI protocols for abnormal command sequences containing shell metacharacters (|, &, ;, $(), backticks) or escape attempts. Correlate suspicious CLI injection patterns with subsequent privilege escalation attempts to confirm exploit chain execution.

suggestion.title: Detect Three-Stage Privilege Escalation Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article title 'Three Steps to the Terminal' and description explicitly reference 'three chained zero-day vulnerabilities' enabling privilege escalation. Each CVE likely represents one escalation stage; detection must account for the staged nature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for privilege transitions on Siemens ROX II. Alert on three related privilege escalation events or three distinct process elevation attempts clustered within 5–10 minutes, progressing from low privilege toward root. Flag repeated escalation attempts across different vulnerability exploitation methods.

suggestion.title: Detect Persistent Root Access Installation
suggestion.rationale: Description explicitly states goal is 'persistent root access.' Root-level persistence post-exploitation is the final stage of the described attack chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Siemens ROX II for root-initiated persistence mechanisms: new system accounts, service installations, cron/scheduling entries, or boot-start modifications introduced immediately after privilege escalation. Baseline normal root activity to isolate anomalous persistence patterns.

suggestion.title: Exploit Chain Temporal Correlation and Progression
suggestion.rationale: Keywords 'exploit chain' and title 'three steps' describe a coordinated, sequential attack. Detection should trigger on the logical progression and temporal clustering of all three stages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Build correlation rules for Siemens ROX II that alert when three or more exploitation indicators (command injection attempts, escalation privilege transitions, process anomalies) occur in sequence within a 10-minute window, consistent with active execution of the documented three-stage zero-day chain.

suggestion.title: ClickFix Social Engineering Lure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'ClickFix Lures' as the delivery mechanism. ClickFix is a known scareware/fake-repair tactic that should trigger detection on suspicious redirect chains and phishing indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for ClickFix campaign indicators: known malicious domains serving fake 'repair needed' popups, suspicious .js or .zip downloads from credential-harvesting endpoints, and suspicious PowerShell/CMD spawned from browser processes with user-agent patterns typical of ClickFix redirects.

suggestion.title: ACR Stealer Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article names ACR Stealer as the payload. Should detect execution by process name, command-line artifacts, file write patterns, or known hash signatures if available.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect ACR Stealer execution: monitor for process names or file paths containing 'acr' or known variant names, suspicious file writes to temp directories with stealer-typical naming, or behavioral anomalies (enumeration of %APPDATA%\*\User Data for browser profiles).

suggestion.title: Browser Token and Credential File Access
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'steal browser tokens and Microsoft 365 files.' Should detect unauthorized reads from browser storage (Chrome/Edge user data, Firefox profile dirs) and M365 credential caches.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process access to browser credential stores: reads of %APPDATA%\Local\Google\Chrome\User Data\*, %APPDATA%\Local\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*, or Firefox profile directories; also monitor for suspicious reads of .config/microsoft/* or MSAL token cache files on endpoints with M365 users.

suggestion.title: Unusual Microsoft 365 File Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'Microsoft 365 Files' as collection target. Should detect large or suspicious file transfers from OneDrive, SharePoint, or Teams after credential compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect M365 exfil post-compromise: baseline file download/sync volume from OneDrive or SharePoint by user; flag anomalies (bulk downloads from non-typical client IP, unusual sync patterns, or access to sensitive file shares at off-hours or by new IPs not in user's baseline).

suggestion.title: PowerShell/CMD Execution from Browser Context
suggestion.rationale: ClickFix and infostealer chains commonly spawn shell commands from browser processes (iexplore, chrome, edge) to download payloads. Should detect parent-child process anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag powershell.exe or cmd.exe spawned as child of browser processes (chrome.exe, msedge.exe, iexplore.exe, firefox.exe) especially with network I/O in command line; correlate with file write to temp or Download folder for .exe/.zip payloads.

suggestion.title: ACR Stealer C2 Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Infostealer operations require command-and-control communication. Article does not name C2 infrastructure, but any IOC list from the article should include exfil destinations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Once C2 domains/IPs are published in IOC feeds, monitor for outbound connections to known ACR Stealer C2 infrastructure; baseline user's normal DNS/network behavior and alert on anomalous geoIP or suspicious TLDs (newly registered, bulletproof hosters).

suggestion.title: Spear phishing targeting Southeast Asian government and diplomatic mail
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'targets Southeast Asian governments and diplomats' — initial access vector almost certainly phishing. No UC generated despite this being the entry point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor email to government/diplomatic domain mailboxes for external attachment-based phishing or credential-harvesting links. Flag messages with lures referencing trade agreements, diplomatic correspondence, or geopolitical events. Correlate successful delivery with downstream malware execution events.

suggestion.title: GoSerpent malware execution from Office macro or embedded script
suggestion.rationale: Malware delivery almost certainly via Office document macro or script-based execution; article mentions 'GoSerpent malware' but no execution detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Office application (WINWORD.EXE, EXCEL.EXE) spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or other interpreters. Monitor for suspicious image loads (uncommon DLLs) immediately after Office process launch. Flag execution from %TEMP% or %AppData% shortly after email delivery.

suggestion.title: Credential harvesting and lateral movement post-compromise
suggestion.rationale: Espionage campaign targeting diplomats implies theft of sensitive credentials or access tokens. Pipeline missed credential-access phase entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-infection, monitor for lsass.exe or mimikatz behavior, LSASS memory dumps, or enumeration of cached credentials. Watch for unusual NTLM authentication failures followed by successes from compromised host. Flag keylogger-like input capture DLL loads.

suggestion.title: GoSerpent command-and-control beaconing to identified C2 infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: No IOCs extracted means no C2 domains or IPs surfaced. Espionage malware will beacon; absence of C&C detection use case is a major gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify malware C2 infrastructure (if IOCs are recovered post-article publication). Monitor for outbound HTTPS/HTTP from compromised diplomatic systems to suspicious domains or IPs. Flag beaconing patterns (periodic connections, consistent user-agent, encrypted payloads) to non-standard ports.

suggestion.title: Bulk data exfiltration from government systems post-GoSerpent compromise
suggestion.rationale: Espionage objective requires data theft. Pipeline generated no exfiltration detection despite 'espionage' goal being explicit in title.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual outbound data volume from diplomatic/government file servers post-compromise. Flag bulk access to shared drives, email archives, or document repositories followed by network exfiltration. Correlate high-volume outbound connections to C2 with local file read patterns indicative of collection.

suggestion.title: Anti-analysis and persistence mechanisms in GoSerpent samples
suggestion.rationale: Sophisticated espionage malware typically employs defense-evasion and persistence. Pipeline missed defense_evasion and persistence kill-chain phases entirely.

Flag anti-debugging techniques (IsDebuggerPresent, CheckRemoteDebuggerPresent). Detect persistence via scheduled tasks with randomized or suspicious names, or WMI event subscriptions.

suggestion.title: W3WP Process Spawning Unexpected Child Processes
suggestion.rationale: SharePoint RCE (CVE-2026-58644) exploits execute arbitrary code in the w3wp.exe IIS worker process, often leading to cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or rundll32.exe spawning. Article context: 'exploited Sharepoint RCE' establishes code execution as outcome.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag w3wp.exe or inetinfo.exe spawning child processes outside expected application paths. Baseline: w3wp should launch only child processes related to SharePoint application pools, not interactive shells or secondary launchers.

suggestion.title: Suspicious ASP.NET/SharePoint Temporary File Creation
suggestion.rationale: RCE exploitation often writes temporary ASP.NET-compiled payloads to Temp directories or SharePoint bin folders. Article phrase 'exploited' implies payload staging and execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor C:\Windows\Temp\, C:\Windows\Microsoft.NET\Framework\Temporary ASP.NET Files, and Program Files\Common Files\Microsoft Shared\Web Server Extensions for unexpected .asp, .aspx, .dll, or .exe creation within minutes of anomalous HTTP requests to SharePoint endpoints.

suggestion.title: HTTP POST/PUT to SharePoint Upload Endpoints Without Matching Session Lifecycle
suggestion.rationale: Exploit delivery via unauthenticated or low-privilege HTTP requests to vulnerable RCE endpoints. Article implies active exploitation before patch availability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST/PUT requests to SharePoint /_api/, /layouts/, or /bin/ endpoints from external IPs with no matching GET request history, no user agent indicative of legitimate client, or requests followed immediately by error 500/502 responses and subsequent child process creation.

suggestion.title: Abnormal PowerShell Invocation from SharePoint Application Pool Identity
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation attacker behavior after RCE—launching PowerShell for lateral movement, reconnaissance, or data exfiltration. Standard follow-on to code execution vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on powershell.exe execution with parent process w3wp.exe or inetinfo.exe, especially with command-line arguments indicative of network enumeration, credential dumping, or script download (IEX, Add-Type, -enc flags).

suggestion.title: SharePoint Web.Config or Machine.Config Unauthorized Modification
suggestion.rationale: Attackers persist by injecting handlers or modules into web.config to execute code on each request. 'Exploited' vulnerability often leads to persistence attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file writes or modifications to web.config, machine.config, or root web.config in SharePoint directories outside of standard patching windows or deployment tools. Flag unauthorized edits to <handlers>, <modules>, or <system.webServer> sections.

suggestion.title: Device Code Flow Abuse — Unusual issuance or redemption
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly targets 'device code' flow for M365 compromise. Attackers ship device codes via phishing, victims redeem them granting OAuth tokens to attacker-controlled apps. Title: 'Device Code and AitM Session Theft'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Sign-in events or token issuance where device code flow is initiated from unusual IPs, followed within minutes by token redemption from a geographically distant or VPN-sourced IP. Alert on device code approval from users who didn't initiate the flow (verify with endpoint behavioral baseline).

suggestion.title: Adversary-in-the-Middle session interception — SSL/TLS certificate anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions AitM for 'session theft'. AitM attacks typically involve proxy tools or compromised network positions intercepting HTTPS. Title: 'AitM Session Theft'.

Cross-correlate with network IDS/proxy logs showing traffic through unapproved proxies, especially around M365 authentication endpoints.

suggestion.title: Microsoft 365 session token theft — Stolen token use from anomalous network
suggestion.rationale: AitM session theft implies token exfiltration and subsequent replay. Detecting legitimate session tokens used from IPs that differ sharply from user baseline is core to this attack. Phrase: 'AitM Session Theft'.

Correlate with absence of legitimate user activity at IP Y. Raise severity if simultaneous MFA bypass or impossible travel to both IPs.

suggestion.title: Phishing email with device code or fake M365 login prompt
suggestion.rationale: PhaaS campaigns deliver device codes or AitM landing pages via email. The title 'Targets Microsoft 365' and phishing-as-a-service model imply email-borne initial access. Implicit in 'Forg365 PhaaS' framing.

suggestion.title: OAuth app consent grant to risky/uncommon applications
suggestion.rationale: Device code flow or AitM interception of legitimate OAuth flows results in consent grants to attacker apps. Detecting unusual application access to M365 mailbox, calendar, or files post-compromise is critical. Implicit in device code attack mechanism.

suggestion.title: Forg365 PhaaS campaign infrastructure — Domain/IP indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article title names 'Forg365' as a specific PhaaS platform targeting M365. Threat-intel pipeline should correlate this name with known infrastructure (phishing domains, C2 IPs, hosting providers). Article URL is Hacker News; full article would likely contain IOCs.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Creation from FortiSandbox Service

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned by FortiSandbox parent process (fortisandbox.exe, java, nginx — depends on deployment) with suspicious command lines (curl, wget, nc, /bin/sh, powershell) or network operations immediately following HTTP requests from untrusted sources.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Endpoint Authentication Bypass Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'unauthenticated attacker' — implies endpoints lacking auth or accessible without credentials; prior art on FortiSandbox suggests /api/system endpoints may be exposed
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track HTTP 200/201 responses to sensitive FortiSandbox endpoints (/api/system/status, /api/upload, /api/tasks) when requests originate from non-admin source IPs or lack valid session tokens. Baseline against your environment's normal admin access patterns.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Cloud/PaaS Account Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article lists three deployments (on-prem, Cloud, PaaS); reconnaissance for exposed FortiSandbox instances is detection prerequisite before exploit attempt
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries for fortisandbox.* domains, cloud provider API logs for FortiSandbox resource enumeration, and Shodan/Censys scanning activity targeting FortiSandbox fingerprints (Server headers, specific HTTP banner strings).

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sustained spikes in 400/403/500 errors to FortiSandbox endpoints within short windows, especially when correlated with repeated requests containing URL-encoded shell metacharacters or common injection strings (e.g., %24%28, %3b%20, %7c).

suggestion.title: Outbound Network Callback from FortiSandbox Host
suggestion.rationale: Command injection often chains to reverse shell or data exfiltration; article says 'execute unauthorized commands' implying post-exploitation movement possible
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected outbound network connections (TCP/UDP) originating from FortiSandbox host IP, especially to non-corporate IPs or known C2 infrastructure. Baseline against legitimate FortiSandbox cloud update/telemetry traffic.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Exposure Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated attacker' can exploit — prerequisite is identifying exposed instances before exploitation can occur.

Query passive DNS, certificate transparency, cloud asset APIs for management interfaces on default/common ports. Asset discovery blocks exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Suspicious HTTP Requests to FortiSandbox Admin Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'specifically crafted HTTP requests' execute 'OS command injection' — HTTP logs contain injection signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt HTTP requests to FortiSandbox endpoints containing shell metacharacters (;, |, &, backtick, $(), **) or common command patterns (bash, cmd, powershell, nc, curl, wget). URL decode and check both URI and POST body. False positives: legitimate admin scripts, API use.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Command Execution from FortiSandbox Process
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'allows attacker to execute unauthorized commands' — successful exploitation spawns child processes from FortiSandbox service.

suggestion.title: Fortinet Product Version Inventory and Patch Compliance
suggestion.rationale: Article provides federal patch deadline 2026-07-19 — standard SOC scan for vulnerable versions across all Fortinet FortiSandbox deployments.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Public Exposure via CVE-2026-25089

suggestion.title: HTTP Command Injection Payload Detection (FortiSandbox)

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Command Execution from FortiSandbox Process

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated HTTP Access to FortiSandbox Admin/API Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly highlights 'unauthenticated attacker.' Pipeline did not suggest detection of missing authentication checks or bypass attempts on protected endpoints.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-25089 Exploitation Signature Detection

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated HTTP Exploitation of Fortinet FortiSandbox

suggestion.title: Child Process Spawning from FortiSandbox Service

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected child process creation under FortiSandbox service accounts (typically fortisandbox, nobody, or root). suggestion.title: CVE-2026-25089 Vulnerability Scanner Hits on Fortinet FortiSandbox

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised FortiSandbox Appliance

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox HTTP Command Injection Detection

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Process Execution Anomaly

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox CVE-2026-25089 Vulnerability Scanner Hits
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV article mandates scanning posture. Article provides CVE identifier and affected product variants; no IOC or detection suggested despite being the primary remediation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference vulnerability scanner outputs (Nessus, Qualys, Tenable) for CVE-2026-25089 against FortiSandbox, FortiSandbox Cloud, and FortiSandbox PaaS instances. Escalate any match with patch status 'Not Patched' and federal due date (2026-07-19) passed.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Unauthorized Authentication Bypass + Execution

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Outbound Network Anomalies Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Command injection typically used for C2 callbacks or data exfiltration. Article does not preclude post-exploitation lateral movement or callback. No network-layer detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from FortiSandbox infrastructure to non-Fortinet, non-approved network ranges. suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Deployment Inventory Cross-Check
suggestion.rationale: Article lists three deployment targets: 'FortiSandbox, FortiSandbox Cloud, and FortiSandbox PaaS.' Pipeline output has no guidance on surveying all three variants or correlating cloud/PaaS deployments with patch status.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-25089 Vulnerability Scanner Match Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'match against your vulnerability scanner' as primary detection method. Pipeline provided zero scanner-based hunts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify positive CVE-2026-25089 detections across Fortinet FortiSandbox, FortiSandbox Cloud, and FortiSandbox PaaS instances. High-confidence indicator of exploitable asset; prioritize by network exposure and patch lag.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox CVE-2026-25089 patch coverage verification
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names CVE-2026-25089 in CISA KEV catalog with federal patch deadline 2026-07-19. Phrase: 'CVE-2026-25089 — Fortinet FortiSandbox OS Command Injection Vulnerability' and 'Federal patch due: 2026-07-19'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and asset inventory for FortiSandbox (on-premise, Cloud, PaaS variants). Flag instances where patch level is below vendor remediation threshold or where CVE-2026-25089 scan result is positive. Cross-reference against remediation SLA targets.

suggestion.title: HTTP-based OS command injection payloads to FortiSandbox endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector explicitly described as 'unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests.' This is the exploitation mechanism; HTTP logs should contain command syntax.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search HTTP logs for requests to known FortiSandbox endpoints (dashboard, API, web console) containing command injection syntax (backticks, $(), command separators, encoded shell metacharacters). Correlate with non-200 HTTP responses or with follow-on process creation events from FortiSandbox processes.

suggestion.title: OS command execution spawned by FortiSandbox processes
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation of 'OS Command Injection Vulnerability' manifests as unauthenticated attackers executing commands. Article: 'execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child processes spawned by FortiSandbox service accounts or processes (java, fortipythonvm, fortilscript, fortisandboxd). Flag unexpected process creation (sh, bash, cmd, powershell) or command-line patterns consistent with attacker commands (reverse shells, curl, wget to external addresses, credential harvesting utilities).

suggestion.title: Network exfiltration or C2 callbacks from compromised FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: Unauthenticated RCE on perimeter appliance typically followed by attacker control and data exfiltration. Post-exploitation activity expected from successfully exploited instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For organizations with confirmed exploitation, hunt outbound connections from FortiSandbox process space to external IPs not in vendor update/support CDN ranges, unusual DNS queries for dynamic DNS domains, or connections to known attacker C2 infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated access to FortiSandbox management or API endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability explicitly requires no authentication: 'unauthenticated attacker.' Baseline legitimate authentication patterns, then flag anomalous access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search FortiSandbox access logs for HTTP requests from untrusted networks lacking valid session tokens, bearer tokens, or API credentials. Establish baselines for legitimate admin access; flag deviation (new source IPs, bulk requests from external networks, API abuse patterns).

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Unauthenticated HTTP Command Injection Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests' — this is the core attack vector and deserves a dedicated detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for HTTP requests to FortiSandbox web interface (default ports 80, 443, 8080) from external/untrusted sources. Prioritize requests with unusual query parameters, shell metacharacters (|, &, ;, >, $, `), or malformed HTTP structure.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox OS Command Execution via HTTP Handler
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability' leading to 'unauthorized commands' — the execution phase occurs after HTTP injection succeeds.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation where parent is FortiSandbox service/web handler (fortisandbox, java processes on sandbox ports), especially if parent has no corresponding user session. Look for shell interpreter spawns (cmd.exe, /bin/sh, /bin/bash) with suspicious arguments.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Public-Facing Asset Inventory Mismatch
suggestion.rationale: Threat article emphasizes this is a public-facing service being actively exploited ('T1190 implies active exploitation against exposed assets'). Asset-exposure hunt is the table-stakes detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference FortiSandbox instances found in network scans / passive DNS against internal asset inventory. Any FortiSandbox with public-routable IP should trigger incident. Run CVE-2026-25089 scanner across all detected FortiSandbox deployments by 2026-07-19 (federal due date).

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Anomalous HTTP Parameter Encoding
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'specifically crafted HTTP requests' without detailing payload structure — this suggests obfuscation or unusual encoding in legitimate-looking HTTP flows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to FortiSandbox endpoints containing double-encoding, Unicode escapes, or HTTP Parameter Pollution (HPP) anomalies. Look for POST/GET requests where parameter values exceed normal length or contain null bytes.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox CVE-2026-25089 Exploit Payload Signature Detection
suggestion.rationale: CVE ID is the minimum correlatable IOC; even without public exploit code, known-exploited status means payload signatures will emerge rapidly.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor threat intelligence feeds (Exploit-DB, Shodan, WAF vendor advisories) for CVE-2026-25089 exploit signatures. Once signatures published, add to WAF/IDS. Alert on any FortiSandbox HTTP traffic matching known POC patterns.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Unauthenticated Command Injection HTTP Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests'—core attack delivery mechanism. No HTTP-level detection hunt generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to exposed FortiSandbox instances (default ports 443, 8443) for command injection metacharacters (pipes, semicolons, backticks, $(), command substitution) in URL parameters, POST bodies, or headers. Correlate request source IPs against known exploit patterns.

suggestion.title: OS Command Execution from FortiSandbox Daemon Processes
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability 'allows execution of unauthorized commands' implies OS-level command spawning downstream of HTTP injection. Article describes execution capability but no process-level hunt provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected child processes spawned from FortiSandbox service accounts (fortisandbox, fsapi, etc.), particularly shell invocations (bash, sh, cmd.exe) or command interpretation utilities (awk, perl, python). Correlate with recent HTTP access logs to same host.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-25089 Asset Inventory and Patch Compliance
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry with federal patch due 2026-07-19; asset discovery is baseline for any actively-exploited vulnerability. Article references template but pipeline emitted zero hunts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results for Fortinet FortiSandbox, FortiSandbox Cloud, and FortiSandbox PaaS instances across all network scopes. Prioritize internet-facing / cloud-hosted assets. Validate patch status against Fortinet advisory; flag any showing unpatched status post federal due date.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Payload Signatures in FortiSandbox API Logs
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'specifically crafted HTTP requests'—implies structured payloads. Unauthenticated endpoint abuse requires API log monitoring, but no endpoint hunt created.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiSandbox API endpoint logs for HTTP requests lacking valid authentication tokens, session cookies, or API keys. Alert on requests containing shell metacharacters, environment variable references, or known RCE payload signatures. Baseline legitimate administrative traffic.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-25089 Exploitation Indicators in Web Server Logs
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation leaves traces: HTTP 200 responses to injection attempts, error pages, unusual response sizes. Article states active exploitation but no behavioral detection pattern offered.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt FortiSandbox web server logs for unusual HTTP response patterns following injection attempts: successful commands (HTTP 200 with output), error messages revealing command execution (bash: syntax error, command not found), or responses with shell output artifacts. Look for repeated attempts from same source IP within short timeframe.

suggestion.title: PowerShell Active Directory User/Group Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'PowerShell Script to Map Active Directory.' Core attack step—no detection generated. Adversary running Get-ADUser, Get-ADGroup, Get-ADComputer, or net group commands to discover target assets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PowerShell child processes or command-line execution of Get-AD* cmdlets or net.exe with group/user enumeration parameters. Establish baseline for legitimate admin activity. Flag execution from non-admin logons, service accounts, or bulk query patterns within <5min (high AD object count returned).

suggestion.title: Obfuscated/AI-Generated PowerShell Script Execution
suggestion.rationale: Title flags 'suspected AI-generated' script—novel evasion vector. Pipeline missed emerging pattern: synthetic malware intended to bypass signature and behavioral detection via statistical anomalies in code generation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PowerShell ScriptBlock execution with anomalous indicators: Base64/Gzip encoded payloads, high-entropy variable names, unusual comment density, function imports from non-standard modules, or process command-line showing runtime string concatenation/substitution building AD discovery commands.

suggestion.title: LDAP Query Spike for Organizational Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Phrase 'map Active Directory' implies comprehensive object enumeration (users, groups, computers). Network-layer detection missing for bulk LDAP search traffic characteristic of reconnaissance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect elevated LDAP query volume from non-admin source IPs or sessions within short window. Flag queries with broad DN scope (wildcard filters), high result counts, or sequential queries targeting multiple object classes. Correlate source IP against baseline organizational user logon locations.

suggestion.title: Post-Discovery Privilege Escalation or Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: Active Directory mapping is reconnaissance for follow-on exploitation. Gap between discovery detection and attack continuation—pipeline missed correlation logic linking enumeration to subsequent credential access or lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate PowerShell AD enumeration events (Get-ADUser, net group queries) with subsequent suspicious activity within 30min: credential harvesting attempts, scheduled task creation, SMB connections to newly enumerated hosts, or logon events to discovered service accounts.

suggestion.title: Remote System Discovery via PowerShell Network Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Mapping AD often includes network topology discovery (T1018). Article does not exclude network reconnaissance; pipeline failed to generate detection for ping sweeps, port scans, or connectivity tests accompanying AD enumeration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PowerShell Test-NetConnection, Test-Path \\hostname\c$, ping.exe, or network diagnostic cmdlets executed after or concurrent with AD enumeration. Flag patterns suggesting host availability checking against discovered AD computer objects.

suggestion.title: Service Account or Domain Admin Targeting Post-Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: AD mapping enables targeting of high-value accounts. Pipeline missed detection for privilege escalation indicators following discovery of privileged AD objects (Domain Admins, Enterprise Admins, service accounts).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After PowerShell AD enumeration, detect subsequent attempted logons to discovered Domain Admin or service accounts, Kerberoasting attempts (TGS requests for discovered service accounts), or credential spraying from same source IP/session.

suggestion.title: Exposed FortiSandbox Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests,' implying internet-exposed FortiSandbox instances. Pipeline should generate asset discovery to identify and enumerate externally-routable appliances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify FortiSandbox instances via HTTP fingerprinting (version headers, management UI paths). Flag externally-routable appliances lacking network segmentation or WAF/IDS protection.

suggestion.title: HTTP Command Injection Payloads to FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies exploitation via 'specifically crafted HTTP requests.' Pipeline should detect OS command-injection metacharacters (;, |, `, $(), &&, ||) in HTTP parameters targeting FortiSandbox endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to FortiSandbox containing shell metacharacters in query strings, POST bodies, or headers. Prioritize unauthenticated requests from untrusted sources.

suggestion.title: Child Process Spawning from FortiSandbox Service
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'execute unauthorized commands'—indicating OS-level RCE. Pipeline should detect unexpected shells or utilities spawned from FortiSandbox parent process context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiSandbox service parent processes spawning cmd.exe, bash, or diagnostic utilities (curl, wget, nc) without operational context. Alert on outbound network activity or file modifications post-execution.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-25089 Patch Compliance Audit

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference Nessus/Qualys/Rapid7 for CVE-2026-25089 matches against patch schedules. Alert on any unpatched instance past 2026-07-19 federal deadline.

suggestion.title: Post-RCE Lateral Movement from FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: Article does not rule out attacker pivot post-exploitation. Pipeline should detect credential theft, network recon, or lateral movement originating from compromised FortiSandbox context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for discovery commands (whoami, systeminfo, net user) or credential-access (SAM reads, LSASS access) from FortiSandbox process trees. Detect SMB/RDP lateral connections initiated from appliance.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Asset Inventory & Patch Compliance
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'Fortinet FortiSandbox, FortiSandbox Cloud, FortiSandbox PaaS' with federal patch due 2026-07-19. Asset exposure hunting is the canonical first step for any KEV entry. Standard template applies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all FortiSandbox instances (on-prem, cloud, PaaS) via network scanning, asset inventory, and cloud API queries. Match against CVE-2026-25089 in scanner data. Flag instances where reported patch level contradicts vulnerability scan results or last update date is older than patch release.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated HTTP Command Injection Exploitation

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests to FortiSandbox endpoints (443, 8080) for payloads containing command injection signatures: backticks, $(), semicolons, pipe operators, or URL-encoded shell metacharacters in query parameters or POST bodies. Unauthenticated requests (missing/invalid auth headers) from external IPs are high-signal. Spike detection on malformed requests is secondary.

suggestion.title: Anomalous OS Command Execution from FortiSandbox Process

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected child processes spawned by FortiSandbox system processes (typically root, fortisandbox user, or system service account). Baseline normal FortiSandbox process trees. Flag any bash, sh, cmd.exe, powershell, or interpreter invocations outside known maintenance windows. Cross-correlate with external HTTP requests in same timeframe.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-25089 Vulnerability Confirmation
suggestion.rationale: Explicit CVE identifier in CISA KEV entry must be matched against all FortiSandbox instances. Article: 'CVE-2026-25089'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Run Nessus/Qualys/Rapid7 or equivalent against all FortiSandbox assets targeting CVE-2026-25089. Alert on any positive match. Create incident for each confirmed vulnerable instance with remediation deadline 2026-07-19. Correlate scanner findings with patch management system to identify patch installation failures.

suggestion.title: External API/Endpoint Access Without Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'unauthenticated attacker' as threat actor. Cloud and PaaS deployments are externally facing and more likely to be directly probed. Requires API-level logging.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiSandbox Cloud and PaaS API access logs for requests with missing, invalid, or expired authentication tokens. Alert on spike in HTTP 401/403 responses from external IPs. Ratio of auth failures to successes or requests from never-before-seen geolocations are secondary indicators of scanning/reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: Exploit Public-Facing Application - WordPress Core RCE
