suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to WordPress core endpoints with suspicious parameter combinations, unusual user-agent strings, or payloads indicative of code injection. Look for requests to unpatched WordPress versions from unauthenticated sources. Correlate with subsequent execution indicators.

suggestion.title: Command Execution via PHP - Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Unauthenticated RCE in WordPress implies arbitrary code execution, typically PHP on Linux hosts. Pipeline must detect post-exploit activity: process spawning, reverse shells, or command-line invocations from web worker processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous child processes spawned by web server daemons (apache, nginx, php-fpm) with suspicious command lines (nc, bash, curl, wget, or interpreted languages). Flag executions of scripting interpreters from /var/www or equivalent web root directories.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Persistence - PHP File Writes
suggestion.rationale: RCE often results in web shell implantation for persistence. Article does not detail post-exploitation behavior, but critical RCEs typically include persistence indicators: anomalous file writes to web-accessible directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation of .php, .phtml, or .php5 files in WordPress directories (wp-content, wp-admin, themes, plugins) outside of known deploy/update windows. Correlate timing with prior HTTP exploit attempts.

suggestion.title: Database Access from Web Process
suggestion.rationale: WordPress RCE enables database exfiltration or manipulation. Attackers typically execute MySQL/MariaDB queries for data theft or backdoor account insertion. Pipeline should alert on abnormal query patterns from web processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect direct TCP connections from web daemons to database ports (3306) with suspicious query patterns: CREATE USER, GRANT, SELECT INTO, or LOAD_FILE operations. Flag multi-megabyte data transfers from database to web process in short windows.

suggestion.title: Outbound C2 from Compromised WordPress
suggestion.rationale: Post-RCE, attacker typically establishes command-and-control. Unauthenticated RCE often leads to botnet enrollment or reverse shell establishment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound HTTPS/HTTP connections from web server processes to non-canonical destinations (non-CDN, non-WordPress.com, non-trusted update servers). Flag connections to known C2 IP ranges or domains with suspicious TLS certificates.

suggestion.title: Patch Status Assessment - WordPress Core Versions
suggestion.rationale: Title includes 'wp2shell' context suggesting specific version or component. Detection must include inventory of unpatched WordPress installations to enable rapid response. Pipeline failed to extract version indicators or patch-level requirements.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query WordPress installations for core version in HTTP headers, readme.html, or js/css versioning. Cross-reference against CVE database for wp2shell to identify vulnerable instances. Alert when unpatched versions are exposed to internet.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Installation — Vite Ecosystem
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'seven malicious Vite npm packages' but zero packages extracted. Detection must identify compromised package installations with malicious post-install scripts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install targeting Vite-related packages. Alert on packages with obfuscated postinstall hooks, excessive hidden dependencies, or registration within 30 days. Cross-reference against npm audit advisory feeds and supply-chain threat databases.

suggestion.title: Blockchain C2 Network Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'Blockchain C2' but zero command-and-control detection generated. Must identify blockchain-based covert channels (RPC endpoints, blockchain explorers, wallet services).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS/HTTP queries to blockchain infrastructure: etherscan.io, infura.io, alchemy.com, blockchain.com, or direct Ethereum/Bitcoin RPC endpoints. Detect repeated wallet address lookups from same process. Flag cryptocurrency service domains accessed from development/build contexts.

suggestion.title: Child Process Execution from npm/Node During Package Install
suggestion.rationale: Malicious packages execute code at install-time via postinstall hooks, but pipeline missed execution-layer detection. Article implies RAT installed via build-time scripts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for node.js spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or bash during npm install/build phases. Detect obfuscated or base64-encoded script payloads. Alert on file writes to non-project directories and unexpected network connections initiated from build processes.

suggestion.title: RAT Persistence Mechanism Installation by Build Process
suggestion.rationale: Article states packages 'deliver a RAT' but zero persistence detection generated. Expected: registry modifications, Startup folder writes, or scheduled task creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Run key modifications, AppData persistence, Startup folder writes, scheduled task creation, or service installation triggered by npm/node processes. Alert on any persistence tactic established outside legitimate project build.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated npm Package Script Analysis
suggestion.rationale: Malicious postinstall hooks employ obfuscation (base64, Unicode escapes, eval); article indicates sophisticated attack, yet pipeline missed script-level analysis of package.json payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Extract npm package.json postinstall/preinstall scripts. Decode base64 and escaped strings. Alert on eval(), exec(), or Function() constructors. Compare against malicious package signatures and deobfuscation heuristics.

suggestion.title: Blockchain Wallet Interaction and Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: RAT targeting development/crypto users likely exfiltrates to blockchain wallets or DeFi protocols; zero exfiltration detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected blockchain wallet creation, fund transfers, or smart-contract interactions from development machines. Monitor for cryptographic operations in JavaScript (webcrypto, signing APIs). Alert on transfer of credentials or secrets to blockchain addresses.

suggestion.title: Kubernetes Token Harvesting or Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states NadMesh 'hunts...Kubernetes tokens.' Detection must cover reads of kubeconfig files, ServiceAccount token access, and in-cluster credential enumeration by bot processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process reads of ~/.kube/config, /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token, or environment variable KUBECONFIG access by suspicious/bot processes. Flag Kubernetes API calls (GET /api/v1/namespaces/{}/secrets) from non-standard principals or external IPs.

suggestion.title: Cloud Credential Material Discovery and Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'hunts exposed AI services for cloud keys'—direct credential theft objective. Detection scope: AWS access keys, GCP credentials, Azure keys in environment, config files, container registries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect subprocess reads/cat of .aws/credentials, .kube/config, .gcp directories. Flag process execution of aws ec2 describe, gcloud auth list, az account show by non-admin/bot user context. Monitor env variable reads for AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS, KUBECONFIG.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance of Exposed AI Service Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article: NadMesh 'hunts exposed AI services'—implies active service discovery and probing phase preceding credential theft. Detection must cover port scanning, endpoint enumeration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid sequential connection attempts to common AI service API ports (8000–8888, 5000, typical model-serving ranges). Flag scanning patterns targeting OpenAI, Anthropic, HuggingFace, or local LLM endpoints. Alert on HTTP/HTTPS probing of /.well-known/, /v1/models, /api/status paths.

suggestion.title: NadMesh Botnet Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article names malware family 'NadMesh.' Pipeline must emit detection for binary execution, module loading, and C2 beaconing tied to this specific threat.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag process creation matching NadMesh signatures (file hashes, command lines, parent-child chains if signatures are available). Monitor for network connections from known NadMesh C2 domains or IPs. Alert on DLL injection, process hollowing, or memory-write patterns indicative of botnet execution.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Compromised Kubernetes Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Stolen K8s tokens enable cluster-wide lateral movement. Detection must cover suspicious pod/service account creation, privilege escalation, and cross-namespace token usage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on new service accounts with cluster-admin or elevated RBAC bindings post-compromise. Detect pods deployed in unusual namespaces using stolen service account tokens. Flag API calls to create/modify ClusterRoles, ClusterRoleBindings, or Secrets from unexpected principals.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Stolen Cloud API Keys
suggestion.rationale: Harvested cloud keys enable persistent infrastructure access. Detection must cover unauthorized IAM/access-key activity, cross-account role assumption, and long-term credential establishment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor API calls (CreateAccessKey, CreateUser, AssumeRole) using compromised credentials. Flag unusual principal/IP combinations using stolen keys for resource enumeration or instance/database access. Alert on federated identity setup or cross-account role assumption by non-service principals.

suggestion.title: Execution of processes signed with DigiCert certificates matching breach indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article describes GoldenEyeDog theft of DigiCert code-signing certificates for malware distribution; should detect process execution signed with DigiCert certs issued during/after breach or matching leaked thumbprints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ProcessSignatureStatus and Signer fields for processes with DigiCert Authenticode signatures. Flag execution of binaries with certificate thumbprints known to be compromised in breach, or DigiCert-signed software from publishers not historically signed by DigiCert. Cross-validate against software asset inventory.

suggestion.title: Code-signed malware delivery from GoldenEyeDog infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes weaponization: stolen DigiCert certs used to sign malware for distribution. Requires detection of signed executables from known GoldenEyeDog C2 or drop sites.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag downloaded/executed files bearing Authenticode signature with DigiCert and source IP/domain in threat-intel feeds for GoldenEyeDog C2 or known malware distribution servers. Signature presence should NOT suppress alert when source is malicious; code-signing trust must be revoked for compromised certificates.

suggestion.title: Abnormal certificate issuer transitions in process execution lineage
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain compromise indicates software signed by one CA (vendor) may now bear different signer (DigiCert leak). Detection should catch CA substitution in signing chains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline signing certificate issuer per software package. Alert when process execution shows issuer mismatch (e.g., vendor software previously signed by vendor CA now signed by DigiCert). Especially high-confidence if new issuer is DigiCert but vendor is not in known DigiCert-signed software list.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance targeting software vendor build/signing infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Compromise of DigiCert implies prior reconnaissance within partner environments or build infrastructure. Should detect enumeration/scanning of certificate stores, code repositories, or signing systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file-system enumeration (dir, ls, find) or registry queries (Get-ChildItem on CERT stores) targeting directories containing certificates, code artifacts, or signing materials on systems in supplier/vendor networks. Correlate with network reconnaissance (DNS to vendor domains, port scans to build-system IP ranges).

suggestion.title: Lateral movement to code-signing or certificate management infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Attacker must reach certificate vaults or signing systems to exfiltrate DigiCert certs. Should detect RDP/SSH/SMB to code-signing systems or unusual process execution on signing servers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag inbound RDP/SSH/SMB connections to systems in signing/certificate infrastructure from external or unusual internal hosts. Alert on process execution (certutil.exe, powershell.exe, openssl) on signing infrastructure with command-line indicating certificate export, import, or listing.

suggestion.title: Certificate revocation list (CRL) or OCSP bypass/suppression
suggestion.rationale: GoldenEyeDog must ensure stolen certificates evade revocation checks. Detection should catch suppression of CRL/OCSP validation or cache poisoning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for registry modifications disabling certificate revocation checks (e.g., SetReg CertCheckMode, DisableCRLChecks). Alert on WinHTTP or Schannel configuration changes that suppress OCSP/CRL validation. Correlate with execution of unsigned or suspiciously-signed binaries.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-25089 Exploitation — Crafted HTTP Request Detection

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Process Execution — Unexpected Child Spawning

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Unauthenticated API Access

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: HTTP requests to FortiSandbox management/API endpoints (port 8080, 8443, 4000 typical) missing Authorization or Session-ID headers. Alert if request count exceeds baseline per-source IP, or if source is external/untrusted.

suggestion.title: Detect Command Injection Payloads to FortiSandbox HTTP Endpoints

Focus on post-install lifecycle events where node_modules scripts execute with parent=npm or parent=node.exe spawning unexpected binaries.

suggestion.title: Blockchain-Based C2 Communication Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title establishes 'Blockchain C2' as delivery mechanism—this is the malware's command channel. Pipeline failed to create detections for blockchain-routed traffic or contract queries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for RAT processes performing DNS lookups to blockchain nodes (Ethereum, Solana, or privacy-focused chains) or establishing connections to known blockchain RPC endpoints. Flag processes initiating HTTPS to blockchain explorers or smart-contract interaction patterns.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Version Downgrades
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks often pivot on typosquatting or dependency confusion. Article references 'malicious Vite npm packages'—detection must cover installation anomalies and package metadata mismatches.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm install commands for packages with names similar to popular Vite libraries, unusual version strings (pre-release tags from untrusted registries), or package.json modifications that enforce specific malicious versions via lock files.

suggestion.title: RAT Capability Indicators from Node.js Process
suggestion.rationale: Delivery mechanism is a RAT (Remote Access Trojan), yet no detections for RAT file operations, persistence, or exfiltration behaviors. Article confirms post-install unpacking into node_modules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor node.exe or child processes for direct registry access, suspicious file writes to Startup folders, execution from temporary directories, or network connections to C2 addresses shortly after package installation. Cross-correlate process lineage: npm → node → suspicious binary.

suggestion.title: npm Registry Compromise Indicators
suggestion.rationale: The attack vector is poisoned packages on npm registry—need telemetry on registry API calls, package metadata queries, or npm CLI using non-standard registries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm CLI invocations with registry overrides (--registry flags pointing to attacker infrastructure), package.json referencing unusual Vite variants, or .npmrc files with non-standard authentication tokens. Flag installations from private/test registries during normal deployment workflows.

suggestion.title: Extraction and Decoding of Node Module Payloads
suggestion.rationale: Post-install scripts typically extract compressed or encoded payloads. Pipeline missed detection of file carving, archive extraction, or PE/shellcode decoding from within node_modules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on archive utilities (7z, tar, unzip) or PowerShell decompression operators executed in node_modules context. Flag processes decoding Base64/hex-encoded blobs or executing inline PowerShell launched from package.json install phases.

suggestion.title: Kubernetes ServiceAccount Token Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article states botnet 'hunts for Kubernetes tokens.' Pipeline produced zero detection coverage for this attack vector, despite being explicit in the title.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on reads of /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token or ~/.kube/config followed by network exfiltration. Flag non-kubelet processes accessing token paths. Correlate file read + outbound connection in <5min window to non-cluster IPs.

suggestion.title: Cloud API Key Harvesting from Exposed AI Service Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'hunts exposed AI services for cloud keys.' No use case for reconnaissance of misconfigured LLM endpoints (HuggingFace, SageMaker, etc.) leaking credentials.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Exfiltrated Cloud Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article implies credential theft enables cloud account takeover. Zero detection for simultaneous credential use across geographies, unauthorized API calls with stolen keys, or anomalous principal behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on API authentication using discovered credentials from IPs outside organization baseline or different regions within minutes of first use elsewhere. Flag calls to sensitive APIs (CreateAccessKey, DeleteUser, ModifyDBInstance) from compromised principals.

suggestion.title: Container Registry and Cloud Storage Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Kubernetes tokens grant access to container registries and storage. Article context implies targeting of ECR/ACR/GCR. No detection for registry scanning or secret enumeration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on ListRepositories, DescribeRepositories, ListImages from unrecognized principals or access denied patterns indicating brute-force repository enumeration. Flag GetAuthorizationToken calls followed by registry pulls.

suggestion.title: Secrets Manager Enumeration and Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Compromised cloud keys provide access to Secrets Manager, Azure Key Vault, etc. No detection for mass secret retrieval or enumeration of secrets outside principal's historical scope.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Trigger on ListSecrets + GetSecretValue patterns from a principal showing no prior secret access. Alert on bulk secret retrieval (>5 secrets in <10min) or access to secrets tagged as 'prod' or 'critical'.

suggestion.title: NadMesh C2 Communication Detection
suggestion.rationale: Botnet must beacon to C2. Article title references 'NadMesh' but pipeline extracted zero indicators. No domains, IPs, or behavioral signatures for botnet C2 defined.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound HTTPS to NadMesh-attributed C2 domains (pending IOC feed). Detect DGA-like query patterns or certificates with known malicious issuers. Alert on port combinations or tunnel signatures consistent with botnet beaconing.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Code-Signing Certificate Usage
suggestion.rationale: Article focuses on theft of code-signing certificates; detection of unexpected certificate issuers or serial numbers in process signature chains directly addresses the post-breach attack surface: 'Code-Signing Certificate Theft.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor executables signed with certificates not matching expected issuers (e.g., certificates bearing DigiCert serial ranges outside legitimate software publishers). Alert on code-signed binaries executed from temporary directories, user-writable paths, or unusual network shares. Cross-correlate with certificate revocation lists for known-stolen serials.

suggestion.title: DigiCert Certificate Store Access by Non-Administrative Processes
suggestion.rationale: Compromise of DigiCert infrastructure implies theft from certificate stores; detecting unauthorized access to local or remote certificate repositories establishes credential-access phase: 'breach and code-signing certificate theft.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes outside the Windows Certificate Store management tools (certmgr.exe, mmc.exe with cert snapin) or key management services reading %APPDATA%\Microsoft\SystemCertificates or HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\SystemCertificates. Flag native access to certificate private key material (PFX/P12 files) from non-service accounts.

suggestion.title: Compromise of DigiCert/Entrust Account Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'DigiCert Breach'; detection of compromised account activity or lateral movement from DigiCert infrastructure establishes initial-access and credential-access phases without requiring IOC specificity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual sign-in patterns to DigiCert and certificate authority portals: impossible travel, off-hours access, new device fingerprints, API key usage from unfamiliar IPs. Alert on bulk certificate issuance, revocation of legitimate certificates, or modification of certificate policies within a short timeframe.

suggestion.title: Malware Signed with Stolen Code-Signing Certificates

suggestion.title: Certificate-Based Persistence via Code-Signing
suggestion.rationale: Stolen certificates enable long-term malware deployment and updates without re-compromise; detection of persistence mechanisms leveraging code-signing certificates maps to the post-theft exploitation phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for signed executables in persistence locations (HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run, startup folders, scheduled tasks). Alert on signed binaries with weak or invalid timestamps, self-signed certificates, or certificates issued to shell companies / regional variations of known publishers.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Unauthenticated API Access

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Internet-Facing Asset Inventory

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Sandbox Escape / Lateral Movement Indicators

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect FortiSandbox processes accessing system files, registry, or network resources outside their expected sandbox scope (e.g., %WINDIR%, /etc, network share access). Flag privilege escalation attempts or file writes to sensitive directories.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Lateral Movement from Compromised Appliance

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Audit Log Tampering or Deletion

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated access to FortiSandbox management/API endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated attacker' can trigger vulnerability. This eliminates auth bypass as a precondition and means detection must focus on exposed, unprotected endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiSandbox administrative or API endpoints for requests that succeed without valid authentication tokens/sessions. Flag 200/201 responses to unauthenticated POST/GET calls to known vulnerable paths (e.g., /api/v*, /admin, /sandbox/*).

suggestion.title: Log injection / command substitution in FortiSandbox request parameters
suggestion.rationale: OS command injection typically exploits unsafe parameter handling in system calls. Article describes 'specifically crafted HTTP requests'; pipeline should generate pattern detection for injection vectors like shell metacharacters, environment variable expansion, or command chaining.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: IPS/WAF rules should trigger on HTTP requests containing shell metacharacters (|, ;, &, &&, ||, $()), backticks, or substitution patterns in parameters destined for FortiSandbox endpoints. Cross-reference with CVE-2026-25089 public PoCs for exact payload signatures once available.

suggestion.title: Patch compliance: FortiSandbox version audit vs. federal due date
suggestion.rationale: Article mandates federal patch due date of 2026-07-19. Pipeline did not generate compliance/inventory use case to verify all instances patched by deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and asset management system for all FortiSandbox instances. Verify installed version is ≥patched version published by Fortinet. Generate compliance report scoped to federal agencies and flag instances unpatched past 2026-07-19 deadline.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable FortiSandbox Instance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states the vulnerability affects 'Fortinet FortiSandbox, FortiSandbox Cloud, and FortiSandbox PaaS' and is actively exploited (CISA KEV status). Scanner-based hunt for unpatched instances before Federal due date (2026-07-19) is baseline defensibility.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query network asset inventory and vulnerability scanner for Fortinet FortiSandbox installations with version prior to patch release or where CVE-2026-25089 remains unresolved. High-confidence signals from authenticated scans (Nessus, Tenable, Qualys) or public-facing service fingerprints (TLS cert, HTTP headers matching FortiSandbox signature).

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated HTTP Exploitation to FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack requires no authentication and uses 'specifically crafted HTTP requests.' Network detection of exploit attempts should monitor HTTP traffic to known FortiSandbox endpoints with suspicious request patterns (URL fragments known to probe injection points, abnormal payload sizes, repeated failed requests).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag inbound HTTP requests to FortiSandbox management interfaces or API endpoints (typically port 443, 8080, 8443) from untrusted networks containing indicators of command-injection payloads (shell metacharacters, common injection strings like `|`, backticks, `$()`, or URL-encoded variants) in GET/POST parameters or request body.

suggestion.title: OS Command Execution Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'execute unauthorized commands' via the injection. Execution-phase detection should monitor for unexpected processes spawned by FortiSandbox service (typically running as root or SYSTEM-equivalent), especially shell interpreters (sh, bash, cmd.exe, powershell) or reverse-shell signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On FortiSandbox hosts, detect child processes spawned by the FortiSandbox service daemon with suspicious command lines (shell invocations, curl/wget downloads, encoded payloads, network connections). Baseline the legitimate process tree and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Patch Compliance by Due Date
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies Federal patch due date as 2026-07-19. Compliance detection should verify all FortiSandbox instances have been patched or mitigated by that date, triggering escalations for outstanding instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and patch-management data on 2026-07-20 to identify any remaining FortiSandbox instances with CVE-2026-25089 unresolved. Trigger incident for any findings post-deadline per Federal compliance requirements.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-25089 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies CVE-2026-25089 as the exploited vulnerability affecting FortiSandbox, FortiSandbox Cloud, FortiSandbox PaaS. Any vulnerability scanner output flagging this CVE is critical inventory for patch prioritization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan results reporting CVE-2026-25089 with critical/high severity. Correlate with asset inventory to identify exposed instances. High-priority remediation ticket. Federal due date 2026-07-19 is hard stop for compliance.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated HTTP Access to FortiSandbox Admin/API Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests.' Detection must flag HTTP access to FortiSandbox endpoints lacking proper authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: HTTP requests to FortiSandbox endpoints (/api/*, /admin, /sandbox) returning HTTP 200 without Authorization header or valid session token. Baseline expected admin IP ranges; alert on geographic/network anomalies.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload Detection in HTTP to FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'OS command injection vulnerability...via specifically crafted HTTP requests.' Payloads will contain shell metacharacters (pipes, semicolons, backticks, command substitution) in HTTP parameters or body.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: HTTP request to FortiSandbox endpoint with shell metacharacters in query string or POST body (e.g., |, &, ;, $(cmd), `cmd`). Particularly high-fidelity if source is external/untrusted network and endpoint normally protected by authentication.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Process Execution Spawned by FortiSandbox Service Account
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation executes 'unauthorized commands.' Must detect unusual child processes spawned by FortiSandbox daemon/service, especially shells and network utilities.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Process creation where parent = FortiSandbox service/daemon, child = cmd.exe, powershell, bash, sh, nc, curl, wget. Establish baseline of known-good admin scripts first to minimize false positives.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Internet Exposure via Port Scan / Network Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article implies actively exploited instances are 'exposed.' Detection must identify FortiSandbox ports (typically 8443, 8080, 443) responding from public/untrusted network segments.

suggestion.title: Successful Admin Console Access Without Valid Session / Credential Bypass

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: HTTP 200 or valid session cookie issued to /admin or /api endpoint from source with no prior authentication record. Failed login attempts immediately followed by successful session access. Geoip/ASNET anomalies.

Flag unpatched systems against patch inventory. Alert on public IP responses to FortiSandbox service probes or banner grabs. Cross-reference against federal patch deadline 2026-07-19 for compliance prioritization.

Flag requests with parameter injection, command-like strings, encoding tricks (URL double-encoding, Unicode), or deviation from baseline API calls. Correlate with CVE-2026-25089 POC patterns. Alert on HTTP 200/302 responses following suspicious requests.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-25089 Vulnerability Scan Match

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Fortinet FortiSandbox (identify by banner, endpoint patterns, or asset inventory) lacking authentication tokens, containing shell metacharacters (;, |, $(), backticks, \n), or matching common OS command injection payloads. Flag any request succeeding (200/201 response).

suggestion.title: Process Execution from FortiSandbox Service
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies OS command injection allows attacker to 'execute unauthorized commands'—direct execution flow means detect child processes spawned by FortiSandbox daemon/service process.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, sh spawned as children of Fortinet FortiSandbox process (or running under its service account). Flag especially if parent is HTTP listener or if executed with system/admin/root context unexpectedly.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-25089 Asset and Patch Inventory Correlation
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV requires federal patch by 2026-07-19; article lists three product variants: 'FortiSandbox, FortiSandbox Cloud, and FortiSandbox PaaS.' Standard practice (referenced in body: asset-exposure template) is flag unpatched instances against scanner data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scan results for CVE-2026-25089 against all Fortinet products. Correlate with asset inventory (product name, version). Alert on any unpatched Fortinet FortiSandbox, Cloud, or PaaS instance visible to untrusted networks or past federal due date.

suggestion.title: HTTP POST/PUT to FortiSandbox with Encoded Payloads
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'specifically crafted HTTP requests' are exploitation vector. Payload encoding (URL, base64, hex, Unicode) is common in command injection evasion—detection must examine decoded content.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect HTTP requests to FortiSandbox endpoints for payloads with high entropy, repeated encoding patterns, or decoded content matching shell commands (grep -P for common payloads: `whoami`, `id`, `cat /etc/passwd`, `powershell -enc`, etc.).

suggestion.title: Fortinet Service Availability Spike Detection
suggestion.rationale: Successful command injection against service may cause denial of service or restart loops. Detection via service restart frequency or response-time degradation on FortiSandbox instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Fortinet FortiSandbox service restart events or uptime drops within 1 hour of HTTP exploitation attempts. Correlate service logs with suspicious HTTP patterns in proxy/WAF logs from same source IP.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Internet Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability exploited by 'unauthenticated attacker' against unspecified deployment model. KEV status means assets ARE being targeted in the wild. Article body does not specify network restriction requirements, implying public-facing assumption.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for FortiSandbox instances in external-facing IP ranges or DNS records. Cross-reference against known internal subnets. Flag instances accessible on HTTP/HTTPS ports to external networks without VPN/WAF interception.

suggestion.title: Anomalous HTTP Requests to FortiSandbox Management Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'specifically crafted HTTP requests' as attack vector. No legitimate traffic patterns provided, but deviation from baseline admin/update traffic should be suspicious.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of legitimate HTTP traffic to FortiSandbox (e.g., admin panel, API calls, update checks). Alert on requests from non-whitelisted IP ranges, non-standard User-Agents, or payloads containing shell metacharacters (|, &, $, `, ;) in HTTP request bodies or URL parameters.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Process Execution from FortiSandbox Service Context
suggestion.rationale: Article defines vulnerability as 'OS command injection'—attacker gains arbitrary command execution. Detection must focus on abnormal child processes spawned from FortiSandbox daemon/service accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child processes spawned by FortiSandbox service account (e.g., fortios, sandbox_daemon). Alert on shell interpreters (/bin/bash, /bin/sh, cmd.exe, powershell.exe) or suspicious binaries (curl, wget, nc, python) with parent = FortiSandbox process and no recent code deployments/maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Vulnerable Version Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is actively exploited (KEV catalog) but does not specify patched versions. Any FortiSandbox instance running pre-patch versions is confirmed exploitable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for FortiSandbox appliances with version < [patch version, assumed TBD per 2026-07-19 deadline]. Cross-reference FQDN/IP against last-phone-home logs and recent security update checklists. Prioritize instances in DMZ or customer-facing networks.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Attempt via Web Application Firewall Evasion
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'specifically crafted HTTP requests'—suggests attacker may be testing multiple payloads or evasion techniques. WAF/IPS should detect malformed or suspicious requests targeting FortiSandbox endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to FortiSandbox URIs (e.g., /admin, /api, /upload, /sandbox/api) containing known command injection payloads (e.g., backticks, $(cmd), |, &&) or null bytes. Flag requests with Content-Length mismatch, double-encoding, or Unicode normalization evasion attempts.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Lateral Movement Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Once command execution achieved, attacker will pivot to adjacent systems. Detection should monitor for network reconnaissance and credential harvesting originating from compromised FortiSandbox instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After detecting T1059 execution on FortiSandbox, watch for unusual network outbound connections (especially port 22, 3389, 445), DNS queries for internal hosts, or credential dumping utilities (secretsdump, mimikatz) launched from FortiSandbox context.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiSandbox: Asset Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes CISA KEV means 'currently exploited in the wild.' Standard asset-exposure hunt is mandatory. Template reference in article: '../_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure'. No UC generated despite explicit guidance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and asset-management systems for Fortinet FortiSandbox, FortiSandbox Cloud, or FortiSandbox PaaS instances. Filter for version/patch status. Flag any instance with CVE-2026-25089 unpatched or unknown patch level.

suggestion.title: HTTP Command Injection Attempts to FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies exploitation via 'specially crafted HTTP requests' with OS command injection payload. No UC created to detect HTTP-layer exploitation patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to known FortiSandbox management/API endpoints for command injection patterns (shell metacharacters, backticks, $(…), semicolons, pipes, redirects). Prioritize unauthenticated requests. Flag baseline deviations.

suggestion.title: OS Command Execution on FortiSandbox Hosts
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability 'allows execution of unauthorized commands' — article describes successful exploitation outcome. No post-exploitation command-execution hunt generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiSandbox host process/command logs for unexpected shell invocations, suspicious process parents, or commands spawned by web application contexts. Look for execution tied to HTTP injection timeframes.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to FortiSandbox Admin/API Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated attacker' — implies no auth required. Pipeline should flag reconnaissance/access attempts to sensitive endpoints without credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to FortiSandbox management UI or API endpoints (e.g. /admin, /api, /rest) from external IPs returning 200/success or 400-level errors without corresponding authentication records. Cluster by source IP and time.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiSandbox Patch Compliance Check
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes federal patch due 2026-07-19 and warns 'patch lag is the silent killer.' No UC generated to track patch remediation status against deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference vulnerability scanner output, patching system records, and asset inventory to identify FortiSandbox instances with CVE-2026-25089 unpatched as of the federal deadline (2026-07-19). Flag for immediate escalation.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Asset Inventory: FortiSandbox Products
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies three product variants: 'Fortinet FortiSandbox, FortiSandbox Cloud, and FortiSandbox PaaS.' Pipeline must correlate presence of these products in asset inventory with CVE-2026-25089 to prioritize highest-risk endpoints for patching given federal due date.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify hosts running Fortinet FortiSandbox (any variant) that either lack patches for CVE-2026-25089 or have unknown patch status. Cross-reference vulnerability scanner logs, asset management systems, and version strings in HTTP headers or process listings to flag exposed instances.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated HTTP Requests to FortiSandbox Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers are 'unauthenticated' and exploit 'specifically crafted HTTP requests.' Pipeline must detect anomalous HTTP patterns (unusual paths, parameter injection, auth bypass indicators) targeting known FortiSandbox endpoints without valid session tokens.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP GET/POST requests to FortiSandbox endpoints (e.g., /pentaho, /api, /admin paths typical of Fortinet products) from external IPs lacking valid authentication headers or session cookies. Correlate request patterns with known CVE-2026-25089 PoC indicators (command injection syntax in query/form parameters).

suggestion.title: OS Command Execution from FortiSandbox Process Context
suggestion.rationale: Core attack mechanism: 'OS command injection vulnerability that allows an unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands.' Pipeline must detect spawned processes (shell, cmd.exe, /bin/bash) or command-line activity initiated by FortiSandbox service accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child processes spawned by FortiSandbox parent processes (typically running as dedicated service account: FortiSandbox, fortinet, sandbox_svc). Flag execution of shells, scripting interpreters, or command utilities with parent=FortiSandbox and no known scheduled tasks/legitimate operations recorded.

suggestion.title: HTTP POST/GET with Command Injection Payloads Targeting FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'specifically crafted HTTP requests' but omits PoC. Detectable via behavioral pattern: injected shell metacharacters (|, &, ;, ``, $()) or OS command keywords (whoami, id, cat, base64, nc, curl) embedded in HTTP parameters sent to FortiSandbox-controlled endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search HTTP request logs for patterns: payloads to FortiSandbox endpoints containing shell metacharacters or command keywords. Common injection points: query parameters, POST body fields, HTTP headers. Filter for requests from external/untrusted networks or anomalous source IPs.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation: Lateral Movement from Compromised FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: Once RCE is achieved via CVE-2026-25089, attacker has OS-level code execution on FortiSandbox host (often network-critical appliance). Watch for subsequent reconnaissance, data exfil, or pivot attempts from this host.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After identifying successful command injection exploitation (see above), escalate to network-layer monitoring: watch for unexpected outbound connections from FortiSandbox host to internal network ranges, DNS lookups for internal hostnames, or file transfer attempts (SMB, rsync, HTTPS exfil) initiated from the compromised appliance.

suggestion.title: Failed Authentication Attempts Preceding FortiSandbox Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'unauthenticated' access, but reconnaissance may involve auth probes or default credential attempts. Detection opportunity: cluster failed login attempts to FortiSandbox admin/API endpoints before successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate failed login/authentication errors on FortiSandbox endpoints (HTTP 401, 403, invalid password logs) with subsequent successful exploitation indicators (HTTP 200 + command execution). Timing: look for attempts within 1-24 hours before RCE confirmed.

suggestion.title: Notarized Binary with Suspicious Child Process Spawning
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'uses notarized dropper to pass Gatekeeper checks.' Notarization is a trust signal; detection must distinguish legitimate notarized software from droppers spawning shell interpreters, curl, or data-exfiltration tools post-execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on notarized binaries (valid code signature + notarization record) that spawn unexpected child processes—particularly /bin/sh, /bin/bash, curl, launchctl, or security-policy manipulation tools. Baseline legitimate notarized apps and flag behavioral deviation.

suggestion.title: CrashStealer Dropper Chain: Staging to Payload Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies CrashStealer as a dropper-based malware family. Detect multi-stage execution: dropper creates temp files, extracts/decodes payload, executes core stealer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify process trees where a notarized/signed application writes executable files to /tmp, /var/tmp, or ~/Library/Caches, then executes them or forks shell children with atypical arguments. Focus on parent=dropper, child=shell or script interpreter.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Crash Report and System Log Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Malware name 'CrashStealer' indicates data theft focused on crash reports (~/Library/Logs/CrashReporter, /Library/Logs). These contain sensitive stack traces, env vars, and credential artifacts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag processes accessing crash-report directories outside standard system/security software. Monitor for bulk file reads, archive operations (tar/zip), or upload via curl/python to exfil crash data.

suggestion.title: LaunchAgent Persistence Registration from Malware Process Lineage
suggestion.rationale: Stealer malware persists via LaunchAgent/LaunchDaemon. CrashStealer's two-stage pattern (dropper→payload) suggests post-exploit persistence is likely, though not explicit in truncated article.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor .plist creation/modification in ~/Library/LaunchAgents linked to dropper parent process. Alert on LaunchAgent Label pointing to /tmp, /var/tmp, or recently-executed unsigned binaries.

suggestion.title: Gatekeeper Trust Control Subversion: Revoked or Malicious Certificates
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'notarized dropper to pass Gatekeeper checks.' Detection must identify certificates associated with CrashStealer family, revoked notarization records, or certificate use outside known developer scope.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Build IOC list of certificates / notarization records linked to CrashStealer. Cross-reference code-signing data on process execution; alert if signature is valid but issuer/developer ID enters threat intel blacklist or shows behavioral anomalies (unusual runtime, network, or FS access).

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Crash Data via Outbound Network Tunnel
suggestion.rationale: CrashStealer implies exfiltration. Detect unusual outbound network traffic from malware process lineage to non-Apple infrastructure, especially bulk transfers or encrypted tunnels.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from CrashStealer process and descendants to domains outside apple.com or known CDNs. Alert on high-volume data transfers, persistent tunnels, or connections to known C2 infrastructure.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-25089 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs 'match against your vulnerability scanner' for CVE-2026-25089. No UC provided for positive scan results or asset-exposure correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when vulnerability scanner reports CVE-2026-25089 on any Fortinet FortiSandbox, FortiSandbox Cloud, or PaaS instance. Correlate with inventory to track unpatched systems. Escalate any findings after Federal due date 2026-07-19.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiSandbox Unauthenticated HTTP Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests'. No detection for anomalous HTTP patterns to FortiSandbox endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP traffic to Fortinet FortiSandbox appliances for command-injection indicators: shell metacharacters, backticks, $(), cmd substitution syntax, unusual parameter values in unauthenticated endpoints. Baseline normal API usage and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Post-Injection OS Command Execution on FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: Article outcome is 'execute unauthorized commands'. Detect abnormal process creation or shell invocation on compromised FortiSandbox hosts post-injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected process spawning or shell commands (bash, sh, cmd.exe) on FortiSandbox appliances, especially with elevated privileges. Flag commands inconsistent with sandbox operations (outbound connections, file exfiltration, enumeration).

suggestion.title: Internet-Facing FortiSandbox Appliance Exposure
suggestion.rationale: T1190 'Exploit Public-Facing Application' combined with CISA KEV active exploitation. Verify no FortiSandbox instances are exposed to internet or untrusted networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory and external scanning (Shodan, Censys) to identify all Fortinet FortiSandbox hosts and confirm none are internet-routable. Alert if any management or API port (443, 8443, custom) is publicly accessible.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-25089 Patch Deployment Compliance
suggestion.rationale: Article sets Federal patch deadline 2026-07-19. No UC for tracking patch application or post-deadline compliance verification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track patch status for CVE-2026-25089 across all FortiSandbox assets. Alert if any system remains unpatched after Federal due date. Correlate patch install logs with baseline inventory to ensure 100% coverage; escalate gaps to compliance team.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox CVE-2026-25089 Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states this is CISA KEV (actively exploited in the wild) and references 'canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in [...#asset-exposure]'. The template should be instantiated with CVE-2026-25089 per the article's own instruction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner data and asset inventory for FortiSandbox, FortiSandbox Cloud, and FortiSandbox PaaS instances. Alert on any system flagged as vulnerable to CVE-2026-25089, and cross-check patch levels against 2026-07-19 federal due date.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated HTTP Command Injection to FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests'—this is a direct attack surface requiring behavioral detection of injection payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST/GET requests to FortiSandbox endpoints (ports commonly 8080, 8443, or 80/443 for cloud/PaaS variants) for command injection patterns in parameters: shell metacharacters, command substitution syntax ($(...),$(...), backticks), path traversal sequences, or OS-specific payloads.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Command Execution on FortiSandbox Host
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'allows unauthorized commands' to execute. Successful exploitation will manifest as unexpected processes spawned from network-sourced context rather than administrative console.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous child process spawning under FortiSandbox service contexts (fortisandbox, sandbox daemon) where parent process indicates network origin (HTTP service, reverse shell handles) or unexpected command-line arguments containing encoded commands or shell invocations.

suggestion.title: Patch Compliance Post-Remediation for CVE-2026-25089
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' and federal agencies required to remediate by 2026-07-19; compliance hunt ensures patched state was verified post-deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After 2026-07-19, verify all FortiSandbox assets report patched version covering CVE-2026-25089. Flag any instance still vulnerable post-due-date as either unpatched (remediation failure) or misconfigured (false-negative scanner result).

suggestion.title: WordPress Core Exploitation via wp2shell Vulnerability
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'WordPress Core Flaw Lets Unauthenticated Attackers Run Code'—explicit exploitation of public-facing application. Pipeline extracted zero initial-access indicators or exploitation vectors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to WordPress installations for wp2shell exploitation payloads. Detect POST/GET requests to vulnerable WordPress endpoints from unauthenticated sources that receive 200 responses. Alert on requests containing code-execution indicators, shell metacharacters, or command-injection patterns in parameters targeting WordPress core.

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution via Malicious WordPress Request
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attackers can 'Run Code' without authentication—explicit execution capability. No execution-phase detection use cases were generated despite clear RCE impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate web server access logs showing wp2shell exploitation attempts with process creation events showing shell interpreters or command executors spawned under web server process identity (www-data, apache, nginx, IIS AppPool). Detect anomalous parent-child relationships and unexpected outbound connections from web server processes.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Child Process Spawning from Web Server
suggestion.rationale: RCE inherently implies code execution and process spawning under web server context. Pipeline missed execution-layer behavioral detection signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child processes created by web server processes (apache2, httpd, nginx, w3wp.exe) spawning command interpreters (/bin/sh, /bin/bash, cmd.exe, powershell.exe). Flag unexpected file modifications, network connections, or privilege escalation attempts from web server worker processes post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: SQL Injection in Unauthenticated WordPress Request
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'SQL injection' as the attack vector. Pipeline emitted zero use cases despite this being the primary initial-access technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to WordPress installations (wp-admin, wp-login.php, public endpoints) for SQL metacharacters and UNION/SELECT payloads in unauthenticated requests. Baseline normal WordPress query patterns and alert on syntax-like strings (OR 1=1, SLEEP(), stacked queries) in GET/POST parameters from external IPs.

suggestion.title: Command Execution Following Web Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes unauthenticated RCE outcome. Pipeline missed detection linking HTTP exploitation attempts to child process spawning from web-server user context (php-fpm, apache2 child).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate suspicious inbound HTTP requests (SQL injection patterns, encoded payloads) against ProcessCreated events spawned from WordPress application processes within 5 seconds. Alert on cmd.exe, /bin/bash, or /bin/sh children from php or httpd parent PIDs in web-server context.

suggestion.title: WordPress Core File Modification or Web Shell Creation
suggestion.rationale: Post-RCE, attackers typically persist via web shells or core-file modification. Article implies exploitation leads to sustained access but pipeline generated no persistence-detection use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation or modification in wp-content/, wp-admin/, or wp-includes/ directories with .php, .phtml, .php5 extensions outside standard deployment windows. Correlate with process execution or HTTP requests to newly created files; flag inline PHP scripts in legitimate WordPress directories.

suggestion.title: Database Schema Enumeration via Web Application
suggestion.rationale: SQL-injection RCE often involves attacker probing database structure (information_schema, sys tables). Pipeline provided no detection for reconnaissance queries through database layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor database query logs for SELECT from information_schema, mysql.user, or sys tables originating from WordPress application user. Alert on HIGH query volume or schema enumeration patterns (SHOW TABLES, SELECT table_name FROM...) following exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Outbound Network Activity from Compromised WordPress Process
suggestion.rationale: RCE typically enables C2 callback or data exfiltration. Article describes unauthenticated code execution but pipeline missed detection for post-exploitation network anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound TCP/UDP connections initiated by php-fpm or apache2 child processes to non-standard ports (not 80/443) or to IPs not in WordPress CDN/plugin-update whitelists. Correlate with timeframe following SQL injection exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Installation with Blockchain-Based C2 Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes seven malicious Vite npm packages delivering a RAT via blockchain C2. Should detect anomalous npm installs followed by outbound blockchain/cryptocurrency network traffic. Phrase: 'Seven Malicious Vite npm Packages Use Blockchain C2 to Deliver a RAT'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install operations (especially for 'vite' package variants) followed within seconds by process spawning network connections to known blockchain nodes or cryptocurrency mining pools. Correlate npm package names against threat intel; flag post-install JavaScript/Node.js child processes making cryptographic or P2P network calls.

suggestion.title: npm Post-Install Script Execution Spawning RAT-Like Process Behavior
suggestion.rationale: Malicious npm packages exploit post-install hooks to execute attacker-controlled code and drop a RAT. Should detect obfuscated or suspicious script execution during package installation. Phrase: 'malicious Vite npm Packages... to Deliver a RAT'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm install lifecycle events (postinstall, preinstall scripts) that spawn child processes with network connectivity, file write activity to $HOME/.cache or %TEMP%, or execution of base64-decoded payloads. Track process parent-child chain from npm → node → unexpected binaries.

suggestion.title: Outbound Blockchain/Cryptocurrency Network Traffic from Development Toolchain
suggestion.rationale: RAT uses blockchain for C2, an unusual vector. Development machines running npm should not initiate cryptocurrency wallet queries, blockchain node syncs, or DNS lookups for mining pools. Phrase: 'Blockchain C2'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound TCP/UDP to known cryptocurrency blockchain RPC endpoints (Ethereum, Bitcoin, Monero RPC ports), blockchain explorers, or mining pool domains originating from npm, Node.js, or build-tool processes on non-infrastructure hosts.

suggestion.title: Vite Package Registry Typosquatting or Version Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies malicious 'Vite npm Packages' — suggests either typosquatting the legitimate Vite package or compromised versions. Should flag registry lookups for variants or unusual version jumps. Phrase: 'Seven Malicious Vite npm Packages'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm registry manifest downloads for package name similarities to 'vite' (vite-cli, vite2, vite-builder, etc.) and flag installations of versions with anomalous timestamps, unusual publisher accounts, or mismatched dependency graphs.

suggestion.title: RAT Beacon Initialization from npm Package Context
suggestion.rationale: RAT must initialize after installation. Look for process spawning, registry/file modifications, persistence mechanisms, or credential harvesting originating from npm post-install. Phrase: 'to Deliver a RAT'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm/Node.js child processes that modify startup locations (registry Run keys, cron jobs, ~/.bashrc), write to ~/.ssh, enumerate system users, or spawn WMI/PowerShell commands for reconnaissance post-installation.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated JavaScript in npm Package Payloads
suggestion.rationale: RAT delivery via npm requires evasion of static analysis. Should detect base64, ROT13, or minified JavaScript hiding malicious logic in package tarballs or install scripts. Phrase: implicit in 'malicious packages deliver RAT'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan npm package postinstall scripts for high entropy strings, base64-encoded buffers, eval() calls, dynamic require statements, or character-code constructs that decode to network I/O or system commands.

suggestion.title: Cloud Service Reconnaissance by NadMesh Botnet
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes botnet actively hunts 'exposed AI services'—indicating discovery/scanning phase targeting misconfigured cloud deployments. Title phrase: 'hunts exposed AI services.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for scanning patterns against common AI service ports/endpoints (LLM APIs, model registries) from single or coordinated sources, combined with HTTP 200/403 responses indicative of service enumeration. Correlate with known NadMesh C2 if available.

suggestion.title: Kubernetes Token/API Key Exfiltration Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states botnet targets 'Kubernetes tokens' and 'cloud keys.' Title phrase: 'for Cloud Keys and Kubernetes Tokens.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious reads of service account tokens from /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/ or environment variable exfiltration. Flag API calls retrieving token secrets, especially from non-service accounts or unusual IPs.

suggestion.title: Cloud Provider Credential Store Querying
suggestion.rationale: Attack objective includes harvesting 'cloud keys'—requires querying credential stores, secrets managers, or environment configs. Implied by article scope.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect enumeration of IAM roles, secrets manager API calls, or environment variable reads within containers. Flag patterns querying multiple credential types in short time windows or from unexpected principals.

suggestion.title: Botnet Command & Control Communication (NadMesh)
suggestion.rationale: Botnet infrastructure must establish C2 to coordinate scanning and exfiltration. No C2 domains, IPs, or ports identified despite critical severity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for NadMesh beacon traffic signatures (if known), unusual DNS queries to C2 infrastructure, or outbound connections from compromised containers to non-standard ports. Correlate with botnet IOC feeds.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Stolen Kubernetes Tokens
suggestion.rationale: Post-compromise, stolen K8s tokens enable lateral movement across cluster workloads and namespaces. Article implies token use for impact/persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag API calls authenticated by service account tokens from unusual sources (external IPs, different clusters). Alert on cross-namespace API access or RBAC policy modifications using stolen credentials.

suggestion.title: Code-Signing Certificate Abuse – DigiCert Breach Window
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly links GoldenEyeDog to 'code-signing certificate theft' from DigiCert; pipeline extracted zero detection use cases despite this being the *core attack vector*. Need to detect binaries signed with certificates issued during compromise window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for binary execution where code-signing certificate issuer=DigiCert AND certificate serial within known-compromised batch AND signature timestamp during breach window (if known). Cross-reference against legitimate software publishers to isolate malware abuse of stolen certs.

suggestion.title: Suspicious DigiCert Certificate Issuance Activity
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain breach implies unauthorized certificate requests or issuance from DigiCert infrastructure. Pipeline missed detecting anomalous cert-generation activity that typically precedes theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag certificate issuance requests from non-standard DigiCert user accounts, batch issuance of code-signing certs for unregistered organizations, or cert generation outside normal business hours if audit data available.

suggestion.title: GoldenEyeDog C2 or Infrastructure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article attributes breach to threat actor by name; pipeline extracted zero actor intelligence or associated infrastructure IOCs (domains, IPs, ASNs). Command-and-control communication should be detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Once actor infrastructure is published in threat reports, correlate network logs for beacon activity to known GoldenEyeDog C2 domains/IPs. Prioritize TLS cert validation anomalies (cert pinning failures, unexpected CAs).

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Lateral Movement in Certificate Authority Environment
suggestion.rationale: DigiCert breach implies attacker moved laterally within their environment to reach cert-signing infrastructure. Pipeline missed defense-evasion and lateral-movement techniques typical of supply-chain attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for logons to DigiCert-infrastructure systems from unusual geographies, off-hours, or using delegated credentials. Look for lateral movement using pass-the-ticket or overpass-the-hash post-compromise.

suggestion.title: Stolen Certificate Authority Credential Usage
suggestion.rationale: Code-signing cert theft typically follows compromise of CA credentials or HSM access. Pipeline extracted zero credential-access or persistence techniques.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for multi-failed authentication attempts against DigiCert HSM/key-storage, successful logins followed by certificate export operations, or cert-signing requests using non-standard APIs or tooling.

suggestion.title: Malware Distribution Using Stolen Code-Signing Certs
suggestion.rationale: The ultimate impact of cert theft is distribution of malware under a trusted signature. Pipeline failed to suggest detection of unsigned→signed binary transitions or unusual publisher trust chains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag processes executing binaries signed with DigiCert certs where: signer organization ≠ expected software vendor, binary hash is unknown/malicious, or cert-signing timestamp is recent (post-compromise).

suggestion.title: HTTP Request to FortiSandbox with Command Injection Syntax
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'specifically crafted HTTP requests' enable exploitation. Pipeline generated zero UCs despite this being the primary attack vector — unauthenticated POST/GET payloads containing shell metacharacters, command substitution ($()), or backticks targeting FortiSandbox endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify unauthenticated HTTP requests to FortiSandbox API/web interface endpoints containing shell metacharacters or command substitution patterns (e.g., $(id), `whoami`, ; bash). Baseline benign administrative requests and flag outliers with payloads matching command injection regex patterns.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access Attempts to FortiSandbox Web Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker is 'unauthenticated' — this is the access path. Pipeline missed detection of missing or invalid authentication tokens reaching FortiSandbox endpoints, which is the prerequisite for exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiSandbox access logs for HTTP 200/successful responses to restricted endpoints without valid session tokens or authentication headers. Track successful unauthenticated access followed by POST requests within same session.

suggestion.title: OS Command Execution from FortiSandbox Process
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability allows 'execute unauthorized commands' — post-exploitation detection. Pipeline generated no execution-phase UCs despite the outcome being documented command execution via OS interpreter.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child processes spawned by FortiSandbox service accounts (typically root or 'forti*' user) with suspicious command-line arguments (e.g., bash -c, /bin/sh, curl, wget). Establish baseline of legitimate administrative maintenance tasks and flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox API Exploitation Attempt Sequence
suggestion.rationale: Article describes HTTP request-based exploitation pathway not captured by pipeline's empty kill chain. Should detect the specific exploitation sequence: discovery → unauthenticated request → injection payload → response anomaly.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track three-phase HTTP exploitation signature: (1) unauthenticated request to /api or /admin endpoints → (2) HTTP 200-299 response → (3) subsequent POST/GET with shell metacharacters within 10 seconds. Flag as exploitation attempt.

suggestion.title: Scanner/Vulnerability Assessment Traffic to FortiSandbox Ports
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends 'asset-exposure hunt' but pipeline generated no UCs for identifying exposed FortiSandbox instances. Should detect port-scanning and vulnerability-scanner probing of typical ports (8080, 8443, 8899).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify inbound connections to FortiSandbox ports (8080/tcp, 8443/tcp, 8899/tcp) from external networks or untrusted internal ranges. Correlate with vulnerability scanner signatures and HTTP User-Agent strings known to probe FortiSandbox.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Proof-of-Concept Command Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Exploits typically validate execution with diagnostic commands. Article's 'unauthorized commands' implies PoC validation traffic. Pipeline should hunt for stereotypical post-exploitation indicators (whoami, id, uname -a output in logs).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search FortiSandbox process logs and syslog for execution of benign diagnostic commands in suspicious context: /usr/bin/id, /usr/bin/whoami, /bin/uname called as children of FortiSandbox service. These are PoC indicators following successful exploitation.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Unauthenticated HTTP Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests.' This is the initial-access vector (T1190) and requires asset-exposure baseline + anomaly detection on exposed FortiSandbox web interfaces.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to FortiSandbox API/management endpoints from unauthenticated sessions or external sources. Alert on 401→200 state transitions, requests containing shell metacharacters in URL/POST parameters, or abnormal request rates to known-vulnerable paths. Cross-reference against asset inventory to flag externally-routable instances due for patching by 2026-07-19.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Command Injection Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'OS command injection vulnerability' and 'execute unauthorized commands'—requires payload detection in HTTP streams for command-execution signatures (T1059.001).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Screen HTTP requests targeting FortiSandbox for shell metacharacters, command keywords (bash, cmd, powershell), and injection syntax (`|`, `;`, `$()`, backticks, `&&`, `||`) in parameters. Correlate successful 200 responses with unexpected child-process creation events from FortiSandbox service context.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Spawning from FortiSandbox Service
suggestion.rationale: Command injection requires process execution; article implies FortiSandbox service executes arbitrary OS commands. Need process-tree monitoring for abnormal children of the FortiSandbox daemon (T1059).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned by FortiSandbox service/agent with unusual executables (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, nc, curl), command-line obfuscation, or no corresponding HTTP API log entry. Baseline normal FortiSandbox child processes (scanner tools, sandbox analysis) to reduce false positives.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox CVE-2026-25089 Patch Compliance Check
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry with federal due-date 2026-07-19 implies urgent inventory/patch-status validation. Standard vulnerability-scanner + asset-inventory query for unpatched instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for CVE-2026-25089 detections; cross-reference against CMDB patch status to identify unpatched or missing-scan instances. Prioritize externally-accessible assets. Alert on any new scanner detections within 48 hours of article publication (7-day lookback).

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Lateral Movement via Command Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article does not restrict scope to single-system impact; successful command injection on network-connected FortiSandbox may enable attacker-orchestrated lateral movement or reconnaissance (T1016, T1018).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-exploitation baseline: after successful command-injection detection, monitor spawned processes for network reconnaissance (ipconfig, route, arp, nslookup, ping) or lateral-movement tools (psexec, winrm, ssh). Flag process network-connection events originating from FortiSandbox service context to unusual internal IPs.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-25089 Asset Exposure & Vulnerability Scan Detection

Flag any unpatched assets discovered before federal deadline 2026-07-19. Cross-reference with external exposure checks (Shodan, SSL certificate enumeration) to identify internet-facing instances.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiSandbox Suspicious HTTP Request Pattern Detection

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP traffic to known FortiSandbox instances for requests containing command injection syntax (backticks, $(), |, &&, ;, etc.) in URI query strings or POST parameters. Correlate unauthenticated source IPs with exploitation attempts. Alert on status 200/500 responses following suspicious payloads.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Command Execution on FortiSandbox Appliances

Look for system commands, shell invocation, or privilege escalation attempts originating from the web layer.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiSandbox Product Inventory & Patch Compliance Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes three product variants (FortiSandbox, Cloud, PaaS) all vulnerable. Inventory and patch status tracking is foundational risk management; federal due-date deadline drives urgency.

Generate daily compliance report showing % of environment patched, days remaining before federal deadline, and critical/high-risk unpatched instances requiring immediate action.

suggestion.title: External Exposure Detection for FortiSandbox Web Services
suggestion.rationale: Article's MITRE T1190 (Exploit Public-Facing Application) and 'unauthenticated attacker' context indicate internet exposure is a prerequisite for exploitation. Network-level exposure detection is critical.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect listening HTTP/HTTPS services on Fortinet FortiSandbox appliances via continuous network scanning. Identify which instances are externally reachable (public IP, no WAF, no geographic restrictions). Flag any internet-exposed FortiSandbox that should be internal-only, and correlate with recent inbound connection attempts from external sources.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiSandbox Security Patch Deployment Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: Federal compliance deadline is 2026-07-19 for CVE-2026-25089. Deployment monitoring ensures patches are applied before deadline and validates remediation.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox public-facing exposure detection

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Fortinet FortiSandbox instances (FortiSandbox, FortiSandbox Cloud, FortiSandbox PaaS product names) exposed to untrusted networks via port scanning, banner grabbing, or vulnerability scanning. Cross-reference with patch status for CVE-2026-25089.

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious child processes spawned by Fortinet FortiSandbox processes (typically running as root/SYSTEM). Expected children: none or only internal Fortinet binaries. Flag: cmd.exe, powershell.exe, /bin/bash, /bin/sh as children of FortiSandbox parent.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated API access to FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'unauthenticated attacker' can reach endpoints. Baseline should detect missing or bypassed authentication to FortiSandbox administrative API endpoints.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox vulnerability scanner detection
