suggestion.title: WordPress wp2shell RCE Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly labels 'wp2shell' as the vulnerability enabling 'Unauthenticated Attackers Run Code'; pipeline extracted no IOCs or use cases. Title establishes public-facing application exploit scenario.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to WordPress endpoints (wp-admin/admin-ajax.php, wp-includes, wp-content) from unauthenticated sources containing encoded payloads, null bytes, or PHP function calls (eval, system, exec, assert). Flag requests missing valid session cookies or Authorization headers.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Creation in WordPress Writable Directories
suggestion.rationale: Naming 'wp2shell' indicates web-shell persistence mechanism; pipeline did not map to T1505.003 or file-creation detections. RCE results in shell artifacts in wp-content/uploads or plugins.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on .php, .phtml, or .phar file creation in wp-content/uploads, wp-content/plugins, or wp-content/themes by w3wp.exe or apache2 processes outside maintenance windows. Correlate with preceding suspicious HTTP POST/PUT requests to WordPress files.

suggestion.title: Command Execution Spawned from Web-Server Process
suggestion.rationale: RCE flaw enables arbitrary code execution; pipeline missed command-execution detection despite article establishing execution capability. Need to detect process spawning chain from web server.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or /bin/bash spawned as child of w3wp.exe, apache2, or nginx with parent chain rooted in svchost or apache parent processes. Monitor for base64-encoded command parameters, encoded payloads, or reverse-shell indicators in process arguments.

suggestion.title: Suspicious POST Requests to WordPress Admin AJAX Handler
suggestion.rationale: Unauthenticated RCE typically targets wp-admin/admin-ajax.php; pipeline did not surface this endpoint-specific exploitation pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag POST requests to wp-admin/admin-ajax.php action parameter with non-existent or malicious values (action=wp_shell, action=rce, action=exec) from public IPs. Alert on polyglot payloads (.jpg.php, .gif.php) or PHP serialization objects in request body.

suggestion.title: Rapid File Writes Followed by HTTP Requests in Web Root
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation chain: HTTP request → file drop → shell execution. Pipeline failed to generate behavioral detections correlating file I/O with network events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate file-creation events in web-root directories (wp-content, uploads) within 60 seconds of HTTP requests from the same source IP. Alert if file permissions are world-readable or executed immediately via subsequent HTTP request.

suggestion.title: Encoded Command Parameters in WordPress HTTP Requests
suggestion.rationale: Web-shell exploitation uses base64/hex encoding to obfuscate payloads; pipeline did not surface encoding-pattern or payload-signature detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP request parameters containing base64-encoded strings, hex-encoded sequences, or gzip-compressed payloads targeting WordPress endpoints. Decode and scan for shell metacharacters (|, &, ;, $()), function names (eval, exec, system, passthru), or reverse-shell signatures.

suggestion.title: SQL Injection via WordPress REST/Query Parameter
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly describes 'unauthenticated RCE via SQL injection'—the SQLi is the entry vector. Article states the exploit targets WordPress core and is unauthenticated, implying web-facing SQL injection in publicly accessible parameters.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor incoming HTTP requests to WordPress installation paths (/wp-admin, /wp-json, /?p=) for SQLi payloads in GET/POST parameters: UNION-based (keywords: UNION, SELECT, WHERE in encoded form %55, %53), time-delay sleep(X) or BENCHMARK(), error-based (MySQL/PostgreSQL error syntax), stacked queries (semicolon-delimited). Baseline legitimate queries first; alert on deviation.

suggestion.title: Shell Process Spawned from Web Server Following SQLi Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates RCE endpoint: SQL injection must execute system commands. Article 'wp2shell' naming suggests direct shell access post-exploit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected child process creation from web server processes (www-data, iis apppool, httpd, nginx). Alert on spawning of interpreters (bash, sh, cmd.exe, powershell.exe, python, perl) or utilities (curl, wget, nc) from web-server parent PIDs immediately following HTTP requests. Correlate timing: SQLi request → process creation within <5s.

suggestion.title: Database Error Leakage in HTTP Response (SQLi Indicator)
suggestion.rationale: SQL injection attempts, especially error-based, generate MySQL/PostgreSQL error messages that may leak in HTTP responses. Article describes a live exploit, so error-based SQLi variants are likely attempted first.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP responses containing database error strings: 'MySQL', 'PostgreSQL', 'ORA-', 'SQL Server', 'Syntax error', 'near line', 'SQL query' in response body or HTTP 500+ status codes paired with SQL keywords in request URL. Cross-reference with request parameters for SQLi signatures.

suggestion.title: Abnormal Database Query Execution from WordPress Instance
suggestion.rationale: SQLi reaching code execution means database is executing attacker-controlled queries. Article emphasizes WordPress core vulnerability, so queries are executed in DB context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor database logs for: UNION-based multi-row SELECTs from information_schema, repeated INTO OUTFILE / LOAD_FILE attempts, CREATE FUNCTION or ALTER FUNCTION commands, EXEC/xp_cmdshell (MSSQL), or SELECT...INTO queries writing to filesystem. Compare against baseline WordPress query patterns (wp_posts, wp_users, wp_options tables only).

suggestion.title: Outbound Network Connection from Web Server Post-SQLi
suggestion.rationale: RCE via SQLi typically results in reverse shell, data exfil, or C2 callback. Article's critical severity and RCE nature suggest post-exploit callback.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected outbound connections (non-standard ports, non-whitelisted destinations) originating from web-server process IP/PID within 30s of SQLi-pattern detection. Establish baseline for legitimate PHP external calls (CDN, mail SMTP); flag deviations to unusual IPs/ports, especially on high-volume data channels or rare protocols (raw socket, DNS tunneling).

suggestion.title: WordPress Administrative User Creation or Privilege Escalation Post-Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Unauthenticated RCE via SQLi to WordPress database allows direct wp_users table modification. Attacker likely persists via new admin account.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor wp_users table for unexpected INSERT/UPDATE rows where user_login is new, user_pass hash changed, or user_registered timestamp is recent but admin meta (wp_capabilities) grants admin role. Correlate with SQLi detection events. Flag if no admin user exists in audit logs prior to database change timestamp.

suggestion.title: Detect Malformed Short TLS ClientHello Packets
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states '11-Byte TLS Requests' as attack vector. Pipeline missed this obvious network-layer detection signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for TLS handshake packets significantly smaller than expected (≤11 bytes to ClientHello frame). Flag connections originating from external networks attempting to initiate TLS with malformed or incomplete handshake sequences, particularly to ports 443 and 8443.

suggestion.title: Detect OpenSSL Process Crash and Restart Cycles
suggestion.rationale: Article title states vulnerability 'could freeze server memory'—impact is service degradation. Pipeline missed process-level impact detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for repeated rapid restart cycles of OpenSSL/TLS services (e.g., nginx, Apache, custom TLS daemons). Alert on process exit codes indicating abnormal termination (segfault, out-of-memory) followed by immediate re-spawning within <60s window.

suggestion.title: Detect Abnormal Memory Consumption by TLS Processes
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'freeze server memory' as exploit outcome. No detection use case for memory exhaustion was generated despite explicit article focus.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor OpenSSL-linked processes (sslengine, openssl, TLS libraries) for memory allocation spikes >500MB sustained for <5s during TLS connection attempts. Correlate with network traffic anomalies (short malformed packets) to differentiate from legitimate large-file TLS transfers.

suggestion.title: Detect CVE-Related OpenSSL Version Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article references specific OpenSSL 'HollowByte' flaw but pipeline extracted no CVE ID or version ranges. Version enumeration from banners/responses is a fundamental threat intelligence requirement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline OpenSSL version from TLS ServerHello banners (TLS_GREASE, cipher suite patterns). Alert on external reconnaissance (nmap, sslscan) probing for versions matching known HollowByte-affected ranges; escalate if followed by malformed TLS packets.

suggestion.title: Detect Repeated TLS Handshake Failures to Same Target
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation pattern of sending 11-byte requests implies repeated connection attempts. Pipeline missed behavioral anomaly detection for brute-force-style TLS attack probes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag sequences of >50 incomplete/malformed TLS handshakes from same source to same target within 60s window. Prioritize if source is external and handshake failures escalate to process crash events on target.

suggestion.title: Malicious npm Package Installation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly references 'Seven Malicious Vite npm Packages'—supply-chain attack vector. Pipeline should detect npm install commands pulling from suspicious or typosquatted package names.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install, yarn add, pnpm add commands for package names matching known malicious Vite package variants. Alert on post-install script execution or unexpected child processes spawned during package installation. Correlate with package manager manifests (package.json, lock files) for unexpected dependencies.

suggestion.title: Blockchain API Communication from Development Hosts
suggestion.rationale: Article title references 'Blockchain C2'—unusual command-and-control mechanism. Pipeline should detect outbound calls to blockchain nodes, RPC endpoints, or crypto exchanges from development/build environments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP/HTTPS connections to known blockchain RPC endpoints (Ethereum, Polygon, Solana nodes), cryptocurrency exchange APIs, or blockchain explorers from non-standard processes (node.js, JavaScript engines). Flag DNS queries for blockchain service domains originating from npm postinstall scripts.

suggestion.title: JavaScript Post-Install Script RAT Execution
suggestion.rationale: Title references 'RAT delivery' via npm packages—npm packages execute post-install scripts. Pipeline should detect file write, process spawning, or network connectivity from JavaScript/node.js contexts during package installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child processes spawned from npm/yarn/pnpm with unusual command lines (PowerShell, cmd.exe, curl, wget). Detect file writes to temp or system directories from node.js processes. Alert on network connections from npm postinstall context to non-standard ports or blockchain infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Supply-Chain Package Metadata Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Article targets Vite build tool ecosystem with malicious packages—suggests name confusion or registry compromise. Detection should flag installations of packages with suspicious or typosquatted names relative to legitimate Vite ecosystem.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference installed package names against npm registry metadata. Flag packages with unusual author changes, recent owner transfers, or suspicious version jumps. Alert on package installations where version does not match requested range or when package pulled from non-standard registry mirrors.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated JavaScript C2 Beacon Detection
suggestion.rationale: RAT payload delivered via npm likely uses obfuscated JavaScript. Detection should identify encoded strings, suspicious Base64/hex decoding, or dynamic code evaluation patterns in node_modules execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect eval(), Function(), require() with dynamically constructed strings executed from node_modules contexts. Alert on decoding of Base64/hex strings followed by network connectivity. Monitor for suspicious Object prototype pollution or require path manipulation patterns.

suggestion.title: Blockchain Wallet Address Hardcoding in Dependencies
suggestion.rationale: Blockchain C2 likely requires hardcoded wallet/address references in RAT code. Pipeline should extract and monitor for known malicious blockchain addresses embedded in source code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan npm package source code and compiled artifacts for hardcoded Ethereum/crypto addresses, blockchain transaction hashes, or RPC endpoint URLs. Correlate extracted addresses against threat intelligence feeds for known C2 infrastructure. Alert if extracted addresses appear in on-chain transaction analysis.

suggestion.title: Kubernetes API Reconnaissance from Untrusted Sources
suggestion.rationale: Article states botnet 'hunts exposed AI services' and 'Kubernetes tokens'—implies probing Kubernetes API endpoints. Distinctive attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on connection attempts to Kubernetes API ports (6443, 10250, 10255, 9090) from external IPs, especially patterns consistent with rapid automated scanning. Track DNS queries for k8s infrastructure hostnames (*.cluster.local, kube-apiserver) from non-k8s-designated hosts.

suggestion.title: Cloud Service Credential Exfiltration via CLI Tools
suggestion.rationale: Core threat: 'hunts...for cloud keys and Kubernetes tokens.' Botnet must enumerate and exfiltrate credentials programmatically.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect cmdline patterns harvesting credentials: env variable dumps (env | grep -i aws|token), reads of ~/.aws/*, ~/.kube/config, or /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token. Alert on child process execution from unexpected services (web apps, containers) accessing credential stores.

suggestion.title: Exposed AI/ML Endpoint Brute-Force Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article phrase 'hunts exposed AI services' indicates automated scanning of cloud-hosted ML/AI endpoints for accessible endpoints lacking authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for rapid sequential HTTP requests to common ML API paths (/v1/models, /api/predict, /metrics, /admin) and high-volume non-200 responses (403/404) from single sources. Correlate with known botnet malware signatures or NadMesh C2 infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Service Account Token Read and Exfiltration from Containers
suggestion.rationale: Specific attack vector: Kubernetes tokens stored in predictable container mount point /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/. Article explicitly mentions this threat class.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process reads of /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token or /var/run/secrets/.../.dockercfg from non-system processes. Detect subsequent egress of token-sized data (base64-encoded ~500+ bytes) to external destinations outside cluster network.

suggestion.title: Multi-Cloud Credential Harvesting Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Botnet scanning for credentials across infrastructure implies attempting multiple cloud provider CLI tools and environment variable patterns sequentially from same source.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate rapid attempts to locate AWS (aws-vault, ~/.aws), GCP (gcloud config), and Azure (az login) credential materials from single host. Detect patterns of env-var querying or file-stat probing against credential directories across multiple cloud provider SDK paths.

suggestion.title: NadMesh Botnet C2 Communication and Credential Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: As botnet malware, NadMesh requires command channel to receive tasking and exfiltrate stolen keys/tokens. Article focuses on credential harvesting, implying attacker collection pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for DNS requests or TLS connections to known NadMesh C2 domains (from threat feeds). Detect credential-sized data payloads in HTTP POST bodies or DNS exfiltration tunneling. Monitor for process spawning with embedded credentials or encrypted outbound beacons containing harvested key material.

suggestion.title: Detect Process Execution of Binaries Signed by Stolen DigiCert Certificates
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states certificate theft linked to GoldenEyeDog. Execution of malware signed with these certificates is the primary post-breach weaponization vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process execution where binary's code signature issuer is DigiCert and signing certificate serial number or thumbprint matches known-compromised set. Correlate execution timestamp, process creator, and parent process against baseline. Prioritize execution outside vendor/developer infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Detect Issuance of Code-Signing Certificates via Compromised DigiCert Account
suggestion.rationale: Breach implies attacker access to issuance infrastructure. Monitor Certificate Transparency logs for new code-signing certificates issued post-breach with anomalous requestor patterns, geolocation, or bulk volume.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse CT logs for DigiCert-issued code-signing certificates with requestor IP geographically inconsistent with customer base, issuance outside business hours, or certificate names matching known malware families or attacker infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Detect Inbound Email Delivery of Code-Signed Malware
suggestion.rationale: Stolen certificates enable malware distribution disguised as legitimate signed software, bypassing reputation filters. Title explicitly links theft to GoldenEyeDog, indicating operational deployment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-correlate email attachment hashes and signing certificates against theft advisory. Flag binaries signed by DigiCert-issued certificates on compromise list regardless of sender reputation. Capture file metadata: name, hash, signer CN, thumbprint.

suggestion.title: Detect Lateral Movement via Network Delivery of Code-Signed Malware
suggestion.rationale: Post-breach, attackers deploy signed malware internally via SMB, WMI, or GPO, exploiting trust in code signatures to bypass endpoint controls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for binaries signed by compromised certificates created via network SMB writes, WMI file deposits, or group policy push. Flag unsigned deployments of binaries with matching code-signing certificate serial numbers in local logging.

suggestion.title: Detect Signed Malicious DLL Load via DLL Search Order Hijacking
suggestion.rationale: Attackers sign malicious DLLs with stolen certificates to evade UAC/AppLocker restrictions and hijack legitimate application loading paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on DLL image loads from unusual paths (temp, downloads, ProgramData) where DLL is signed with DigiCert-issued certificate on compromise list. Verify DLL load does not match application manifest or expected dependency.

suggestion.title: Detect Supply Chain Infection via Trojanized Software Update
suggestion.rationale: Stolen code-signing certificates enable repackaging of legitimate software with injected malware and re-signing, appearing legitimate during update check and distribution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor software update payloads (Windows Update, vendor updates) for executables signed by DigiCert certificates issued during compromise window. Cross-validate product version, signer metadata, and update timestamp against vendor release schedule. Yara scan update binaries for known malware signatures despite valid certificate chain.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiSandbox—Unauthenticated HTTP Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests' to unauthenticated FortiSandbox instances. Zero UCs generated despite this being the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiSandbox listening ports (typically 8080, 8443, 541) for unauthenticated HTTP/HTTPS requests with command-injection payloads (shell metacharacters: |, &, ;, `, $(). Correlate with HTTP 200/400 responses indicating processing of requests to /upload, /api, /analyze, or admin endpoints without authentication headers.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiSandbox—OS Command Execution Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability' allowing 'unauthorized commands' execution. Missing T1059.001 (Command Line Interface) detection for actual payload execution on FortiSandbox OS.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On FortiSandbox systems, detect unexpected child processes spawned from FortiSandbox service processes (fortisandbox, lighttpd, or service account runners). Look for sh/bash/cmd execution with stdin from network sockets, or process creation from HTTP service threads.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-25089—Asset Exposure Scan
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' using template, explicitly stating 'worth one quick check across your fleet — patch lag is the silent killer.' Pipeline generated zero asset-discovery detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner output for systems reporting FortiSandbox (any version) with CVE-2026-25089 not yet patched. Cross-reference with asset inventory to confirm externally-facing instances and validate patch application date against federal due date 2026-07-19.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiSandbox Unauthenticated HTTP Command Injection Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests'—requires detection of malicious HTTP payloads targeting exposed FortiSandbox ports
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP POST/GET requests to FortiSandbox standard ports (4000, 4001, 5000) from external/untrusted sources containing shell metacharacters (backtick, pipe, semicolon, $(), &&, ||) or known OS command separators. Prioritize requests with error response codes indicating injection rejection.

suggestion.title: Process Spawning from FortiSandbox Service Processes
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability'—FortiSandbox should never spawn child shells (cmd.exe, bash, sh); any such process spawning indicates exploitation of T1059.001
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned by Fortinet FortiSandbox services with names: cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, sh, python.exe, or perl.exe. Inspect command line for obfuscation or encoded payloads. Match against patches issued after 2026-07-19.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Service Abnormal HTTP Error Patterns in Logs
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation attempts precede successful RCE; article's federal urgency indicates defenders should hunt failed injection attempts before patch deadline
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search FortiSandbox service logs and HTTP access logs for error codes or stack traces in same timeframe as suspicious HTTP requests. Look for patterns indicating argument parsing failure, shell metacharacter rejection, or command execution errors.

suggestion.title: HTTP injection payload detection to FortiSandbox endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'via specifically crafted HTTP requests'—exploitation is HTTP-borne. Requires WAF or proxy logs for parameter inspection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to FortiSandbox with shell metacharacters, command substitution operators ($()), or OS-specific injection markers in query parameters or POST bodies. Correlate requests from external IPs to /api, /admin, or management endpoints.

suggestion.title: Command execution spawned from FortiSandbox process context
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability 'allows…execution of unauthorized commands'—successful exploitation results in process creation. Look for child processes launched from FortiSandbox service account.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect new process creation where parent is FortiSandbox daemon (e.g., fortisandbox, fssandboxd) and child is shell, cmd.exe, powershell, or bash. Cross-reference timing with HTTP access logs for correlation.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated HTTP access to FortiSandbox management interface
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'unauthenticated attacker'—exploitation does not require credentials. Hunt for external HTTP requests that bypass authentication checks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify HTTP 200/302 responses from FortiSandbox APIs or dashboards where source IP is external and no authentication cookies/tokens are present or valid. Spike in 401→200 sequence per source IP suggests auth bypass.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability scanner match: CVE-2026-25089 on assets
suggestion.rationale: Template instructs 'vulnerability scanner' check—capture assets running vulnerable FortiSandbox versions prior to federal due date 2026-07-19.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest FortiSandbox version reports from scanners and flag any instance matching vulnerable versions (versions before patched release). Cross-reference against network exposure tools to confirm external reachability.

suggestion.title: OS command stderr/stdout exfiltration from FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation, attacker will want output from injected commands. Monitor FortiSandbox logs and process output for unexpected command results.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag large stderr/stdout output written to unexpected file descriptors or network sockets from FortiSandbox processes. Look for base64 or hex-encoded output patterns suggesting data staging.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Public Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'unauthenticated attacker' accessing FortiSandbox via HTTP — presupposes internet-exposed instances. Pipeline missed initial-access reconnaissance phase entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify FortiSandbox instances (ports 8000, 8001, typical admin ports) reachable from untrusted networks. Search passive DNS, Shodan, certificate logs for FortiSandbox FQDN/IP exposure. Query firewall inbound rules permitting direct HTTP to FortiSandbox management.

suggestion.title: HTTP Command Injection Attempt — FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'specifically crafted HTTP requests' enable injection. Pipeline ignored the HTTP attack vector entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to FortiSandbox endpoints for command metacharacters (`;`, `|`, `&`, backticks, `$()`) in query parameters and POST bodies. Alert on injection payloads matching common OS command syntax (bash, cmd.exe, powershell). Signature-based detection of known FortiSandbox injection paths.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Process Spawning from FortiSandbox Service
suggestion.rationale: OS command injection necessarily spawns child processes from FortiSandbox process context. Article describes 'execute unauthorized commands' but pipeline produced no execution-phase detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes created by FortiSandbox service (java.exe, python.exe, cmd.exe, /bin/bash) with unusual command lines or file paths. Establish baseline of expected child processes; flag deviations. High alert if spawning from network-accessible FortiSandbox instance.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Error Logs — Command Injection Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Failed injection attempts and successful exploitation both leave diagnostic trails in application logs. Pipeline skipped vendor-specific log analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse FortiSandbox application logs for error codes related to invalid requests, shell escape sequences, or unexpected command execution. Correlate with timestamps of inbound HTTP requests. Alert on sequences suggesting injection testing (multiple payloads to same endpoint in short window).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-25089 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article itself recommends 'asset-exposure hunt' and standard scanner template. Pipeline failed to operationalize the template provided in the article body.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner database for all systems flagged as vulnerable to CVE-2026-25089 (Fortinet FortiSandbox OS Command Injection). Cross-reference with network exposure data (internet-facing IPs). Prioritize remediation by CVSS (critical) and federal patch due date (2026-07-19).

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Unauthenticated OS Command Injection via HTTP
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests.' No detection use case was generated despite this being the core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiSandbox listener ports (default 8080 or 443) for HTTP POST/GET requests containing command injection signatures (shell metacharacters: $(), backticks, ||, ;, pipes in query params or POST body). Baseline should show zero matches from untrusted IPs before incident date.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Unauthorized Child Process Spawning
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'execute unauthorized commands' — successful injection must spawn child processes. Pipeline failed to generate execution-layer detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child processes spawned by FortiSandbox daemons (fortisandbox, sandbox-agent, etc.) with unexpected parent-child relationships or command lines. Focus on cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, sh spawning from network service accounts or www-data equivalents.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Service Log Anomalies During Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability is in FortiSandbox OS — native logs should show parse errors or unexpected entries during injection attempts. No UC suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse FortiSandbox application logs for entries indicating failed or malformed request handling: HTTP 400/500 errors with unusual payloads, stack traces mentioning shell/system calls, or authentication bypass attempts. Correlate with process creation events within seconds.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-25089 Patch Compliance Audit
suggestion.rationale: Article mandates 'Federal patch due: 2026-07-19.' Pipeline should have generated hunting guidance for post-patch verification and systems still vulnerable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory all FortiSandbox instances (products: FortiSandbox, FortiSandbox Cloud, FortiSandbox PaaS) via vulnerability scanner. Confirm patch version >= remediation build post-2026-07-19. Flag any instance not patched AND accessible from internet-facing network segment.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox: CVE-2026-25089 Vulnerability Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'match against your vulnerability scanner' — pipeline must surface asset-discovery use case for Fortinet FortiSandbox (Cloud, PaaS) instances with vulnerable versions prior to 2026-07-19 patch deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan inventory for Fortinet FortiSandbox product (FortiSandbox, FortiSandbox Cloud, FortiSandbox PaaS) with CVE-2026-25089 unfixed. Alert on any vulnerable instance; prioritize externally exposed assets per CISA due date 2026-07-19.

suggestion.title: HTTP Command Injection Attempts Against FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'specifically crafted HTTP requests' combined with 'unauthenticated attacker' — pipeline must detect payloads containing shell metacharacters (semicolon, pipe, &&, backticks, $()) in HTTP requests targeting FortiSandbox endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP access logs for GET/POST requests to FortiSandbox URIs (e.g., /api/, /admin/, /upload/) containing shell metacharacters or known command-injection patterns. Flag requests with no authentication tokens (unauthenticated). Correlate with WAF blocks or 200-OK responses post-injection.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox: Unauthorized Process Spawning
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'execute unauthorized commands via ... HTTP requests' — this describes post-compromise OS-level code execution. Pipeline must hunt for abnormal process creation from FortiSandbox service accounts (e.g., sandbox, fortisandbox).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation spawned by FortiSandbox service principals (UID/GID or Windows service account) with unexpected parent processes, command lines, or destinations (especially reverse shells or C2 callbacks). Baseline normal FortiSandbox process patterns first.

suggestion.title: Internet-Exposed FortiSandbox Asset Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated attacker' attacking 'public-facing application' — pipeline must identify FortiSandbox instances reachable from internet (banner grab, port scan, Shodan/Censys correlation).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference external asset scans (Censys, Shodan historical, active discovery) for Fortinet product banners or known FortiSandbox-specific HTTP response headers (e.g., 'Server: Fortinet'). Alert on any hit; compare against approved DMZ asset inventory.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox: Patch Compliance Check Pre-Deadline
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Federal patch due: 2026-07-19' — pipeline must generate compliance-alert use case to flag any FortiSandbox instance not patched by federal deadline, especially on systems subject to compliance audit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Automated alert 5 days pre-deadline (2026-07-14) for any Fortinet FortiSandbox instance still unpatched. Include version strings, install path, and owner for remediation. Escalate if asset is internet-exposed or handles sensitive data.

suggestion.title: HTTP Anomaly: Request Body Size / Encoding Spike to FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'specifically crafted HTTP requests' — obfuscated or oversized payloads (base64, hex, URL encoding, chunked) in POST bodies to FortiSandbox endpoints may evade simple pattern matching.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP POST/PUT requests to FortiSandbox endpoints with abnormally large body size (> 10KB baseline), multi-layer encoding, or unusual Content-Transfer-Encoding headers. suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected child process creation from FortiSandbox web services (w3wp, nginx, tomcat, Java processes). Establish whitelisted parent-child process pairs per environment; flag anomalies with suspicious command lines or execution context.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Exploited FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: Unauthenticated access to FortiSandbox could be pivoted for lateral movement or data exfiltration. Monitor network connections initiated by the compromised application to unexpected internal/external destinations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish FortiSandbox egress policy baseline. Alert on outbound connections to non-whitelisted internal subnets, sensitive hosts (databases, domain controllers), or suspicious external IPs. Prioritize connections with high data volume or to known C2 indicators.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Service Crashes or Error Spikes
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation attempts may destabilize the service or trigger defensive logging. Monitor service logs for crashes, restarts, or abnormal error rates correlated with suspicious HTTP requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected FortiSandbox service restarts, crash dumps, or elevated error counts. Correlate with suspicious HTTP traffic or failed authentication attempts in the preceding time window.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiSandbox Unauthenticated HTTP Command Injection Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests'—core attack vector requiring endpoint/proxy monitoring for injection patterns against FortiSandbox endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to FortiSandbox API/admin endpoints (typically :8080, :443) for shell metacharacters (|, ;, &, $()), command substitution syntax, or known OS-command-injection signatures in URL parameters, POST bodies, or headers. Flag unauthenticated sources from external IP ranges.

suggestion.title: Process Execution from FortiSandbox Service Spawn
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies successful injection results in 'execute unauthorized commands.' Endpoint detection must capture child-process chains: FortiSandbox service → shell/interpreter with suspicious arguments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when FortiSandbox-related processes (e.g., cmdagent, fnsandbox) spawn shells (bash, sh, powershell.exe) with obfuscated arguments, unexpected working directories, or network activity. Look for parent-child chains crossing service/user boundaries.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiSandbox CVE-2026-25089 Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status implies active in-the-wild exploitation. Asset-exposure detection must identify FortiSandbox instances (including Cloud, PaaS variants) reachable from untrusted networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-correlate vulnerability scanner results (CVE-2026-25089 on FortiSandbox/FortiSandbox Cloud/FortiSandbox PaaS) against network scope. Flag instances exposed to external IP ranges or without firewall/segmentation controls. Validate against patch-management records post-2026-07-19 federal due-date.

suggestion.title: HTTP Header Pollution / Injection to FortiSandbox Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Attack surface is 'specifically crafted HTTP requests.' Detection requires inspection of HTTP headers and payloads for injection attempts targeting known vulnerable URIs before they reach the service.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to FortiSandbox endpoints (/api/*, /admin/*, /settings/*) for oversized headers, header-value anomalies, or characters triggering command parsing (backticks, $(…), newlines, wildcards). Use Web Application Firewall rule sets to block known command-injection payload signatures.

suggestion.title: Network Scanning Activity Targeting FortiSandbox Ports
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV implies active reconnaissance and exploitation in the wild. Detection should identify network scan patterns against FortiSandbox default ports (8080, 443, 8888) from external sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid, sequential connection attempts to FortiSandbox management ports from single source IPs, especially from public/untrusted ranges. Correlate with HTTP/404 responses, service-banner fingerprinting, or known FortiSandbox scanner user-agents to identify exploitation reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox: Unauthenticated Command Injection via HTTP
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests' — no detection scenario provided despite this being the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to FortiSandbox endpoints for command injection payloads (shell metacharacters: semicolon, pipe, ampersand, backticks, $(), ${} in query strings or POST bodies). Flag requests arriving before 2026-07-19 without valid authentication tokens.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox: Child Process Execution from HTTP Handler
suggestion.rationale: Article describes OS command injection but no process-level detection; exploitation should spawn shells as children of the FortiSandbox HTTP daemon.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on FortiSandbox processes (java.exe, python.exe, or Fortinet http handler) spawning unexpected child processes (bash, sh, cmd.exe, powershell). Parent-child relationship with no legitimate job queue entry is high-confidence.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox: Application Log Error Spike from Injection Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation attempts will likely generate malformed parameter errors in FortiSandbox logs; no log-based detection provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiSandbox application logs for sudden increase in HTTP 400/403 errors or 'invalid parameter' messages from single source IP. Correlate with payloads containing shell syntax (semicolon, pipe, command substitution operators).

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: FortiSandbox Internet-Facing Instance Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry implies public-facing FortiSandbox exposure; CVE exploitability is entirely dependent on network accessibility.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for internet-routable instances of FortiSandbox (default ports 8080, 8443, or custom). Cross-reference against patched asset inventory. Flag any instance with kernel/OS build date pre-patch-window (before 2026-07-19).

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox: CVE-2026-25089 Vulnerability Signature Match
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies CVE-2026-25089 but pipeline generated no scanner-based IOC or signature detection recommendation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Deploy CVE-2026-25089 detection via vulnerability scanners (Nessus, Qualys, Rapid7). Correlate with Shodan/Censys data for public-facing FortiSandbox instances. Due date: 2026-07-19.

suggestion.title: Notarized Malware Execution with Gatekeeper Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article headline explicitly states 'Uses Notarized Dropper to Pass Gatekeeper Checks'—this is the core attack vector (T1553.004). Pipeline failed to map this defense-evasion technique to a detection use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for execution of notarized applications that exhibit suspicious post-execution behavior (spawning hidden processes, accessing credential stores, establishing unexpected network connections). Flag processes from notarized bundles with mismatched code signatures or notarization timestamps far in the past.

suggestion.title: Dropper to Payload Stage Transition
suggestion.rationale: Article names it explicitly a 'dropper' mechanism. Pipeline missed modeling the two-stage attack (dropper → payload), which is the classic execution technique for macOS malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect parent-child process chains where notarized or legitimate-appearing parents spawn unexpected child processes with high entropy names, from temporary directories (/tmp, /var/tmp, ~/Library/Caches), or with code signatures mismatched to the parent.

suggestion.title: CrashStealer Infostealing Activity
suggestion.rationale: Malware name 'CrashStealer' indicates collection phase (credential/data theft). Pipeline generated zero collection-phase use cases despite this being explicit in the malware name.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious file access by dropper-spawned processes targeting ~/Library/Keychains, Safari/browser profile directories, SSH key locations, or .plist files containing credentials. Flag keyboard capture, screenshot APIs, or clipboard access from suspicious process chains.

suggestion.title: Infostealer Command-and-Control Communication
suggestion.rationale: An infostealer must exfiltrate stolen data via C2. Article provides no indication of C2 infrastructure, but pipeline should have generated detection use case for this critical capability (T1041, T1071).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound DNS queries and HTTP/HTTPS connections from process chains originating from the notarized dropper. Prioritize connections to newly registered domains, non-standard ports, or IPs without reverse DNS. Flag data volume inconsistent with legitimate app behavior.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Gatekeeper Bypass Artifacts
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes Gatekeeper evasion. Pipeline should flag specific techniques for bypassing macOS security controls (T1036.005 Masquerading, extended attribute manipulation).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for removal or modification of com.apple.quarantine extended attributes on downloaded files. Detect unsigned executables in .app bundles, mismatched code signing identities, or processes executed from double-extension filenames (e.g., 'App.app.bin').

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiSandbox Command Injection Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability allows 'unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests'—direct exploitation attempts should be huntable via HTTP access logs and request payload analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for HTTP requests targeting Fortinet FortiSandbox endpoints with payloads characteristic of OS command injection (shell metacharacters, command separators, or known exploit URIs). Correlate with Fortinet product identification in network telemetry or asset inventory.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Vulnerable Version Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry mandates federal remediation by 2026-07-19; pipeline must surface vulnerable instances. Article explicitly specifies affected products: 'FortiSandbox, FortiSandbox Cloud, and FortiSandbox PaaS'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan the fleet for Fortinet FortiSandbox instances and version-match against known vulnerable releases for CVE-2026-25089. Flag any internet-exposed instances immediately; CISA KEV designation indicates active exploitation.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Command Execution on FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: Article describes successful injection leads to 'execute unauthorized commands'—once injection succeeds, command execution logs should be monitored. 'OS command injection' implies T1059 execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiSandbox system logs for unexpected process spawning, shell invocations, or command execution patterns outside normal operational scope. Look for batch/shell commands initiated without user action, especially from web service processes.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiSandbox CVE-2026-25089 Vulnerability Scan Coverage
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly tags this CVE as CISA KEV (known exploited); standard risk practice requires scan coverage confirmation. Pipeline should reference the CVE identifier for correlation with scanner findings.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Verify all Fortinet FortiSandbox appliances are scanned and checked for CVE-2026-25089 presence. Cross-reference scanner reports against asset inventory; flag false negatives (scanner says not vulnerable but version matches affected range).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-0257 GlobalProtect Authentication Bypass Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'GlobalProtect portal and gateway... allows the attacker to bypass security restrictions and establish an unauthorized VPN connection.' Pipeline generated zero detection for the primary attack vector. Confirmed active exploitation from May 17, 2026 onward by Rapid7 observations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on GlobalProtect authentication requests with malformed payloads consistent with CVE-2026-0257 bypass techniques. Flag successful VPN sessions from IPs with no prior authentication history or from geographies inconsistent with user baseline. Correlate failed auth patterns preceding successful bypass attempts.

suggestion.title: Post-VPN Ransomware Deployment Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'intrusions... resulted in Qilin ransomware deployment' following CVE-2026-0257 exploitation. Pipeline failed to detect post-compromise activity. 'Post-exploitation tradecraft varied across intrusions, from rapid encryption-only operations to full double-extortion.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid file encryption across multiple network shares within 60 minutes of VPN session establishment. Alert on spawning of encryption-related utilities (vssadmin.exe, wbadmin.exe) or large volume of file modifications to .ransomware extensions. Correlate with outbound data transfers for double-extortion staging.

suggestion.title: Qilin RaaS Affiliate Scanning and Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'extensive scanning activity observed' and multiple Qilin affiliates exploiting under RaaS model. 'Arctic Wolf Labs assesses with moderate confidence that intrusions... are likely ongoing.' Pipeline did not identify reconnaissance phase or threat actor infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GlobalProtect VPN endpoints for abnormal health-check probes or repeated connection attempts from new source IPs. Flag systematic scanning of GlobalProtect services from known RaaS infrastructure. Alert on patterns consistent with vulnerability scanning for unpatched PAN-OS instances.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Post-VPN Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates attackers pivot from VPN entry into internal networks for encryption deployment across domains. 'Post-exploitation tradecraft' implies internal reconnaissance and movement before encryption. Pipeline missed lateral movement detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After successful VPN access, alert on SMB or RDP traffic from VPN session to internal hosts, followed by executable drops or credential access attempts (lsass dumps, ntlm_theft). Flag network scanning from newly-connected VPN clients to internal subnets.

suggestion.title: Double-Extortion Data Exfiltration Pre-Encryption
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'full double-extortion' operations by Qilin affiliates. Implies data staging and exfiltration before encryption. Pipeline did not detect exfiltration phase preceding encryption.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect high-volume outbound transfers to external cloud services or non-standard ports from systems behind compromised VPN. Alert on connection patterns to known Qilin data staging infrastructure or public paste services. Correlate with database access and document collection activity.

suggestion.title: Unpatched PAN-OS GlobalProtect Inventory Risk
suggestion.rationale: Article warns 'limited exploit attempts on unpatched PAN-OS devices without mitigations applied.' CISA ordered federal agencies to patch within three days (May 29 deadline). Pipeline missed asset inventory and patch compliance detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain inventory of Palo Alto PAN-OS versions and flag instances running builds prior to May 13, 2026 patch release. Cross-reference unpatched instances with Shodan/Shadowserver exposed GlobalProtect lists (167K+ instances). Alert on any exploit attempts against confirmed unpatched targets.

suggestion.title: WordPress Plugin Directory Scanning for wp2shell
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'public exploit fuels mass scanning' — attackers probe for /wp-content/plugins/wp2shell/ or plugin metadata endpoints to enumerate vulnerable instances before exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP GET requests to /wp-content/plugins/wp2shell/ paths, particularly when originating from external sources or occurring at abnormally high rates across multiple targets. Cluster by source IP to identify mass scanning campaigns.

suggestion.title: WordPress Plugin Exploitation via Public Exploit Code
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'public exploit' availability driving growth — attackers execute known payloads against wp2shell, likely via POST to plugin-specific endpoints or file-upload mechanisms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on POST requests to wp-config.php, wp-admin/upload.php, or plugin-upload endpoints with payloads containing shell metacharacters, base64-encoded PHP, or common webshell signatures. Monitor child processes spawned by www-data/apache user following suspicious HTTP activity.

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution via WordPress Webshell Upload
suggestion.rationale: wp2shell is a shell-upload plugin; article indicates 'mass' exploitation suggesting file-based compromise. Detect when plugin successfully uploads and executes shell code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PHP file creation in wp-content/uploads/ or wp-content/plugins/ directories followed by HTTP requests that trigger command execution. Correlate suspicious process spawning (bash, whoami, curl) with recent file-write events in WordPress directories.

suggestion.title: Mass WordPress Installation Discovery via HTTP Fingerprinting
suggestion.rationale: Article describes active scanning campaign — attackers perform HTTP probes to identify WordPress instances (wp-includes, wp-admin headers, cookie patterns) before targeting with wp2shell exploit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect source IPs making rapid sequential HTTP requests across disparate internal/external WordPress installations with User-Agent strings or request patterns consistent with automated scanners. Flag when single source probes >50 unique WordPress endpoints in <1 hour.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation WordPress Configuration Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Following successful wp2shell exploitation, article notes 'exploitation grows' — attackers read wp-config.php for database credentials and API keys, enabling lateral movement and data theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file-read events on wp-config.php or wp-settings.php by non-owner processes. Correlate with HTTP responses containing Base64-encoded config data, outbound SQL connections to non-standard ports, or DNS queries to exfiltration domains immediately post-compromise.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable WordPress Plugin Installation via Unpatched Core Vulnerability
suggestion.rationale: Article cites 'public exploit' availability; wp2shell likely exploits known WordPress core or plugin vulnerability. Detect installations remaining unpatched despite public advisories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference WordPress version/plugin version logs against public CVE databases. Alert when wp2shell or dependent plugins are detected on hosts running WordPress versions with known unpatched RCE flaws. Flag installations >30 days behind latest patch.

suggestion.title: Langflow RCE Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Langflow RCE Attack' but no execution-phase detection was generated to catch exploitation attempts against the Langflow service.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP POST/GET requests to Langflow service endpoints (typically :7860/api/*) containing serialized Python objects, shell metacharacters, or known RCE payloads. Flag process execution spawned directly from Langflow Python runtime with atypical command-line arguments.

suggestion.title: ENCFORGE Ransomware File Encryption Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Title identifies 'ENCFORGE Ransomware' as the payload, yet no impact-phase detection exists for file encryption behavior or ransom note creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk file-write activity targeting common model storage paths (.model/, .weights/, /models) with rapid sequential file modifications. Flag creation of .encforge extension variants or ransom note files (ENCFORGE_RANSOM.txt, ENCFORGE_NOTICE.html). Correlate with encryption key generation or cryptographic API calls.

suggestion.title: Targeted Discovery and Enumeration of AI Model Files
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes targeting 'AI Model Files' but no discovery-phase detection was generated for reconnaissance of model directories or file enumeration patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for recursive directory enumeration of typical ML model locations (/models, ~/.cache, /opt/huggingface, C:\Users\*\AppData\Local\huggingface). Flag processes (esp. cmd.exe, PowerShell, bash spawned post-Langflow compromise) searching for .pt, .pkl, .h5, .onnx, .pth file extensions in high volume.

suggestion.title: Langflow Child Process Execution with Suspicious Arguments
suggestion.rationale: RCE via Langflow would spawn shell processes; no detection addresses command injection or code execution through Python runtime interpreters.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when cmd.exe, bash, or sh spawned as child of python.exe or langflow processes with parent network activity from external IPs. Flag parent processes with ambiguous/obfuscated command lines or environment variables (PYTHONPATH, PYTHONHOME) set to unusual paths.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Compressed Model Archives
suggestion.rationale: AI model theft commonly precedes encryption; article does not specify but RCE + model targeting suggests data ex-filtration phase. No detection for bulk compression or staging.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation of .zip, .tar.gz, or .7z archives in temp directories containing extracted .pt or .pkl files. Correlate with large outbound data transfer (>100MB) to non-corporate IPs immediately post-exploitation. Flag 7zip.exe, tar, or gzip spawned by Langflow child processes.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to ServiceNow AI Platform Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Unauthenticated Code Execution'—this is the attack vector. Pipeline extracted no detection for authentication bypass or sessionless access to protected ServiceNow endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP 200 responses to ServiceNow /api/now/ai/* or /api/gpt/* endpoints from external IPs where Authorization header is absent, session token is missing, or pre-authentication indicators exist. Correlate temporal proximity with subsequent anomalous activity from same source.

suggestion.title: Code Execution Payload in ServiceNow AI Request
suggestion.rationale: Article headline promises 'Code Execution' but pipeline generated zero execution-phase detections. Should monitor for injection patterns in platform requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST/PUT requests to ServiceNow AI endpoints containing command-injection markers (shell metacharacters: |, &, $(), backticks) or script payloads (script tags, eval(), exec()) in request body or parameters, especially in unauthenticated session context.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Process Spawning from ServiceNow Service
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation of ServiceNow instance. No detection suggested for process-level anomalies or child-process creation under svc_* accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or bash spawned as child of java.exe or node.exe under ServiceNow service accounts with parent-process command-line absent or mismatch. Alert on unexpected network I/O or file access from spawned shells.

suggestion.title: Data Staging or Exfiltration from ServiceNow Post-RCE
suggestion.rationale: A critical RCE on ServiceNow (customer data platform) implies high-value exfiltration risk. Pipeline missed detection for bulk queries or outbound data transfer anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual outbound HTTPS/HTTP volume from ServiceNow instances post-compromise, or unexpected SQL queries against user/configuration tables from service accounts, followed by data staging in temp directories or archive creation.

suggestion.title: CVE-Specific ServiceNow AI Platform Exploit Pattern
suggestion.rationale: No detection signature offered for the specific exploit mechanism. Once CVE and POC details are public, require deterministic request matching.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Match HTTP requests to ServiceNow against known exploit request signatures (specific API path, parameter name/value combinations, or payload structure patterns from public POCs or vendor advisories).

suggestion.title: ServiceNow AI Platform Authentication Bypass Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article premise is 'unauthenticated' exploitation. No detection for session-hijacking, token-forgery, or auth-bypass artifacts in logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag requests to ServiceNow AI endpoints with abnormal or missing auth headers, mismatched user-agent/geolocation for the session owner, or rapid endpoint enumeration before exploitation attempt.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox CVE-2026-25089 Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in `../_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure`. Substitute this CVE wherever the template references `<CVE>`: CVE: `CVE-2026-25089`'. Pipeline ignored this direct instruction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify FortiSandbox, FortiSandbox Cloud, and FortiSandbox PaaS instances in your environment. Cross-reference against vulnerability scanner data and asset inventory. Prioritize by federal patch due-date (2026-07-19) and active exploitation status (CISA KEV).

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Unauthenticated Command Injection HTTP Payloads
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests'. Pipeline missed detection for malicious HTTP patterns targeting the exploit vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to FortiSandbox instances for command injection patterns (shell metacharacters, command separators, backticks, $() syntax in parameters). Flag anomalous POST/GET to API endpoints since exploitation requires no authentication.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Unexpected Child Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes OS command injection capability allowing attacker command execution. Pipeline did not generate detection for post-exploitation process spawning—the primary impact of successful code injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected child processes spawned by FortiSandbox service (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, sh, nc, curl). Prioritize detection of reverse shells, enumeration tools, or privilege escalation attempts from FortiSandbox parent process.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Instance Reconnaissance via HTTP Headers
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status indicates active exploitation. Attackers will probe for vulnerable instances. Article identifies HTTP-based exploitation, implying reconnaissance via HTTP fingerprinting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP probes containing FortiSandbox-specific User-Agent strings, requests to known API paths (/rest/v2/, /api/v2/), or responses revealing FortiSandbox server headers. Flag systematic scanning of FortiSandbox web console ports (typically 8443, 8000).

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Release Tag Redirected to Orphaned Commit
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The attacker deleted the original version tags and relocated them to the malicious commit, which was the orphaned commit... re-pointed several existing release tags to their malicious commit.' This is the core obfuscation and persistence mechanism; no detection logic exists.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub Actions repositories for release tags deleted and re-created pointing to commits absent from all branches. Flag tags (v*, release-*, semver) re-pointed to orphaned commits, especially in repos with >5000 dependents. Correlate with sudden code changes in malicious commit.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Encrypted Secrets Exposed in Plaintext Logs
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'An attacker with write privileges on the Action repo made a commit that caused encrypted secrets to appear in plaintext in the GitHub Action logs.' Direct credential exposure vector affecting all downstream users.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan GitHub Actions run logs in public repos for plaintext credential patterns (AWS key prefix, GitHub PAT, base64-encoded secrets). Alert when step output or log tail contains unencrypted values matching registered secret names. Cross-reference with repos using compromised Action version.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Compromise via Compromised GitHub Action Dependency
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'About 23,000 GitHub repos use this Action as part of their CI and DevOps workflows... The attacker deleted the original version tags and relocated them to the malicious commit.' Single compromised Action repo cascades to thousands of downstream consumers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for GitHub Actions pinned to specific versions (e.g., tj-actions/changed-files@v35) that suddenly execute different code after tag re-pointing. Correlate tag change in upstream Action repo with unexpected process execution or network calls in downstream repos using that version.

suggestion.title: Orphaned Git Commit Tagged with Production Release Version
suggestion.rationale: Article demonstrates: 'You can still navigate to that commit, even though it is no longer associated with any existing branch' and 'the attacker could point people to the malicious commit simply by updating... release tags.' Orphaned commits hide malicious code from branch-level audits.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For critical GitHub Action repos (>1000 dependents), scan for commits reachable via refs but orphaned from all branches. Alert if orphaned commits are tagged with release/version tags. Examine commit diff for credential-access logic, exfiltration, or external network calls.

suggestion.title: GitHub Action External Network Call to Fetch Payload
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The attack relied on making an external network call to pull down the attack code, which ultimately led to it being noticed by services that monitor anomalous network activity.' Unwhitelisted egress from Action runner is detection opportunity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub Actions runners for egress to external domains/IPs not declared in workflow YAML. Alert on curl/wget/python-requests executing in Action steps after recent upstream Action repo commit. Correlate with repos pinned to re-tagged versions.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Write Access Grant to High-Dependency GitHub Action Repository
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'As of this writing, it's unknown why the attacker had write permissions on the repo that houses this GitHub Action code. But, the key enabling factors for this attack beyond just having write permissions were...' Root-cause enabler: unauthorized write access to supply-chain artifact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For GitHub Actions with >5000 dependents, alert on: (1) new user/service-account write/admin role grants; (2) unexpected push activity from dormant accounts; (3) branch protection rule disablement; (4) force-push to main. Investigate timing correlation with downstream fork/watch activity.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure Hunt: CVE-2026-25089 Fortinet FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: Article mandates 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and explicitly lists affected products: 'Fortinet FortiSandbox, FortiSandbox Cloud, and FortiSandbox PaaS.' CISA KEV scope requires asset discovery prior to all other hunts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset database for Fortinet FortiSandbox instances (all variants). Cross-reference against patch release timeline (vendors typically release patch by federal due date 2026-07-19). Flag any unpatched or unscanned appliances as immediately exploitable.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated HTTP Exploitation of FortiSandbox (T1190)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests.' Attack requires zero authentication and HTTP is the delivery mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP request logs for traffic to known FortiSandbox management or API endpoints from external sources. Detect requests containing command-injection sequences (shell metacharacters: semicolon, pipe, dollar-paren, backticks) in URI, query string, or POST body.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload Execution on FortiSandbox (T1059.001)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability allows... execute unauthorized commands.' Successful exploitation results in arbitrary command execution under FortiSandbox service privileges.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor process execution logs on FortiSandbox appliances and parent servers for command shells (cmd.exe, /bin/bash, /bin/sh) spawned from web service processes or unprivileged contexts. Alert on OS commands executed outside maintenance windows or change tickets.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Public-Facing Exploitation – HTTP Request Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests'—directly implies detection of malformed or suspicious HTTP parameters targeting FortiSandbox endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiSandbox admin/API endpoints (typically port 8080, 8443, 541) for HTTP requests with OS command metacharacters (pipe, semicolon, backtick, $(), &&, ||) in query parameters or POST bodies. Baseline legitimate admin traffic, then flag requests from non-admin subnets or with unusual User-Agent strings.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Process Execution – OS Command Injection
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability allows 'execute unauthorized commands'—requires endpoint monitoring for unexpected child process spawning from FortiSandbox service accounts (e.g., fortisandbox user running shell, nc, curl, wget).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation events where parent is FortiSandbox daemon/worker process spawning shells (bash, sh, cmd.exe, PowerShell) or network utilities (curl, wget, nc, telnet). Legitimate FortiSandbox operation rarely spawns child processes; any occurrence is suspicious.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure – Fortinet FortiSandbox Internet Accessibility
