suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of actors who have legitimately called the PR-update endpoint over 30 days; flag any new users on this route within 24-hour window. Aggregate hits, source IPs, and target URLs to detect token-based attack patterns.

suggestion.title: Public-token authentication used to modify private-repository branch
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability: 'UpdatePullRequest() then authorizes the pull request update against the target pull request's head repository, which is the private repository.' This is authentication/authorization-state tampering not captured by suggested techniques.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate API tokens with public-only scope (or read-only scope) against branch-modification operations on private repositories. Flag tokens performing writes to repositories they lack explicit permission for, indicating authorization-bypass.

suggestion.title: Gitea token-scope circumvention via public-repository route proxy
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Gitea checks the token's public-only restriction against the route repository, which is the public base repository.' suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect requests to public repository endpoints that result in modifications to private-repository pull requests. Cross-reference repository ownership and token scopes: if a public-repo endpoint call updates a private-repo's head branch, log as scope-bypass attempt.

suggestion.title: Gitea Actions job execution from unexpected principals or IP ranges

Article does not address detection of the initial job submission from a compromised or stolen token.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Gitea Actions job invocations from principals that have never run jobs before, or from IPs geographically inconsistent with baseline. Cross-reference actor identity against repository ownership to flag out-of-character submissions.

suggestion.title: Rapid sequential Gitea artifact access probing (task/artifact ID enumeration)

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Artifact endpoint requests from a single user/token over a 1–5 minute window. Alert if taskID or artifactName parameter changes more than 5 times, or if requests show systematic increment/enumeration patterns (e.g., taskID 100→101→102).

suggestion.title: Gitea artifact access crossing repository boundaries (cross-repo read)
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'cross-repository artifact read.' While UC_8_3 hunts cross-task access, detection should explicitly track artifact reads that reference different repository names or owner contexts within the same signed URL session.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Extract repository name or owner from artifact URLs in download requests. Cluster by authenticated user/token. Alert if a single user downloads artifacts from 3+ distinct repositories within a 10-minute window, or if an artifact URL's repository name does not match the authenticated user's repositories.

suggestion.title: UPnP Service Exposure on DD-WRT Devices

suggestion.title: Malformed UPnP Packet / Buffer Overflow Attempts

suggestion.title: DD-WRT Firmware Version Inventory & Patch Compliance
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2021-27137 is in CISA KEV—exploitation is active and remediation is mandatory by 2026-07-24. Pipeline generated no asset-inventory hunt to locate vulnerable DD-WRT firmware versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan network inventory for DD-WRT devices and extract firmware version. Cross-reference against known-vulnerable versions. Flag any device with version < [patch version] and ensure patch deployment by federal due date 2026-07-24.

suggestion.title: Network Segmentation: UPnP Service Reachable from Untrusted Networks

suggestion.title: DD-WRT Device Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated attacker can overflow an internal buffer used by UPnP' — requires asset-exposure detection for exposed DD-WRT instances via UPnP service advertisement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for UPnP service advertisement on 1900/udp or HTTP banners containing 'DD-WRT' string. Correlate with asset inventory to flag unpatched instances. Expected sources: SSDP traffic, HTTP banner grabs, network device scans.

suggestion.title: CVE-2021-27137 Buffer Overflow Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability' in UPnP service — detect crafted UPnP payloads targeting the vulnerable code path in M-SEARCH or SOAP requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag UPnP traffic with abnormal packet sizes, malformed SOAP payloads, or oversized buffer values directed at DD-WRT on 1900/udp. Correlate with UPnP service crashes in device syslog to confirm exploitation success.

suggestion.title: DD-WRT Post-Exploitation Shell Access

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DD-WRT system logs for shell invocations (sh, bash, busybox), wget/curl calls, or process spawning following UPnP service anomalies. Alert on unexpected iptables, route, or network interface modifications.

suggestion.title: DD-WRT Vulnerability Patch Compliance Scan
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies federal patch deadline 2026-07-24 and CISA KEV guidance emphasizes patch lag as primary risk — scan environment for unpatched or outdated DD-WRT firmware versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for DD-WRT devices and compare firmware version against patched baseline post-2026-07-24. Prioritize internet-facing or externally-accessible instances. Alert on any device running pre-patch firmware versions.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance of DD-WRT UPnP Configuration
suggestion.rationale: Article states attack targets 'internal buffer used by UPnP' — reconnaissance activity probing UPnP service configuration or capability discovery precedes exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect repeated M-SEARCH queries, SSDP service requests, or SOAP descriptor fetches targeting DD-WRT devices. Baseline UPnP query patterns to identify anomalous reconnaissance prior to exploitation.

suggestion.title: DD-WRT UPnP Buffer Overflow Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated attacker to overflow an internal buffer used by UPnP and trigger a code execution vulnerability'—direct exploitation of the vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound traffic to UPnP ports (1900/UDP, 5000/TCP) on DD-WRT devices for malformed/oversized payloads, multipart SOAP requests, or abnormal packet sizes that could trigger buffer overflows. Correlate with service crashes or unexpected restarts.

suggestion.title: DD-WRT Public-Facing Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'Exploit Public-Facing Application' (T1190) and federal agencies required to remediate—assumes DD-WRT is internet-accessible.

suggestion.title: DD-WRT Service Crash or Unexpected Termination

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected UPnP daemon termination, core dumps, or rapid restart loops on DD-WRT devices. Correlate timing with inbound UPnP traffic spikes to isolate exploitation attempts.

Flag any devices still running vulnerable firmware builds.

suggestion.title: UPnP Reconnaissance or Service Fingerprinting

suggestion.title: CVE-2021-27137 Vulnerable DD-WRT Instance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and references `<CVE>` substitution template. Pipeline generated no UCs at all. Need to hunt for exposed DD-WRT instances running vulnerable versions.

suggestion.title: UPnP Buffer Overflow Exploitation Attempt

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Code Execution on DD-WRT
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'trigger[s] a code execution vulnerability' but pipeline mapped no execution-phase detection. Successful exploitation grants unauthenticated shell access.

suggestion.title: DD-WRT Device Reconnaissance Scan
suggestion.rationale: Article implies pre-exploitation reconnaissance phase: attackers must identify DD-WRT devices before attempting buffer overflow. No UC captures network scanning for these devices.

suggestion.title: Buffer Overflow Exploit Attempt Detection

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormally large UPnP payloads, malformed UPnP packets with buffer-overflow-signature padding (repeated byte sequences), or UPnP request sizes exceeding DD-WRT's expected buffer limits. Correlate with immediate process spawning or reverse-shell callbacks.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Code Execution on DD-WRT
suggestion.rationale: Article states buffer overflow 'trigger[s] a code execution vulnerability.' Pipeline has no detection for the post-exploitation phase despite this being the impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected process spawning from DD-WRT management services (e.g., UPnP daemon spawning shells, wget/curl, iptables commands). Monitor for unexpected outbound connections from router IP to external IPs immediately post-compromise.

suggestion.title: DD-WRT Lateral Movement / Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Compromised DD-WRT router is network edge asset with access to internal LAN. Article does not scope post-exploitation actions, but active exploitation warrants lateral-movement detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for anomalous internal traffic origination from DD-WRT management interface IPs (DHCP, DNS, ARP spoofing, internal scanning). Detect command-and-control beaconing from router to external infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable DD-WRT Device Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability affects 'public-facing' DD-WRT routers exploited in the wild (KEV status). Pipeline generated no hunts to find vulnerable instances despite article recommending 'standard asset-exposure hunt'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate devices running DD-WRT versions vulnerable to CVE-2021-27137 via vulnerability scanner integrations or banner-grab data. Alert on any public-facing instances in DMZ, edge networks, or cloud environments where router/gateway devices are internet-accessible.

suggestion.title: UPnP Buffer Overflow Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability is 'stack-based buffer overflow' in 'UPnP' service allowing 'unauthenticated attacker' to 'trigger code execution'. Pipeline missed execution-phase detection for in-flight exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor UPnP (UDP 1900, TCP 1900, TCP 5000, TCP 5353) traffic to DD-WRT devices for oversized or malformed M-SEARCH/SSDP packets, unusual parameter sizes, or proof-of-concept payload signatures. Stack overflows typically manifest as abnormally large Content-Length headers or payload sizes in UPnP discovery/control frames.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Code Execution on DD-WRT
suggestion.rationale: Article states overflow 'could allow... code execution'. If exploitation succeeds, should detect shell spawning, binary execution, or reverse-shell callbacks from compromised router.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DD-WRT devices for unexpected process spawning (busybox, sh, wget, curl), unexpected outbound connections to non-ISP destinations, or memory-access violations in UPnP daemon logs (if available). Cross-correlate with IDS/IPS alerts on UPnP exploitation signatures.

suggestion.title: Network Reconnaissance for Vulnerable UPnP Services
suggestion.rationale: Before exploiting buffer overflow, attacker must discover UPnP-enabled targets. Article describes unauthenticated attack, implying reconnaissance phase (T1046 network scans, T1592 info gathering).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on SSDP M-SEARCH floods or discovery queries from external IPs targeting internal networks. Watch for bulk UPnP port scanning (1900, 5000, 5353) from single source IPs over short time windows, especially if source IPs resolve to hosting providers or proxy services.

suggestion.title: CVE-2021-27137 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states CISA KEV entry with federal patch due 2026-07-24; standard asset-exposure hunt required to detect unpatched DD-WRT instances. Pipeline template suggests asset-exposure UC but generated none.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scanner results containing CVE-2021-27137 or DD-WRT products with versions prior to patched release. Correlate against patch-deadline 2026-07-24 to identify non-compliant assets.

suggestion.title: UPnP Buffer Overflow Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'buffer overflow... by UPnP' and 'unauthenticated attacker'—implies network-based attack surface. Pipeline did not extract UPnP attack vectors or network-based detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous UPnP traffic patterns (oversized payloads, malformed SOAP requests, or non-standard port 1900 activity) originating from untrusted networks targeting DD-WRT devices. Alert on port 1900/UDP or HTTP control-point requests with suspicious Content-Length headers.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Code Execution via DD-WRT Buffer Overflow
suggestion.rationale: Article states overflow 'trigger[s] a code execution vulnerability'—implies RCE execution phase. Pipeline mapped only T1190; missed T1059 execution and post-exploit process detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After CVE-2021-27137 exploitation, monitor DD-WRT devices for unexpected child processes spawned by system daemons (e.g., upnpd, minissdpd). Flag execution of shells, reverse shells, or download utilities launched from network service contexts.

suggestion.title: Patch Compliance Deadline Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Federal patch due: 2026-07-24' and notes 'patch lag is the silent killer.' Pipeline template mentions federal due-date importance but generated no UC for deadline tracking or compliance validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference asset inventory against DD-WRT firmware versions and CISA due date 2026-07-24. Generate compliance reports by patch status and days-overdue. Escalate any device still running vulnerable firmware past the deadline.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated UPnP Service Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack is 'unauthenticated'—implies reconnaissance via UPnP SSDP discovery or control-point queries. Pipeline did not map discovery or lateral-movement reconnaissance for UPnP-based asset identification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SSDP multicast queries (239.255.255.250:1900) or M-SEARCH requests on internal networks seeking UPnP-enabled devices. Flag port 1900/UDP responses that advertise DD-WRT user-agent strings to external sources.

suggestion.title: DD-WRT Vulnerable Instance Detection via Vulnerability Scan
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly requires 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and directs to scan for 'CVE-2021-27137' — SOC must identify unpatched DD-WRT systems before federal due date.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory and vulnerability scanners for DD-WRT systems with unpatched firmware. Flag instances showing missing security updates for CVE-2021-27137 before remediation deadline 2026-07-24.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated UPnP Protocol Buffer Overflow Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'stack-based buffer overflow...used by UPnP' allows 'unauthenticated attacker' to 'trigger code execution' — exploitation occurs on exposed UPnP services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect malformed, oversized, or repeated UPnP requests (SSDP/SOAP protocols) targeting DD-WRT devices on network edges. Look for buffer overflow patterns or unusual method calls from external sources.

suggestion.title: Process Execution Following UPnP Service Interaction
suggestion.rationale: Article threat describes successful exploitation will 'trigger a code execution vulnerability' — post-exploitation indicator linking UPnP activity to unexpected process spawning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate inbound UPnP protocol requests to DD-WRT systems with process creation events. Flag child-process spawning with unusual parents or command-line arguments following UPnP service traffic.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance for DD-WRT Devices via SSDP Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Attackers locate vulnerable instances first — article implies UPnP advertisement discovery mechanism used to find targets before exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SSDP M-SEARCH queries identifying DD-WRT user-agents or device descriptors. Alert on external sources querying UPnP multicast or parsing device advertisements.

suggestion.title: CVE-2021-27137 Vulnerability Detection (Asset Inventory)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2021-27137 — match against your vulnerability scanner' yet pipeline extracted zero IOCs. Foundation UC for identifying affected DD-WRT instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner logs and asset databases for systems reporting affected DD-WRT versions or UPnP services running on DD-WRT hardware. Compare scanner results against federal patch due date 2026-07-24.

suggestion.title: UPnP Service Exposure Hunting (DD-WRT)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability...used by UPnP and trigger a code execution.' No network exposure detection suggested for exploitable UPnP ports.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for UPnP services (UDP 1900 multicast, TCP 1900) on network segments where DD-WRT devices are deployed. Correlate with patch status to identify unpatched exposed instances.

suggestion.title: Buffer Overflow Exploitation Attempts (UPnP)

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for malformed or oversized UPnP packets to DD-WRT devices, particularly SSDP discovery responses or device description XML requests. Correlate payload patterns with known CVE-2021-27137 exploits.

suggestion.title: Patch Compliance Tracking (Federal Due Date)

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track DD-WRT devices and patch deployment status against federal due date 2026-07-24. Alert on any unpatched instances still online after deadline.

suggestion.title: DD-WRT Device Fleet Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'worth one quick check across your fleet' but no device discovery or fingerprinting UC provided. Foundation for targeting correct assets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all DD-WRT instances via HTTP server banners, UPnP device descriptors, DHCP vendor strings, or known subnet patterns. Cross-reference against patch inventory.

suggestion.title: DD-WRT UPnP Service Buffer Overflow Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could allow an unauthenticated attacker to overflow an internal buffer used by UPnP and trigger a code execution vulnerability.' No UC was generated to detect exploit attempts against this specific vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to common DD-WRT UPnP endpoints (/upnp, /soap) from untrusted sources. Baseline typical UPnP device discovery patterns and alert on malformed or oversized payloads. Flag connection attempts to port 1900 (UPnP) paired with subsequent suspicious system calls.

suggestion.title: DD-WRT Device Inventory and Public Exposure Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes CISA KEV status (currently exploited in the wild) and references 'asset-exposure hunt' but no UC was generated for identifying or inventorying vulnerable DD-WRT devices.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory and vulnerability scanner findings for DD-WRT installations, particularly those exposed to public/untrusted networks. Cross-reference patch status against known-safe versions post-2026-07-24. Flag devices answering on default DD-WRT ports (80, 443, 8080) without authentication overlay.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Code Execution via DD-WRT RCE
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'code execution vulnerability' resulting from the buffer overflow, but no detection UC addresses the execution phase following successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On compromised DD-WRT routers, monitor for anomalous process spawning (especially sh, bash, wget, curl) originating from UPnP or network-facing services. Flag execution of arbitrary binaries in /tmp or /var/tmp immediately following UPnP service anomalies. Correlate process creation with parent process UPnP daemon (upnpd, miniupnpd).

suggestion.title: CVE-2021-27137 Asset Exposure & Remediation Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in [_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure]' and explicitly recommends substituting CVE-2021-27137. Federal patch due date 2026-07-24 triggers compliance hunts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory all network-accessible DD-WRT instances via port scanning or vulnerability scanners. Cross-reference against known-vulnerable versions prior to CVE-2021-27137 fix release. Flag any instances not patched by federal due date 2026-07-24.

suggestion.title: UPnP Stack-Based Buffer Overflow Exploitation Attempts

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for malformed UPnP SSDP discovery packets (UDP/1900) or control protocol messages (TCP 49152+) to DD-WRT hosts with abnormal payload sizes or content patterns indicative of buffer overflow attempts.

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor compromised DD-WRT devices for unexpected child processes spawned from UPnP daemon, unusual command-line invocations (especially shell interpreters), or binary writes to system partitions post-compromise.

suggestion.title: DD-WRT Device Inventory & UPnP Service Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability...used by UPnP.' No detection generated for asset discovery of vulnerable DD-WRT deployments or identification of exposed UPnP services (UDP port 1900, SSDP). This is first-order hunt for exposed assets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for SSDP M-SEARCH requests (UDP port 1900) and HTTP requests to UPnP device descriptor endpoints. Enumerate responses containing DD-WRT vendor strings. Cross-reference with patch-status database to isolate pre-2026-07-24 unpatched systems.

suggestion.title: Malformed UPnP SOAP Request Detection (Buffer Overflow Attempt)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'overflow an internal buffer used by UPnP...trigger code execution.' No network-based detection generated for actual exploit attempts—malformed SOAP messages, oversized Device Description Protocol payloads, or crafted UPnP packets targeting the overflow.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect UPnP SOAP requests with anomalously large payloads, malformed XML, or repeated request patterns targeting vulnerable endpoint. Flag requests originating from untrusted networks toward internal UPnP services. Correlate with IDS/WAF alerts for buffer-overflow indicators.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Command Execution Linked to UPnP Interaction
suggestion.rationale: Article describes RCE outcome ('trigger a code execution vulnerability') but no hunt for post-compromise activity. Missing: detection of unexpected process spawn, reverse shells, or command execution following UPnP service interaction on same host.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Timeline-correlate UPnP service requests (port 1900/TCP or UDP) with unusual child process spawning on the same endpoint within 10-30 seconds. Flag interactive shells (cmd.exe, bash, sh) or reverse-shell payloads (curl, powershell remote downloads) originating from system processes (UPnP daemon).

suggestion.title: CVE-2021-27137 Vulnerability Confirmation via Passive Fingerprinting
suggestion.rationale: Article provides 'CVE-2021-27137' explicitly for vulnerability scanner matching, but pipeline omitted asset-based detection. Passive HTTP banner grabbing on port 80/443 and UPnP Device Description parsing can confirm vulnerable DD-WRT version strings without active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse HTTP Server headers and UPnP Device Description XML payloads for DD-WRT version strings. Cross-reference against known-vulnerable version ranges (pre-patch 2026-07-24). Alert on any match in external-facing assets.

suggestion.title: Federal Due-Date Patch Compliance Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Federal patch due: 2026-07-24'—a hard deadline for federal agencies. Pipeline should flag compliance tracking: monitor patch deployment rates across asset inventory to predict SLA miss before deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset database for all DD-WRT devices; correlate with patch-management system. Flag systems unpaired with evidence of patch application by 2026-07-24. Generate executive alert 7 days before deadline for any systems still in vulnerable state.

suggestion.title: CISA KEV Active-Exploitation Surge Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article source is 'CISA KEV'—by definition, actively exploited in wild. Pipeline should flag baseline spike in exploitation attempts for CVE-2021-27137 vs. historical rate, confirming pivot to active campaign phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish 30-day baseline of UPnP exploitation attempts targeting CVE-2021-27137. Alert if attempt rate exceeds baseline by >5x in 24-hour window, indicating coordinated campaign. Cross-check with external threat-feed confirmations of worm/botnet activity.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner Hit: CVE-2021-27137 in DD-WRT Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'CVE-2021-27137 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and emphasizes CISA KEV currently exploited status. Scanner detections are the first-line alert for this exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Vulnerability scanner finds CVE-2021-27137 on DD-WRT device with exposed UPnP. Correlate scanner timestamp with network segmentation bypass or public IP exposure to prioritize risk tier.

suggestion.title: Exposed DD-WRT UPnP Port Discovery

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for inbound UDP 1900 (SSDP) or TCP 49152-49200 (UPnP TCPv4) traffic destined to DD-WRT devices from external subnets. Spike in SSDP M-SEARCH frames may indicate reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: UPnP Buffer Overflow Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'stack-based buffer overflow...trigger code execution vulnerability.' Once exposed, exploitation involves malformed UPnP payloads. Detection requires protocol-level inspection of UPnP XML/SOAP messages for oversized or crafted inputs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect malformed UPnP SOAP requests or XML payloads exceeding normal bounds. Correlation with DD-WRT UPnP service logs showing crashes or restarts within minutes of suspicious traffic.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation: DD-WRT Process/Service Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'allow...code execution.' After successful buffer overflow, attacker gains RCE. Look for behavioral changes: unexpected process spawning, network outbound connections, or firmware modifications on compromised DD-WRT device.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DD-WRT syslog for abnormal process creation (shell, wget, curl). Detect outbound connections from DD-WRT to known C2 or data exfil infrastructure. Flag firmware backup/restore operations outside normal maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Federal Compliance Tracking: CVE-2021-27137 Remediation Deadline
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Federal patch due: 2026-07-24.' CISA KEV enforcement requires tracking — SLA breach indicates compliance risk. Asset inventory must tag all DD-WRT devices and enforce patch application by deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset database for all DD-WRT devices (identify via MAC OUI, DHCP hostname patterns, UPnP SSDP responses). Cross-reference with patch/update logs. Alert on any device still running unpatched firmware as of 2026-07-24.

suggestion.title: CVE-2021-27137 Vulnerability Scanning — DD-WRT UPnP

suggestion.title: Exploit Attempts Against UPnP Service (Port 1900)

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for malformed or oversized UPnP packets targeting port 1900/UDP on DD-WRT device ranges. Flag SSDP or UPnP service requests with suspicious payload lengths or format violations consistent with buffer overflow attempts.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Child Processes from UPnP Daemon

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any process spawned by UPnP daemon (upnpd, miniupnpd) or network services on DD-WRT routers, especially with unusual parent-child relationships, command-line injection attempts, or reverse-shell indicators.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised Router to Internal Network

suggestion.title: Asset Inventory: DD-WRT Instances with CVE-2021-27137 Exposure

Flag unpatched devices and track patch deployment against federal deadline. Correlate with external scanning (Shodan, Censys) to identify internet-exposed instances.

suggestion.title: Network Detection: UPnP Buffer Overflow Exploitation Attempts

Alert on sequence anomalies in device-to-device UPnP traffic. Correlate with known DD-WRT UPnP fingerprints.

suggestion.title: Code Execution Detection: Unexpected Shells or Service Launch on DD-WRT
suggestion.rationale: Article states exploit 'trigger[s] code execution vulnerability'—successful exploitation results in RCE; monitor device logs for unauthorized process spawning and shell access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected SSH/Telnet login success on DD-WRT from external sources, new root or unprivileged shell spawns in device logs, unknown service startup, or cron job creation. Baseline normal admin activity first; flag anomalies with timing correlation to exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation: Lateral Movement from Compromised Router

Monitor for modifications to routing tables, DHCP scope changes, or DNS poisoning. Flag if compromised router becomes C2 relay, credential harvesting point, or MITM node.

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query patch management system for CVE-2021-27137 remediation status across all DD-WRT instances. Flag devices patched past deadline; escalate as compliance violation. Track time-to-patch distribution to identify slow remediation patterns.

suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV context and 'unauthenticated attacker' language indicates immediate network-exposure risk; segmentation audit surfaces blast radius.

suggestion.title: Asset Inventory: DD-WRT Systems

suggestion.title: UPnP Service Exposure: DD-WRT
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies UPnP as attack surface: 'buffer used by UPnP' and 'unauthenticated attacker.' Pipeline must hunt for exposed UPnP services on network perimeter.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify UPnP (UDP 1900, TCP 1900) traffic originating from external IPs to internal DD-WRT systems. Correlate with asset inventory to flag unsecured UPnP endpoints. Baseline: any UPnP inbound from untrusted networks is suspicious.

suggestion.title: CVE-2021-27137 Exploitation Attempt (Buffer Overflow Patterns)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'stack-based buffer overflow' via UPnP service. Pipeline must detect exploitation attempts—malformed UPnP packets or oversized payloads triggering buffer conditions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormally large UPnP protocol messages or malformed SOAP/XML payloads to DD-WRT UPnP listeners. Flag packets exceeding normal UPnP message size boundaries. Correlate IDS rules for buffer overflow signatures with UPnP port traffic.

suggestion.title: Patch Compliance: CVE-2021-27137 Deadline Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies federal due date '2026-07-24'. Pipeline must enforce deadline tracking to flag non-compliant systems and audit readiness.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference DD-WRT asset inventory with patch management system. Flag any systems not showing successful patch deployment or version update by 2026-07-23. Generate compliance report for audit and incident escalation.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner Correlation: CVE-2021-27137
suggestion.rationale: Article instructs 'match against your vulnerability scanner.' Pipeline must integrate CVE-2021-27137 as detection rule in Qualys, Tenable, or equivalent scanners.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enable CVE-2021-27137 detection in active and passive vulnerability scanners. Report any DD-WRT systems showing positive match. Filter out false negatives (e.g., patched versions, isolated systems) to focus on actively exploitable assets.

suggestion.title: CVE-2021-27137 DD-WRT Vulnerability Scan Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states CISA KEV status ('observed exploited in the wild') and prescribes asset-exposure hunt; pipeline produced zero use cases despite clear guidance to apply template to this CVE with federal due-date 2026-07-24
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for DD-WRT instances flagged vulnerable to CVE-2021-27137 in vulnerability scanner output. Cross-correlate with asset inventory to identify public-facing or internet-routable devices. Federal agencies must remediate by 2026-07-24.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated UPnP Buffer Overflow Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'stack-based buffer overflow...by UPnP' and 'unauthenticated attacker...trigger code execution'; network exploitation patterns should be detected but pipeline surfaced no use cases
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for malformed UPnP SOAP requests, oversized Content-Length payloads, or suspicious M-SEARCH responses directed at DD-WRT instances. Look for network patterns consistent with buffer overflow exploitation on UDP 1900 or typical UPnP ports.

suggestion.title: Public-Facing DD-WRT Inventory Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'public-facing application' and unauthenticated attack vector; asset exposure discovery is missing despite being core to CISA KEV hunts
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify DD-WRT devices exposed on public internet or DMZ via UPnP fingerprinting (SSDP advertisements, HTTP banner grabs, default web interface signatures). Correlate external visibility against internal asset inventory to identify undocumented public-facing routers.

suggestion.title: DD-WRT UPnP Buffer Overflow Exploit Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated attacker to overflow an internal buffer used by UPnP and trigger a code execution vulnerability.' This is the primary attack surface and requires hunt rules for malformed UPnP packets or buffer-overflow payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for UPnP service communications (UDP 1900, TCP 49152–65535) targeting DD-WRT devices with anomalously large or malformed payloads; correlate with subsequent process spawning or network outbound connections from the device.

suggestion.title: DD-WRT Device Reconnaissance (UPnP Discovery)
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies vulnerability in UPnP service; attackers must discover exposed DD-WRT devices first. Article phrase: 'publicly-facing application' implied by CISA KEV requirement for 'observed exploited in the wild.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for SSDP M-SEARCH traffic (UDP 1900) at scale; correlate responses containing 'DD-WRT' or 'UPnP/1.0' device descriptions; flag internet-routable devices identified as DD-WRT.

suggestion.title: DD-WRT Post-Exploitation Command Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states buffer overflow 'trigger[s] a code execution vulnerability.' No specification of execution method, but article implies arbitrary code. Should hunt for shell spawning, unexpected process trees, or shell metacharacters in UPnP-adjacent logs post-overflow.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DD-WRT device logs (syslog, auth logs) for shell spawning (sh, bash, ash) immediately following UPnP service anomalies or crashes; correlate with outbound connections or sensitive file access.

suggestion.title: CVE-2021-27137 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly references 'CVE-2021-27137 — match against your vulnerability scanner.' Pipeline must emit IOC for scanners and asset-inventory queries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset-inventory for DD-WRT firmware versions ≤ [unfixed version]; cross-reference with vulnerability scanner reports containing CVE-2021-27137; flag unpatched instances and remediation-overdue date (2026-07-24 per article).

suggestion.title: DD-WRT Firmware Version Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'DD-WRT' product but does not specify vulnerable firmware versions. Pipeline should enumerate firmware versions or recommend telemetry-collection rule to extract firmware version from device banners or config, enabling risk-stratified remediation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Capture HTTP responses from DD-WRT web UI (port 80, 443) to extract 'Server' or 'X-UA-Compatible' headers; correlate firmware version regex against public CVE-2021-27137 impact matrix to identify unpatched assets.

suggestion.title: Asset Inventory: DD-WRT Exposure on WAN
suggestion.rationale: Article states CVE-2021-27137 affects DD-WRT with 'unauthenticated attacker' threat model and article context implies federal agencies must remediate. Primary hunt: identify at-risk devices before exploitation. Article: 'DD-WRT contains a stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated attacker.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for CVE-2021-27137 against DD-WRT product. Cross-reference with network exposure assessments (WAN-exposed management interfaces, UPnP services). Identify systems past federal patch deadline (2026-07-24).

suggestion.title: UPnP Service Discovery Probing from External Sources
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names UPnP as attack vector: 'overflow an internal buffer used by UPnP and trigger a code execution vulnerability.' Reconnaissance pattern: attackers probe for vulnerable UPnP services on accessible networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on SSDP discovery probes (UDP/1900) originating from external/untrusted IP space targeting internal gateways. Flag sequential UPnP M-SEARCH requests consistent with device enumeration. Correlate spike with DD-WRT asset locations.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Code Execution on Network Device
suggestion.rationale: Article outcome: 'trigger a code execution vulnerability.' Detection must cover behavioral indicators on router after successful exploit—unexpected processes, connections, or configuration writes from network infrastructure devices.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If DD-WRT endpoints have agent coverage, baseline normal UPnP service behavior and alert on child processes spawned from UPnP daemon. Monitor for unexpected outbound connections (non-HTTP/DNS) from compromised router to external infrastructure immediately post-UPnP interaction anomaly.

suggestion.title: CVE-2021-27137 Vulnerability Detection in Active Scans
suggestion.rationale: Standard detection baseline. Article explicitly names CVE-2021-27137 as the exploited vulnerability. Pipeline instructions note: 'CVE: CVE-2021-27137' must be substituted into asset-exposure hunt templates.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query CVSS/vuln scanner for CVE-2021-27137 findings. Segment by DD-WRT version. Identify unpatched systems. Cross-correlate with last scan date vs. federal remediation deadline (2026-07-24). Flag any flagged assets with outbound network activity post-detection.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Router Management Interface Access
suggestion.rationale: Successful RCE via UPnP frequently enables attacker to establish persistence or exfiltrate config (credentials, routing rules). Detecting anomalous access to router HTTP/HTTPS admin interfaces signals post-exploitation activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DD-WRT admin interface (typically TCP/80, 443, 8080) for login attempts and config changes from IPs not in baseline. Flag access anomalies occurring shortly after UPnP probe or service crash indicators. Alert on configuration backup download or firmware writes.

suggestion.title: CVE-2021-27137 Asset Exposure — DD-WRT Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and provides template guidance: 'Substitute this CVE wherever the template references <CVE>: CVE-2021-27137'. Pipeline generated zero asset-inventory or vulnerability-scan use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and asset-inventory systems for DD-WRT instances matching CVE-2021-27137 criteria. Cross-reference firmware versions against patch timeline (due 2026-07-24). Flag all public-facing DD-WRT devices on ports 23, 80, 443, and 1900 (UPnP).

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated UPnP Buffer Overflow Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'unauthenticated attacker to overflow an internal buffer used by UPnP and trigger a code execution vulnerability'—core execution vector, yet pipeline missed execution-phase detection entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DD-WRT UPnP daemon (port 1900/UDP, 1989/TCP) for malformed packets exceeding buffer limits. Correlate with unexpected process termination, restart cycles, or core dumps. Alert on rapid successive UPnP service crashes within <5min window.

suggestion.title: UPnP Service Discovery from Untrusted Networks
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes vulnerability exploitable by 'unauthenticated attacker'—discovery phase must precede exploitation. Pipeline generated no reconnaissance-phase use case for UPnP enumeration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag SSDP M-SEARCH packets (239.255.255.250:1900) originating from external/untrusted networks. Baseline UPnP service responses from internal DD-WRT devices. Alert on successful device enumeration or descriptor fetches from untrusted sources.

suggestion.title: DD-WRT Firmware Patch Compliance — Federal Deadline Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Federal patch due: 2026-07-24' but pipeline generated zero compliance or audit-timeline use case. Regulatory deadline tracking is critical SOC function for CISA KEV.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query CMDB/inventory for all DD-WRT instances. Extract firmware versions and compare against patch release date (2026-07-24). Generate compliance exceptions report; correlate un-patched devices against network exposure (external DNS, port scans, public-facing status).

suggestion.title: Memory Fault Detection in UPnP Stack Handler
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'stack-based buffer overflow'—suggests runtime memory fault signatures (segmentation faults, illegal memory access) yet pipeline missed kernel/process-level execution indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor UPnP daemon process (upnpd, miniupnpd) for segmentation faults, illegal memory access, or unhandled exceptions. Correlate with abnormal termination codes or supervisor restarts. Collect core dumps if available; analyze for exploitation signatures (jump-to-shellcode, return-oriented programming).

suggestion.title: GitHub Release Tag Repositioning to Malicious Commit
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'The attacker deleted the original version tags and relocated them to the malicious commit, which was the orphaned commit. The attacker re-pointed several existing release tags to their malicious commit.' Tag manipulation is the core obfuscation mechanism and a direct detection opportunity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when version/release tags (v35, v36, etc.) are modified to point to different commits than historical references, especially to commits outside main/master branches. Flag tag redirection events coupled with commits that have no associated pull requests.

suggestion.title: Orphaned Commit Creation and Obfuscation
suggestion.rationale: Article details: 'Having the attack commit orphaned from any branches, including the main branch. These factors added a bit of obfuscation to hide the attack.' Orphaned commits are explicitly identified as a 'key enabling factor' and are the obfuscation mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag commits that are not reachable from any branch head but are still accessible via URL or tag. Correlate orphaned commits with tag changes; alert when orphaned commits are referenced by release tags, especially if those commits modify CI/CD configuration or secrets handling.

suggestion.title: Plaintext Secrets Exposure in GitHub Actions Logs
suggestion.rationale: Core impact stated: 'caused encrypted secrets to appear in plaintext in the GitHub Action logs. This could lead to a devastating breach on a public repo where the Action logs are also public.' This is the credential-access payload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub Actions logs for patterns matching common secret formats (AWS credentials, API tokens, GitHub tokens) that appear in plaintext. Compare against organization's known secret prefixes to detect unencrypted credential leakage in workflow runs.

suggestion.title: Anomalous External Network Calls from GitHub Actions
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'The attack relied on making an external network call to pull down the attack code, which ultimately led to it being noticed by services that monitor anomalous network activity.' This external call is how the attack was detected and is the C2/exfiltration channel.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unexpected outbound connections from GitHub Actions runners to non-approved domains, especially in early job steps or in steps that should not perform network operations. Correlate with commit metadata to identify when new network rules or code patterns were introduced.

suggestion.title: Write Access Grant to High-Dependency Repository
suggestion.rationale: Foundational condition: 'A malicious actor had write access to a repo that 23,000 other repos relied on.' While origin unknown, unexpected write permissions on widely-used CI/CD actions should trigger alerts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on new write-level permissions granted to non-core-maintainer accounts on high-dependency repositories (>100 downstream dependents). Flag access grants from unusual geographies or times relative to account history.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Compromise via Popular GitHub Action
suggestion.rationale: Attack exploits trust relationship: 23,000 repos use changed-files as a dependency. Compromise of this action distribution point affects all consumers downstream. Article notes impact: 'About 23,000 GitHub repos use this Action as part of their CI and DevOps workflows.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor popular GitHub Actions for unexpected code changes, new external dependencies, or new network calls. Alert all downstream consumers when a high-dependency action introduces suspicious patterns. Track version pinning compliance—repos pinned to v35 are at risk.

suggestion.title: DD-WRT Vulnerable Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'DD-WRT contains a stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability' with federal patch due 2026-07-24—SOC must identify and inventory vulnerable instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory and vulnerability scanners for DD-WRT installations matching CVE-2021-27137. Cross-reference with network exposure data to identify externally-reachable instances that represent immediate exploitation risk.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated UPnP Buffer Overflow Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'unauthenticated attacker to overflow an internal buffer used by UPnP and trigger a code execution vulnerability'—this is the core exploitation vector requiring network-layer detection of malformed UPnP payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor UPnP traffic (UDP 1900, TCP 5000-5009) for oversized or malformed payloads targeting DD-WRT hosts. Alert on IDS signatures matching buffer overflow patterns in SSDP/UPnP protocol messages destined to vulnerable devices.

suggestion.title: UPnP Service Crash or Abnormal Restart on DD-WRT
suggestion.rationale: Stack-based buffer overflow inherently risks segmentation fault; article's 'overflow an internal buffer' mechanism will inevitably produce service termination or restart cycles detectable via system logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected termination or rapid restart cycles of UPnP daemon (miniupnpd or equivalent) on DD-WRT instances. Correlate process crashes with network anomalies (sudden loss of UPnP responsiveness) to distinguish exploitation attempts from legitimate faults.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Code Execution from UPnP Service Context
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation will 'trigger a code execution vulnerability'; attacker gains arbitrary execution within service context. Monitor for command spawning from UPnP process context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unexpected process launches (bash, wget, nc) with UPnP daemon as parent or context. Alert on command-line arguments indicating reconnaissance (ifconfig, cat /etc/passwd), persistence (crontab), or lateral movement (ssh, nmap).

suggestion.title: External Network Exposure of DD-WRT UPnP Service
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV documents active exploitation 'in the wild'; unauthenticated attack surface requires UPnP publicly accessible. Perimeter must isolate or protect UPnP from internet routing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan perimeter for inbound traffic to UPnP ports (UDP 1900, TCP 5000+) from internet-routable source IPs. Flag any DD-WRT instance with publicly-accessible UPnP as misconfiguration. Verify ingress ACLs block external UPnP traffic.

suggestion.title: Asset exposure: DD-WRT instances with UPnP enabled
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability allows 'unauthenticated attacker to overflow an internal buffer used by UPnP'; exposed instances are prime targets for T1190 exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for DD-WRT devices with UPnP service discovery responses (SSDP traffic port 1900) or successful UPnP device enumeration. Correlate against asset inventory to identify exposed routers without firewall rules blocking UPnP.

suggestion.title: CVE-2021-27137 vulnerability scanner matches
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs: 'CVE-2021-27137 — match against your vulnerability scanner'; pipeline must extract and surface this as detection basis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor vulnerability scanner output (Nessus, Qualys, Tenable) for CVE-2021-27137 detections against DD-WRT devices. Alert on any matches; federal patch due date is 2026-07-24, flag patch lag beyond that date.

suggestion.title: UPnP buffer overflow exploit traffic (network-based)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability' in UPnP handler; exploit traffic will exhibit malformed UPnP control protocol messages with oversized payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect UPnP protocol traffic (UDP/1900, TCP/49152-65535 for control/event channels) with abnormally large payloads or malformed XML/SOAP messages. IDS signatures for DD-WRT UPnP buffer overflow (known PoC exploits).

suggestion.title: Patch verification: DD-WRT firmware version audit
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' and federal deadline 2026-07-24; detection must include version checks to confirm vulnerable vs. patched firmware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate DD-WRT devices via SNMP system description, HTTP Server headers, or UPnP device descriptors to extract firmware version. Alert on versions vulnerable to CVE-2021-27137 (version threshold per vendor advisory).

suggestion.title: CVE-2021-27137 Exploitation Detection (UPnP Buffer Overflow)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability' in UPnP affecting DD-WRT; 'unauthenticated attacker' and 'code execution vulnerability' with active CISA KEV exploitation status. Pipeline generated zero detections despite clear attack vectors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DD-WRT instances for anomalous UPnP multicast traffic, oversized or malformed UPnP payloads indicating buffer overflow attempts, and unexpected child process spawning correlating with UPnP activity on ports 1900/UDP and 80/TCP.

suggestion.title: DD-WRT Asset Exposure and Patch Compliance Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and describes vulnerability in public-facing context (T1190). Federal patch deadline 2026-07-24 requires inventory tracking. Pipeline omitted asset discovery detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all DD-WRT instances via network scanning (HTTP/HTTPS on 80/443, SSH 22, UPnP 1900/UDP); cross-reference against patch management for CVE-2021-27137 status. Flag unpatched devices as critical due to CISA KEV active-exploitation confirmation and federal compliance deadline.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Code Execution from DD-WRT RCE
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'code execution vulnerability' outcome of buffer overflow; CISA KEV status confirms exploitation in wild. Pipeline failed to generate post-compromise detection despite RCE being primary threat impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor compromised DD-WRT devices for unexpected shell spawning (sh, bash, ash), outbound connections to non-ISP nameservers or foreign IPs, file modifications in /etc or /bin directories, and persistence mechanisms (cron, rc.local, init.d changes).

suggestion.title: Exposed DD-WRT UPnP Service Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is in 'internal buffer used by UPnP' on public-facing DD-WRT. Implies UPnP service enumeration and port 1900 exposure hunting. 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' referenced in article.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for inbound traffic to UDP 1900 (UPnP) from untrusted networks. Cross-reference DD-WRT inventory against public IP exposure. Flag devices with UPnP service responding to external queries. Template: look for SSDP M-SEARCH responses indicating exposed UPnP.

suggestion.title: DD-WRT UPnP Buffer Overflow Exploit Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated attacker to overflow an internal buffer used by UPnP and trigger code execution.' Network-based detection of malformed UPnP requests targeting stack frame corruption patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for UPnP requests with payload size anomalies or crafted buffer sequences. IDS/IPS rule: detect SUBSCRIBE/NOTIFY/M-SEARCH packets with oversized headers or binary payloads matching DD-WRT UPnP daemon buffer layout. Flag CVE-2021-27137-specific signatures.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation DD-WRT Process Spawning
suggestion.rationale: Buffer overflow 'trigger[s] code execution'—post-exploitation implies shell spawning or service restart. Monitor for abnormal process activity from UPnP daemon (typically upnp or miniupnpd process on DD-WRT).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child process spawning from UPnP daemon (e.g., upnpd, miniupnpd spawning /bin/sh, bash, or wget). Monitor for unexpected network connections initiated by UPnP process post-crash. Cross-reference with DD-WRT device inventory.

suggestion.title: DD-WRT Firmware Modification Detection
suggestion.rationale: Code execution via buffer overflow likely results in firmware tampering or persistence. Article implies active exploitation—monitor for filesystem changes in /etc, /www, or firmware partitions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag modification of DD-WRT config files (/etc/config/*), web root (/www), or firmware regions. Monitor for unexpected reboots with hash mismatches on critical binaries. Alert on persistence mechanisms (cron jobs, rc scripts) added post-compromise.

suggestion.title: DD-WRT CVE-2021-27137 Vulnerability Scan
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry—federal due date 2026-07-24. Article states 'even if scanners say not vulnerable because of patches, worth one quick check.' Asset inventory + vulnerability assessment of DD-WRT version numbers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference DD-WRT device inventory against known-vulnerable firmware versions (pre-patch releases for CVE-2021-27137). Query vulnerability scanner for CVE-2021-27137 matches. Alert on unpatched devices exposed to internet. Correlate with network exposure data.

suggestion.title: DD-WRT Public-Facing Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated attacker' can trigger overflow — requires exposed instances. Use case template referenced in article (`_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure`) with CVE-2021-27137.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for WAN-facing devices responding with DD-WRT HTTP signatures (web UI on 80/443/8080, /Status_Router.live.asp, DD-WRT version strings in HTTP headers). Correlate with device inventory to flag unpatched instances.

suggestion.title: UPnP Buffer Overflow Exploitation Traffic
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability...in UPnP' — exploitation likely sends malformed SOAP/SSDP payloads with oversized buffers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect abnormal UPnP traffic (UDP/TCP 1900, 5000, 49152+) with payload sizes exceeding normal SSDP/SOAP message boundaries or malformed structure matching known CVE-2021-27137 exploit patterns.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Remote Code Execution on Router
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'trigger a code execution vulnerability' — successful exploitation results in shell access on DD-WRT device.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for process spawning on DD-WRT devices following suspicious UPnP traffic: bash, sh, wget, curl, or iptables commands. Monitor for unexpected process creation or script execution on router/gateway devices.

suggestion.title: Configuration Exfiltration from Compromised DD-WRT
suggestion.rationale: Router code execution commonly followed by extraction of credentials/WiFi keys from nvram or config files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect access to /etc/config, /etc/passwd, nvram dumps, or wireless PSK files on DD-WRT post-exploitation. Hunt for bulk file reads or tar/compression of config directories.

suggestion.title: Router-Sourced Internal Network Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Compromised router pivots to internal network — searches for connected hosts, open ports, credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for ARP scans, DNS queries, or port scanning originating from compromised router IP targeting internal subnets post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: Botnet Recruitment or Persistence via DD-WRT
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV implies active exploitation; compromised routers often conscripted into botnets or retained for C2 beachhead.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for outbound connections from DD-WRT devices to known C2 infrastructure, large volumes of encrypted traffic, or DNS queries to known botnet domains post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: DD-WRT Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes unauthenticated access ('unauthenticated attacker') and CISA KEV context signals active scanning for exposed DD-WRT instances. No asset inventory use case generated despite this being the canonical first hunt for any public-facing vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify DD-WRT devices accessible from the internet by scanning for HTTP responses matching DD-WRT WebUI signatures (default ports 80, 443, 8443; distinctive HTML footprints in 200-OK responses). Correlate with vulnerability scanner output to identify patched vs. at-risk instances.

suggestion.title: UPnP Buffer Overflow Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability exists in 'internal buffer used by UPnP'—attack vector is explicitly UPnP protocol abuse. No detection for malformed or oversized UPnP packets attempting overflow.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor UDP port 1900 (UPnP SSDP) and TCP ports 49000–49999 (UPnP device control) for abnormal traffic: packets exceeding typical UPnP message sizes, malformed XML payloads in M-SEARCH or NOTIFY requests, or rapid sequential UPnP requests from single source IP. Correlate with IDS/IPS alerts for buffer-overflow-like payload patterns.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Process Execution on DD-WRT
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'code execution vulnerability'—post-exploitation activity on compromised DD-WRT devices must be monitored. No use case for detecting shell spawning or reverse shells.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On DD-WRT instances where logging is enabled, detect unexpected process spawning (busybox, sh, wget, curl) with network outbound connections or abnormal parent-child relationships (UPnP daemon spawning shells). Establish baseline of normal DD-WRT processes and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance of UPnP Services
suggestion.rationale: KEV context implies active exploitation; reconnaissance precedes exploitation. Article does not mention reconnaissance, but asset-discovery and port-scanning activity is a precursor to targeted CVE exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for SSDP M-SEARCH requests (UDP 1900) originating from external IP ranges targeting internal DD-WRT instances, or rapid UPnP port-scan activity (49000–49999 TCP). Correlate multiple SSDP discovery attempts from same source IP as indicator of UPnP service enumeration.

suggestion.title: Identify DD-WRT Devices in Managed Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'Vendor: DD-WRT, Product: DD-WRT' as the affected product. Asset baseline is prerequisite for targeted vulnerability hunting and patch compliance tracking before 2026-07-24 deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for DD-WRT devices by device model or firmware identifiers. Correlate against CVE-2021-27137 timeline to identify unpatched instances and prioritize remediation by federal deadline.

suggestion.title: Detect Exploitation of UPnP Buffer Overflow in DD-WRT
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could allow an unauthenticated attacker to overflow an internal buffer used by UPnP and trigger a code execution vulnerability.' Malformed UPnP requests are the exploitation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for malformed UPnP SOAP messages targeting DD-WRT devices on standard UPnP ports (49152-49161). Flag oversized or structurally invalid payloads in M-SEARCH, NOTIFY, or control requests.

suggestion.title: Monitor for Code Execution Post-Buffer Overflow in DD-WRT
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies the overflow 'trigger[s] a code execution vulnerability.' Successful exploitation leads to arbitrary code execution; detecting this phase is critical for identifying compromised devices.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected child processes spawned by UPnP daemon (upnpd, miniupnpd) on DD-WRT routers, or new outbound connections from UPnP service to external hosts indicative of post-exploitation shell activity.

suggestion.title: DD-WRT Asset Exposure and CVE-2021-27137 Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'unauthenticated attacker' accessing exposed UPnP service—baseline hunt for vulnerable product instances required.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan all network devices for DD-WRT installations and cross-reference against CVE-2021-27137 patch status. Flag any device with unpatched firmware as of federal due date 2026-07-24. Correlate external network exposure (WAN access to ports 80, 443, 8080) with unpatched inventory.

suggestion.title: UPnP Buffer Overflow Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'stack-based buffer overflow' in 'internal buffer used by UPnP' — protocol-level payload anomaly detection required.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor UPnP service traffic (UDP 1900, TCP 1900-1901) for payloads exceeding normal parameter boundaries, stack smashing signatures, or malformed SOAP/XML in M-SEARCH requests and device descriptor queries targeting DD-WRT targets.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated UPnP Service Access Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'unauthenticated attacker' exploit path—baseline normal UPnP access patterns required before exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unauthenticated external access to UPnP control paths (/upnp/*, /soap, device descriptor endpoints) on DD-WRT devices. Establish baseline of legitimate UPnP discovery patterns and flag anomalous multicast/unicast probing or device control attempts from WAN.
