suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query all DD-WRT appliances for running firmware version via management interface or SNMP. Compare against vendor's patched release list. Flag any device running vulnerable build; cross-reference with firewall/network position for exposure level.

suggestion.title: Unpatched DD-WRT Device Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is 'currently being exploited' with federal patch deadline 2026-07-24. 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' is explicitly recommended but no use case exists to identify exposed DD-WRT instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results and network inventory for DD-WRT instances matching CVE-2021-27137. Prioritize public-facing devices; correlate with external IP enumeration to surface internet-accessible targets.

suggestion.title: UPnP Stack-Based Buffer Overflow Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability...used by UPnP' but no detection covers malformed UPnP packets or exploitation patterns on port 1900/UDP.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt IDS/IPS logs for exploitation signatures targeting UPnP (UDP port 1900, SSDP discovery). Flag stack-smashing payloads, oversized buffers, and known CVE-2021-27137-specific exploit patterns in network traffic.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Code Execution on Compromised DD-WRT
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers can 'trigger a code execution vulnerability' but no use case detects successful command execution or shell spawning post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected process spawning, reverse shells, and privileged commands executed on DD-WRT systems. Alert on outbound connections from compromised devices to command-and-control infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner Rule Matches for CVE-2021-27137
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly instructs: 'match against your vulnerability scanner' using CVE-2021-27137 identifier. No use case correlates scanner findings with this CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any vulnerability scanner detection of CVE-2021-27137 or DD-WRT stack-based buffer overflow. Escalate to immediate remediation given active exploitation and federal patch deadline of 2026-07-24.

suggestion.title: Exposed DD-WRT UPnP Service Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker is 'unauthenticated' and exploits 'an internal buffer used by UPnP'—this requires network-facing UPnP service, the direct attack surface. No UC generated to detect exposed UPnP on DD-WRT devices.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound UPnP SSDP (UDP 1900) probes and connection attempts to UPnP management ports (TCP 49152+) from untrusted sources targeting internal DD-WRT devices. Baseline expected UPnP traffic by device; flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: CVE-2021-27137 Scanner Hit Remediation
suggestion.rationale: Article prescribes 'CVE-2021-27137 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and notes federal due-date 2026-07-24, yet pipeline generated zero UC for tracking or prioritizing scanner results against this CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scanner matches for CVE-2021-27137 affecting DD-WRT devices. Cross-reference asset inventory to quantify exposure, prioritize by network exposure (internal vs. Internet-facing), and enforce remediation SLA against federal deadline.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Command Execution on DD-WRT
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'trigger[s] a code execution vulnerability' following UPnP buffer overflow. No execution-phase UC to detect abnormal process spawning or persistence on compromised DD-WRT devices.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DD-WRT syslog for abnormal process forking (especially from init/networking daemons), unexpected shell spawning, or modification of system binaries post-UPnP access. Correlate with network detections of inbound UPnP exploitation attempts for confirmation.

suggestion.title: Malformed UPnP SOAP Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Stack-based buffer overflow requires crafted SOAP payloads with oversized field values. Article specifies 'buffer overflow' attack mechanism, but no network-layer detection for malformed UPnP protocol traffic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag UPnP SOAP requests (typically multipart/related or application/soap+xml over UDP 1900) with payload sizes exceeding baseline, binary injection patterns, or nested encoding anomalies in device descriptor fields. Public PoCs exploit parsing vulnerabilities in UPnP descriptor handling.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: DD-WRT UPnP Service Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability affects UPnP and is actively exploited against 'exposed assets'—pipeline should generate the standard asset-inventory hunt to locate DD-WRT devices running UPnP on the network.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for SSDP (Simple Service Discovery Protocol) announcements and M-SEARCH requests (UPnP discovery traffic on UDP/1900) originating from or destined to internal hosts. Fingerprint responses for DD-WRT user-agent strings or characteristic SOAP/XML service descriptions. Flag any exposed instances accessible from external network segments.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Detection: UPnP Buffer Overflow Payload Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'stack-based buffer overflow' triggered via UPnP—pipeline should hunt for abnormal UPnP control protocol (SOAP) payloads with oversized Device Description or Service Description requests that could overflow internal buffers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect UPnP SOAP/XML requests (HTTP/TCP 1900 or proxied via 49152-49200) with unusually large content payloads, deeply nested XML, or repeated buffer-fill patterns targeting UPnP device services. Correlate with subsequent process crashes or unexpected service restarts on target.

suggestion.title: Process Execution Monitoring: Unauthenticated RCE Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states overflow 'trigger[s] a code execution vulnerability'—pipeline should generate UC monitoring for unexpected child processes spawned from UPnP service context (upnp daemon, miniupnpd, etc.) on affected DD-WRT devices.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation events where parent process is UPnP daemon (upnpd, miniupnpd, ssdpd) spawning child processes with high-entropy names, network utilities (wget, curl), or shell interpreters. Flag any execution outside normal UPnP service scope.

suggestion.title: Network Behavior: DD-WRT Service Crashes and Recovery Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Buffer overflow exploitation typically manifests as service instability before successful RCE—hunt for DD-WRT device reboots, UPnP service restarts, or connection resets correlated with exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate inbound UPnP traffic anomalies (malformed SOAP requests, oversized payloads) with downstream events: connection timeouts to port 1900, abrupt service disconnections, or SNMP trap messages indicating device restart. Multiple failed connection attempts followed by spontaneous device recovery suggests exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scan Baseline: CVE-2021-27137 Exposure Inventory
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV mandates federal remediation by 2026-07-24; article calls for 'quick check across your fleet'—pipeline should generate UC correlating vulnerability scanner findings with network asset inventory to establish exposure baseline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Aggregate all DD-WRT devices from network scans and patch-compliance reporting. Flag any instances with firmware versions vulnerable to CVE-2021-27137 and cross-reference with network exposure (accessible from untrusted networks, internet-facing). Prioritize remediation by federal deadline 2026-07-24.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Post-Exploitation: DD-WRT as Pivot Point
suggestion.rationale: While article focuses on initial exploitation, compromised DD-WRT (often perimeter/edge device) could enable lateral movement into internal networks—pipeline should include UC for detecting suspicious internal traffic originating from compromised DD-WRT.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for internal network connections or DNS queries originating from DD-WRT device that deviate from baseline. Flag scanning activity, unusual port access to internal systems, or tunneling protocols (SSH, VPN) initiated from compromised UPnP daemon context.

suggestion.title: Inventory DD-WRT Devices in Enterprise Network
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Vendor: DD-WRT, Product: DD-WRT' with federal patch due 2026-07-24. Asset discovery is prerequisite for remediation. Pipeline generated zero asset hunting UCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and asset inventory for DD-WRT instances. Cross-reference firmware version against CVE-2021-27137 affected versions. Flag unpatched devices for immediate containment given 3-day federal deadline.

suggestion.title: Detect Exposed UPnP Services on Edge Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'buffer overflow vulnerability...in UPnP' + 'unauthenticated attacker' — UPnP service must be internet-exposed for exploitation to occur. This is the initial-access prerequisite the pipeline ignored.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan external attack surface for open UPnP ports (UDP 1900 SSDP, TCP 49153-65535 control). Correlate inbound traffic to DD-WRT device IPs. Any exposed UPnP = critical risk given active wild exploitation.

suggestion.title: Hunt UPnP SSDP Discovery/Enumeration from External Sources
suggestion.rationale: Pre-exploitation reconnaissance: article describes 'unauthenticated attacker' exploiting buffer overflow — requires prior discovery/fingerprinting of vulnerable UPnP service.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SSDP M-SEARCH multicast queries (UDP 239.255.255.250:1900) and UPnP unicast probes originating from external/untrusted networks. Repeated discovery attempts against same IP = reconnaissance fingerprinting ahead of exploitation.

suggestion.title: Detect CVE-2021-27137 Buffer Overflow Exploitation in UPnP Traffic
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector: article explicitly states 'stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability' in UPnP triggers 'code execution'. Zero exploitation-pattern detection generated by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: IDS should alert on CVE-2021-27137 signatures. Monitor UPnP control protocol (SOAP/HTTP) on control ports for oversized/malformed payloads, null bytes, or known overflow gadgets. Correlation with DD-WRT device IP + failed process execution logs = high-confidence exploitation.

suggestion.title: Detect Child Process Spawning from UPnP Daemon (Post-Exploitation)
suggestion.rationale: Article: successful buffer overflow 'trigger[s] a code execution vulnerability' — code runs in UPnP daemon context. Pipeline missed this execution-confirmation UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any process spawning from UPnP daemon parent (upnpd, miniupnpd, etc.) especially shells, reverse shells, or wget/curl. DD-WRT UPnP typically runs as root — any child process = code execution achieved. Alert on first occurrence.

suggestion.title: Monitor UPnP Port Mapping Configuration Changes (Persistence)
suggestion.rationale: Post-RCE, attacker gains UPnP API control for persistence. Article: exploitation occurs 'in UPnP' — implies attacker can reconfigure device. Pipeline did not model persistence layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor UPnP device descriptor (xml) changes, new port mappings, or device name/serial modifications. Sudden configuration drift on previously-stable DD-WRT = compromise signal. Baseline device state and alert on variance.

suggestion.title: CVE-2021-27137 Scanner Match — DD-WRT Vulnerability Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states this is CISA KEV (actively exploited). Pipeline should have instantiated the asset-exposure template with CVE-2021-27137 substitution as instructed. No use cases generated at all.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search vulnerability scanner and patch-management logs for CVE-2021-27137 matches. Flag any unpatched DD-WRT devices with exposure to external networks or UPnP service binding to WAN interfaces.

suggestion.title: UPnP Service Exploitation Attempt — DD-WRT Buffer Overflow
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability...in UPnP' allowing code execution. This is the exploit vector itself: unauthenticated attacker sends malformed UPnP packets to trigger overflow.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for crafted UPnP SOAP requests or M-SEARCH packets targeting port 1900/UDP or HTTP ports 49152+ on DD-WRT devices. Look for abnormal payload sizes or malformed protocol structures that could trigger buffer overflow conditions.

suggestion.title: Code Execution Post-Overflow — Process Spawning on Network Device
suggestion.rationale: Article states buffer overflow 'trigger a code execution vulnerability.' Success would result in arbitrary code running on DD-WRT device, likely spawning processes or network connections from the device.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DD-WRT devices for unexpected process execution following failed/successful UPnP exploitation attempts. Flag unusual outbound connections initiated from router IP addresses post-compromise.

suggestion.title: DD-WRT Device Inventory — UPnP Service Fingerprint
suggestion.rationale: To hunt this vulnerability, SOC must first know which devices run DD-WRT and expose UPnP. Article targets 'public-facing' applications; implied prerequisite is network-wide UPnP service enumeration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain continuous asset inventory of all UPnP services on the network. Flag any DD-WRT devices (identifiable by User-Agent or default firmware strings in SSDP M-SEARCH responses). Correlate with patch-management records to identify unpatched instances.

suggestion.title: Federal Patch Deadline Compliance — CVE-2021-27137 Remediation Check
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Federal patch due: 2026-07-24.' SOC should have automated hunt to verify no unpatched DD-WRT instances remain after this date; auditors/regulators will ask.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post due-date (2026-07-24), any scanner or log evidence of DD-WRT device *without* the patch for CVE-2021-27137 is a remediation failure. Trigger escalation for all unpatched instances on or after deadline.

suggestion.title: DD-WRT CVE-2021-27137 Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' applies and requires CVE-2021-27137 as the search criterion. Identifies DD-WRT product with unauthenticated RCE via UPnP; inventory and scanning are the primary early-warning control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search vulnerability scanners and asset management for DD-WRT devices with CVE-2021-27137 or unsupported firmware versions. Correlate with network exposure to untrusted segments. Verify all DD-WRT instances have patch deployment evidence before 2026-07-24 federal deadline.

suggestion.title: UPnP Service Exposure from Untrusted Networks
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability affects 'internal buffer used by UPnP' and requires unauthenticated network access; UPnP exposure is the necessary precondition for this CVE to be exploitable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound UDP 1900 traffic (SSDP discovery) and TCP 1900 (UPnP control) reaching DD-WRT devices from external or untrusted networks. Flag any SSDP M-SEARCH responses or UPnP service enumeration replies from internal DD-WRT IPs to external sources.

suggestion.title: DD-WRT Buffer Overflow Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies attack mechanism as 'stack-based buffer overflow' of UPnP buffer; detecting malformed or oversized UPnP payloads would catch active exploitation attempts if IDS signatures are available.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If CVE-2021-27137 IDS/IPS signatures are deployed, trigger on packets with abnormally large SSDP/UPnP protocol payloads, malformed SOAP envelopes, or suspicious buffer-overflow indicators (repeated bytes, NX bypass patterns) destined to port 1900 on DD-WRT targets.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Process & Network Activity from DD-WRT
suggestion.rationale: On successful buffer overflow exploitation, the article states 'code execution vulnerability' will enable attacker commands; detecting unexpected shells, reverse connections, or outbound scanning from compromised DD-WRT is critical for timely breach detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DD-WRT syslog or process logs for unexpected child processes spawned from httpd or UPnP daemon context (reverse shells, curl, wget, netcat, python). Flag outbound DNS queries or connections from DD-WRT to non-RFC-1918 addresses outside the device's normal baseline.

suggestion.title: DD-WRT Firmware Patch Compliance Verification
suggestion.rationale: Article assigns federal 2026-07-24 remediation deadline; compliance monitoring ensures vulnerable instances do not remain exposed past the enforcement date and is a primary control against CISA KEV exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Periodically query asset management and firmware version databases to confirm all DD-WRT devices are either patched, decommissioned, or network-isolated before 2026-07-24. Alert on any device that remains vulnerable and exposed after deadline or shows evidence of failed patch attempts.

suggestion.title: Exposed DD-WRT Instances on Network Perimeter
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated attacker' can exploit—foundational indicator of internet-facing exposure. Asset-exposure hunt is standard CISA KEV triage per source body template reference.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for DD-WRT web interfaces (ports 80/443) and UPnP services (1900/UDP, 5000/TCP) reachable from untrusted networks. Cross-reference firewall edge logs and vulnerability scanner data to identify CVE-2021-27137-vulnerable instances exposed to internet.

suggestion.title: UPnP Buffer Overflow Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'buffer overflow vulnerability...used by UPnP...overflow an internal buffer.' Direct exploitation vector requires detection of malformed SOAP requests, oversized UPnP headers, and known payload signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor UPnP SOAP requests (M-SEARCH, NOTIFY) for abnormally large payloads, malformed headers, or Content-Length mismatches. Detect binary patterns consistent with buffer overflow shellcode in UPnP device description or subscription messages.

suggestion.title: Child Processes Spawned from UPnP Daemon
suggestion.rationale: Article: overflow 'trigger[s] a code execution vulnerability'—successful exploitation manifests as command execution. Unauthenticated RCE via UPnP would spawn shell/binary from upnpd process.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected child processes (bash, sh, nc, wget, curl) spawned by UPnP daemons (upnpd, miniupnpd, ssdp). Correlate with preceding suspicious UPnP network traffic to identify exploitation→execution causality.

suggestion.title: DD-WRT Patch Compliance and Vulnerability Status
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes federal patch due date (2026-07-24) and 'patch lag is the silent killer.' Enterprise must scan fleet for vulnerable versions and track remediation timeline against regulatory deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset scanners for DD-WRT devices running versions prior to patched release. Generate compliance reports showing days-overdue vs. federal deadline, prioritize internet-facing instances, track patch deployment progress.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Persistence on Compromised DD-WRT
suggestion.rationale: Article implies full RCE ('code execution'). Post-compromise, adversary typically establishes persistence via new admin accounts, backdoor users, firewall rule changes, or port forwarding entries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DD-WRT configuration changes for unauthorized user accounts, new SSH keys, firewall rules, or port-forwarding entries outside maintenance windows. Cross-correlate with absence of legitimate admin authentication events.

suggestion.title: Data Integrity Check: Title/Body CVE Mismatch

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Pipeline validation: flag articles where metadata (title, CVE ID) conflicts with body content. Implement consistency check ensuring CVE mentioned in title matches CVE discussed in threat description.

suggestion.title: Unpatched DD-WRT Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Federal patch due: 2026-07-24' and emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer.' Pipeline must surface all DD-WRT devices still running vulnerable firmware versions prior to deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for DD-WRT devices. Cross-check firmware version against known-vulnerable builds. Flag devices without patches applied before federal due-date. Correlate against CISA KEV catalog entry published 2026-07-21.

suggestion.title: UPnP Protocol Exploitation Attempts

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for UPnP requests (UDP 1900, TCP 49152-65535) to DD-WRT devices. Flag payloads exceeding typical UPnP message size. Detect rapid UPnP discovery scans or control message sequences that could trigger buffer overflow. Alert on failed/crashed UPnP services post-attempt.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Code Execution Post-Overflow
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated attacker to overflow...trigger a code execution vulnerability.' Pipeline must detect post-compromise activity following successful buffer overflow exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for process spawning or network outbound connections immediately following UPnP service crashes or restarts on DD-WRT devices. Correlate unexpected command execution with preceding UPnP traffic anomalies. Monitor for shell invocation, reverse shells, or persistence mechanisms launched post-crash.

suggestion.title: CVE-2021-27137 Vulnerability Scanner Detections
suggestion.rationale: Article references template methodology: 'Substitute this CVE wherever the template references `<CVE>`: CVE-2021-27137'. Pipeline must generate scanner-based detection logic for this specific CVE identifier.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scanner results flagging CVE-2021-27137 on any asset. Prioritize active, Internet-facing DD-WRT devices. Cross-reference patch dates against federal deadline (2026-07-24). Escalate if vulnerable device has outbound C2 indicators or anomalous UPnP activity.

suggestion.title: DD-WRT Device Exposure on Internet

Correlate with internal asset inventory. Any gap (asset not in inventory but externally exposed) indicates shadow IT risk for CVE-2021-27137 exploitation.

suggestion.title: CVE-2021-27137 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2021-27137 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and directs to asset-exposure hunt templates. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this direct instruction.

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query patch management and vulnerability data for any DD-WRT system still reporting CVE-2021-27137 vulnerable status after 2026-07-24. Cross-reference with external-exposure scans. Escalate non-patched internet-facing instances to incident response.

suggestion.title: UPnP Buffer Overflow Exploitation Indicators

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and network asset inventory for DD-WRT instances. Cross-reference against patch timeline (due 2026-07-24). Flag any device with version pre-fix date or absence of security patch. Prioritize internet-facing instances with UPnP enabled.

suggestion.title: UPnP Buffer Overflow Exploitation Attempts — Malformed Requests

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution Post-Exploitation — Process Execution from UPnP Service Context

suggestion.title: DD-WRT UPnP Service Crash Anomalies — Exploitation Indicator
suggestion.rationale: Buffer overflow attempts typically trigger service crashes before achieving stable RCE. Pipeline did not capture anomalous daemon termination as an exploitation signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DD-WRT syslog for repeated restarts/crashes of UPnP daemons or web-UI services. Correlate timing with inbound network traffic on UPnP ports. Sudden service restart without administrative action may indicate failed or successful exploitation attempt.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized DD-WRT Configuration Changes — Post-Exploitation Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Successful RCE via buffer overflow would enable persistent access via config modification (firewall rules, user accounts, port forwarding). Pipeline did not generate detection for post-compromise configuration drift.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DD-WRT configuration files (nvram backups, firewall rules, user accounts) for unexpected modifications. Flag creation of new admin accounts, firewall rule additions allowing inbound access, or port-forwarding rules. Correlate with exploit-attempt timeframes.

suggestion.title: CVE-2021-27137 Vulnerability Scan Findings

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor UPnP traffic (SSDP, SOAP) to DD-WRT devices for malformed payloads, overly long request bodies, or repeated rapid requests from external IPs—common buffer-overflow exploitation patterns. Flag spike in failed UPnP probe responses.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Command Execution on DD-WRT Device

suggestion.title: npm Package Execution via Postinstall Scripts

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm install hooks spawning unexpected child processes (PowerShell, cmd, curl, wget) from npm.cmd or node.exe context with parent node_modules path. Correlate with suspicious network egress to non-standard registries or C2 domains.

suggestion.title: CI/CD Pipeline Credential Exfiltration via Compromised Dependencies
suggestion.rationale: Article metadata: 'CI/CD persistence' and 'credential harvesting' are explicit attack vectors. Wormable npm packages can access CI/CD environment variables (AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN, etc.).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag npm postinstall scripts or build steps that read environment variables matching credential patterns (SECRET, TOKEN, KEY, PASSWORD) and exfiltrate via HTTP/DNS. Look for child processes of npm/Node with access to .env or CI provider secret APIs.

suggestion.title: Worm-like Self-Propagation via npm Dependency Chain
suggestion.rationale: Keywords explicitly state 'worm propagation'; npm malware can cascade by installing additional malicious packages or modifying package.json dynamically. Article: 'wormable malware' attack pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm modules with unexpected dependencies added post-installation or package.json mutations during build. Flag dynamic require() calls pulling packages from attacker-controlled registry mirrors. Monitor for npm install retries against unusual registry endpoints.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Compromise via npm Registry Namespace Squatting
suggestion.rationale: Article addresses 'GitHub' and 'supply chain' compromise; npm typosquatting and namespace hijacking are canonical vectors. Keywords: 'GitHub, npm packages, supply chain'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for npm package installations with names similar to popular packages (one-char typos, underscore/dash swaps) or reserved namespaces. Alert on first-time package installs from high-entropy authors. Cross-reference with GitHub account compromise signals.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated Payload Detonation in npm postinstall/build
suggestion.rationale: Keywords: 'obfuscation, payload'; article abstract mentions detection of obfuscated multi-stage payloads in npm attack chains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Base64/hex-encoded or eval()-style code execution in npm scripts or package.json fields. Flag Node.js processes calling Buffer.toString(), atob, or Function() constructor during dependency resolution. Monitor for secondary binary drops to %TEMP% or /tmp.

suggestion.title: Shai Hulud Campaign IOC Detection (npm Artifacts)
suggestion.rationale: Metadata references 'Shai Hulud' campaign; this should trigger threat-actor-specific detection logic for known malicious package names, GitHub accounts, or registry tokens associated with this campaign.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create IOC-driven detections for known-malicious npm packages, authors, and registry credentials tied to Shai Hulud campaign. Alert on installs of flagged packages or from compromised GitHub accounts. Cross-correlate with CDN/registry access logs.

suggestion.title: Detect Internet-Exposed DD-WRT Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' is canonical approach and 'Anything in CISA KEV is currently being exploited.' Exposure is the necessary precondition for exploitation; must identify and flag all WAN-accessible DD-WRT instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify DD-WRT devices (banner-grab on ports 80/443, UPnP SSDP probes on UDP 1900, DHCP fingerprints) reachable from untrusted networks. Cross-reference against patch database to flag any lacking CVE-2021-27137 fix. Priority: patch due date 2026-07-24; flag all unpatched post-deadline.

suggestion.title: Monitor UPnP Traffic for Buffer Overflow Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability...used by UPnP' and 'unauthenticated attacker' — exploitation via crafted UPnP requests is the attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag UPnP traffic (UDP 1900, TCP 1900) to DD-WRT with payload anomalies: oversized Content-Length, null-byte injection, malformed XML, or repeated rapid requests. Cross-correlate with subsequent process spawning or outbound network activity from UPnP daemon context.

suggestion.title: Alert on Post-Exploitation Process Execution from UPnP Context
suggestion.rationale: Buffer overflow 'trigger[s] a code execution vulnerability' — successful compromise results in RCE. DD-WRT process logs will show anomalous command execution under UPnP daemon privileges.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DD-WRT syslog and process audit logs for unexpected child processes spawned from upnp daemon, reverse shell indicators (bash -i, nc -l), or file modifications outside normal UPnP operation. Alert on root-context process creation correlated with UPnP traffic anomalies.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner Findings for CVE-2021-27137
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'even if your scanners say not vulnerable...it's worth one quick check' — scanner discrepancies (false negatives) combined with patch lag pose active risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results (Nessus, Qualys, Tenable) for CVE-2021-27137 matched to DD-WRT firmware. Flag hosts reported as vulnerable OR missing scan coverage. Cross-reference last-patched date against deadline (2026-07-24); escalate if unpatched post-deadline.

suggestion.title: Firmware Version Compliance Check Against CISA KEV Patch Timeline
suggestion.rationale: Federal agencies required to remediate by 2026-07-24 per article; compliance verification is audit requirement. Post-deadline unpatched devices are red-flag risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest DD-WRT firmware version telemetry. Determine patched version from vendor advisory. Alert on any instance with firmware < patched version. If current date >= 2026-07-24 AND device unpatched, escalate to critical compliance violation.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable DD-WRT Instance Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' is recommended and describes 'unauthenticated attacker to overflow an internal buffer used by UPnP.' Pipeline generated zero asset-discovery UCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for exposed DD-WRT instances via UPnP M-SEARCH enumeration on ports 49152/tcp and UDP 1900. Alert on device responses with DD-WRT user-agent headers on Internet-facing network segments. Correlate with vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2021-27137 susceptibility.

suggestion.title: UPnP Buffer Overflow Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article details 'overflow an internal buffer used by UPnP and trigger a code execution vulnerability' but pipeline captured zero exploitation-attempt detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor UPnP SOAP traffic for oversized or malformed payload fields, particularly in SetDevice, GetServiceDescription, or InvokeAction calls. Flag requests with parameter values exceeding expected buffer boundaries or non-RFC-compliant encoding patterns.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Code Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'trigger a code execution vulnerability' but no post-exploitation detection UC provided. Code execution is the stated impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DD-WRT devices for unexpected child process spawning from miniupnpd daemon, shell invocation, or fw rule modifications via iptables following UPnP anomalies. Flag file system writes to /etc or /www directories.

suggestion.title: CVE-2021-27137 Patch Compliance Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Federal patch due: 2026-07-24' and emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' but no compliance or inventory UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for DD-WRT firmware versions released before vulnerability patch date. Generate non-compliance alerts for devices not updated by federal deadline. Cross-reference with scanner data to confirm susceptibility status.

suggestion.title: CVE-2021-27137 Vulnerability Confirmation via Scanner
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'patch lag is the silent killer' and recommends 'one quick check across your fleet.' Requires VM scan correlation: 'Match against your vulnerability scanner' with this specific CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Nessus, Qualys, Tenable, or similar for CVE-2021-27137 findings on DD-WRT devices. Cross-reference patch-management records to identify devices with lag post-2026-07-24 due date. Flag any DD-WRT instance with open UPnP (ports 1900 UDP, 49152+ TCP) remaining unpatched.

suggestion.title: Malformed UPnP Buffer Overflow Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack vector as 'stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability' in 'UPnP' component. Buffer overflows are delivered via oversized or malformed protocol frames to the UPnP daemon.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect abnormally large UPnP SOAP payloads, truncated SOAP headers, or binary-pattern anomalies in UPnP SSDP/Control Point traffic (UDP 1900, TCP 49152+). Flag requests exceeding typical config message sizes or containing non-printable characters.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Command Execution on DD-WRT
suggestion.rationale: Article states overflow 'trigger[s] a code execution vulnerability'—successful exploitation results in shell command execution with router privileges.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DD-WRT syslog for unexpected process spawning, shell invocations, or binary execution (wget, curl, nc, sh, bash) originating from UPnP daemon (upnpd) or network-accessible services outside normal maintenance hours.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized DD-WRT Configuration Modifications
suggestion.rationale: Post-compromise, attackers modify router config for persistence: new port-forwarding rules, DNS poisoning, firewall bypass. Article implies attackers retain code execution post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on modifications to DD-WRT nvram, startup scripts, firewall rules, or port-forwarding tables outside administrative change windows. Correlate timing with exploitation indicators. Flag new WAN-to-LAN port forwarding, DNS hijacking entries, or firewall rule insertions.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Compromised DD-WRT Router
suggestion.rationale: Compromised router becomes pivot point for internal network access via port forwarding, bridging, or tunneling. Article's 'code execution' result implies persistent internal access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sudden spike in port-forwarding usage or new routing rules on DD-WRT. Monitor for bidirectional tunneling patterns (SSH, RDP, SMB reverse shells) traversing router WAN-to-LAN or LAN-to-external. Flag internal traffic flows initiated from router that lack corresponding inbound setup.

suggestion.title: External Probing for Vulnerable DD-WRT UPnP Exposure
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV designation confirms active wild exploitation. Attackers fingerprint exposed DD-WRT instances via UPnP discovery before delivering exploit payload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect repeated UPnP SSDP M-SEARCH discovery requests or UPNP Control Point SOAP probes querying device descriptions from external IPs. Flag patterns consistent with mass scanning (e.g., sequential IP ranges querying port 1900 or 49152).

suggestion.title: Detect DD-WRT UPnP buffer overflow exploitation attempts (CVE-2021-27137)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability...could allow an unauthenticated attacker to...trigger a code execution vulnerability.' This is the active exploitation phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for malformed or oversized UPnP SOAP requests targeting DD-WRT devices, particularly M-SEARCH responses or device-descriptor queries on UDP 1900 and TCP 49152+. Buffer overflow signatures should include abnormally large request payloads or control URL overflows.

suggestion.title: Identify externally-exposed DD-WRT instances with UPnP enabled
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'unauthenticated attacker' access, indicating the attack surface is public-facing UPnP services—asset discovery is the precondition.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for devices responding to UPnP M-SEARCH queries or advertising UPnP on standard ports. Cross-reference asset inventory against patch status for CVE-2021-27137 (due 2026-07-24) to identify unpatched DD-WRT instances.

suggestion.title: Detect command execution following UPnP buffer overflow exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes overflow leading to code execution; detection must capture post-exploitation shell activity on compromised DD-WRT routers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unexpected process spawning, shell invocation, or network connections from DD-WRT devices following UPnP protocol anomalies. Look for reverse shells or command callbacks to external IPs.

suggestion.title: CVE-2021-27137 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs: 'CVE-2021-27137 — match against your vulnerability scanner.' Pipeline generated zero IOCs and zero use cases despite this clear mandate.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag systems where vulnerability scanner reports CVE-2021-27137 (DD-WRT buffer overflow) in live UPnP services. Cross-reference against patch inventory to identify systems still vulnerable past the federal due date 2026-07-24.

suggestion.title: UPnP Service Exposure on Suspected DD-WRT Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'allow an unauthenticated attacker to overflow an internal buffer used by UPnP.' UPnP exposure is the attack surface; pipeline missed this exposure hunt entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for UPnP services (UDP port 1900) responding to SSDP M-SEARCH discovery requests on networks. Correlate exposed UPnP services with known DD-WRT device fingerprints (vendor strings in UPNP device descriptions). Prioritize externally-facing instances.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Buffer Overflow Exploitation Attempts (CVE-2021-27137)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated attacker to overflow...trigger a code execution vulnerability.' The execution phase requires detection logic for buffer overflow and post-exploitation indicators; pipeline generated no use cases for this phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal UPnP service crashes, segmentation faults, or restarts following inbound UPnP requests. Look for signs of successful code execution (unexpected child processes spawned by UPnP daemon, reverse shell indicators, or outbound C2 connections immediately post-UPnP anomaly).

suggestion.title: DD-WRT Patch Lag on CISA KEV Deadline
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes: 'Even if your scanners say "not vulnerable" because of patches, it's worth one quick check...patch lag is the silent killer.' and specifies federal due date 2026-07-24. Pipeline missed the temporal urgency and compliance angle.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any DD-WRT devices where the last recorded patch date is before 2026-07-24 AND CVE-2021-27137 is still unpatched in your asset inventory. Escalate as regulatory/compliance risk if devices remain vulnerable beyond the federal deadline.

suggestion.title: SonicWall SMA1000 RCE exploitation attempt (CVE-2026-15409/15410)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'attackers were exploiting the SMA1000 flaws...to install custom malware weeks before SonicWall disclosed the flaws.' This is active, in-the-wild exploitation of internet-facing remote-access appliances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SonicWall SMA1000 devices for abnormal HTTP/HTTPS requests to admin interface, unauthenticated command execution attempts, or POST payloads containing shell metacharacters. Alert on successful credential-free access to the appliance console or unexpected process spawning post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiSandbox unauthenticated command injection (CVE-2026-39808/25089)
suggestion.rationale: Article notes these 'allow unauthenticated command injection' and were 'later added to CISA's KEV catalog on July 16, after exploitation was detected.' CISA set federal remediation deadline of July 19 under BOD 26-04.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Fortinet FortiSandbox appliances for inbound requests with suspicious command injection patterns (backticks, pipes, semicolons, $() syntax) in URI parameters or POST bodies. Flag unauthenticated access to sensitive endpoints. Correlate with CISA BOD 26-04 alert triggers.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated access to internet-exposed F5 BIG-IP application delivery controller
suggestion.rationale: Article states F5 BIG-IP has 'unauthenticated, network-reachable vulnerabilities affecting internet-facing application delivery controllers and load balancers' at the 'edge of enterprise networks, making them attractive targets for attackers.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful unauthenticated connections to F5 BIG-IP management interface or sensitive REST API endpoints from untrusted external IPs. Monitor for abnormal query strings, POST body injection, or access to /mgmt/ paths without prior authentication events.

suggestion.title: Juniper Junos OS DoS via remotely exploitable crash flaw
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies Juniper flaws in JSA110083/JSA110086 'can be used to crash affected networking devices, potentially causing denial-of-service conditions' and are 'remotely exploitable.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Juniper router/switch device logs for unexpected reboots or crashes correlated with suspicious inbound traffic. Alert on network traffic patterns (malformed packets, specific payload sequences) known to trigger the vulnerability. Track SNMP trap messages indicating device unavailability.

suggestion.title: Delayed infrastructure firmware patching post-CVE-discovery window
suggestion.rationale: Article highlights HP Poly Video advisory shipped 'four months after an included Qualcomm GPU driver vulnerability (CVE-2026-21385) had already been exploited in attacks and added to CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog.' This gap exposes organizations during active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory firmware versions of edge devices (routers, SmartNICs, DPUs, GPUs) and cross-reference against CISA KEV catalog. Alert if an in-use firmware version contains a known-exploited CVE, even if the device is not internet-facing. Measure patching lag (CVE date to firmware update date) and escalate if lag > 30 days for critical/known-exploited flaws.

suggestion.title: State-sponsored exploitation of network infrastructure (Volt Typhoon / Salt Typhoon indicators)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Russian and Chinese state-sponsored threat actors have increasingly targeted vulnerable network edge devices' and names Volt Typhoon and Salt Typhoon as historical actors who 'repeatedly exploited flaws in routers, VPNs, firewalls' to 'breach critical infrastructure and telecommunications providers.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate anomalous access to internet-exposed infrastructure (routers, VPNs, firewalls, ADCs) with threat-intel indicators associated with Volt Typhoon (living-off-the-land techniques, OT scanning patterns) and Salt Typhoon (multi-stage reconnaissance, persistence via firmware/supply chain). Alert on known C2 domains or ASNs linked to state-sponsored infrastructure operators.

suggestion.title: Windmill Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Read
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states flaw allows 'Read Arbitrary Server Files Without Authentication' — this is the core attack path and should generate detection baseline. Pipeline missed entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Windmill for unauthenticated HTTP requests to file-serving or API endpoints that successfully return file contents (especially system files, configs, credentials). Baseline expected auth header presence and alert when absent but request succeeds.

suggestion.title: Windmill Path Traversal Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Arbitrary file read typically exploited via path traversal (../, ..\ sequences). Article describes reading files without auth — traversal is likely mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Windmill HTTP requests containing path traversal sequences or encoded variants (%2e%2e/, ....//,  unicode escapes) in file-path parameters. Flag all successful (200/206 response) traversal attempts.

suggestion.title: Sensitive File Exfiltration via Windmill
suggestion.rationale: Arbitrary file read enables credential/secret theft. Article impact is information disclosure — need detection for reading /etc/passwd, shadow, database configs, API keys.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Windmill service account accessing system-critical or credential-bearing files (SAM, NTDS, .ssh, .aws/credentials, app configs) outside scheduled admin tasks. Correlate with exfiltration channels.

suggestion.title: Windmill Vulnerability Scanning Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires attacking known Windmill version/endpoints. Should detect probing for file-read endpoints or CVE-specific request patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of Windmill endpoint requests (filereader, rawfile, export, etc.). Alert on non-standard endpoints, rapid endpoint enumeration, or requests with suspicious file-path payloads from single source.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation File Enumeration via Windmill
suggestion.rationale: After gaining arbitrary read, attacker will enumerate system for additional targets. Detect behavioral shift from single-file read to systematic file discovery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Windmill returning 200-responses to rapid sequential file-read requests targeting different paths, especially system directories (/etc, /proc, Windows\System32) within short time window.

suggestion.title: Weaponized HTA Execution via mshta.exe
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'weaponized HTA downloader via Microsoft HTML Application Host ("mshta.exe")' as the entry point, but no detection UC was generated despite clear process execution artifact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for mshta.exe spawning with HTA file arguments, particularly when downloaded from malicious staging domains or launched via ClickFix techniques. Correlate with subsequent child process execution of installers or PowerShell.

suggestion.title: Trojanized Software Installer Execution with Embedded Python Bytecode
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'trojanized installers bundled with a malicious Python package' via NSIS scripts executing 'byte-compiled Python code.' Multiple installer names provided (MobaXterm, WebEx, DBeaver, FACEIT) but no detection use case created.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect NSIS installer execution followed by unexpected Python process spawning or memory execution. Flag installers for legitimate software (MobaXterm, WebEx, DBeaver) that originate from non-standard or staging domains (eorthopaedics, web-devtools, zynaris).

suggestion.title: PowerShell Runspace C2 Agent (WLDR) Task Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article details: 'PowerShell-based C2 memory implant...features encrypted beaconing, task queuing, and a Runspace execution engine.' Yet no use case for detecting PowerShell Runspace activity or WLDR agent-specific IoCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PowerShell Runspace-based execution (particularly via CreateRunspace() API) and task queuing patterns. Correlate with network beaconing to known C2 domains (eorthopaedics.com, sastoro.com) that include HWID-based URL parameters (/feed/, /alpha/).

suggestion.title: C2 Beaconing with Hardware-Bound Victim Identifier
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'All C2 URLs incorporate a victim hardware identifier derived from the C: drive volume serial number...enabling the distinct C2 communication for each of the compromised victims.' No detection use case for HWID-parameterized C2 communications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify outbound HTTPS connections to known C2 domains (windowscreenrepairnearme.com, aipythondevs.com) with URL path components matching volume serial number patterns. Detect Polygon smart contract queries (0x6ae382ed...) via Eth_call for fallback C2 domain resolution.

suggestion.title: Browser Credential and Cryptocurrency Wallet Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'stealing browser data and cryptocurrency wallets' and 'Starland RAT...stealing browser data.' Pipeline generated no detection for credential access or wallet enumeration despite explicit victimology.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes accessing browser profile directories (Chrome, Firefox, Edge) and cryptocurrency wallet storage locations. Flag unusual access to Appdata/Local/Google/Chrome/User Data or similar wallet paths. Correlate with Starland RAT or Python process spawning.

suggestion.title: Telegram Bot Beacon and Notification Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article documents: 'actor controls two Telegram bots...used for receiving the implant's execution notification beacons, including messages with victim's machine fingerprints and cryptocurrency wallet inventories.' No detection use case for Telegram bot C2 communications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound HTTPS connections to api.telegram.org and correlation with known malicious bot IDs (8384531459/skuefq_bot, 7993597060/komandastuk_bot). Monitor for JSON-formatted exfiltration payloads containing HWID, machine fingerprints, or wallet inventory data in TLS plaintext or metadata.

suggestion.title: DD-WRT Device Network Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated attacker' can overflow buffer in UPnP service; article explicitly recommends asset-exposure hunts and template substitution for this CVE. Pipeline generated no use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for network-accessible DD-WRT devices on typical UPnP ports (1900/UDP, 5000/TCP) or fingerprint UPnP service banners. Cross-reference against patch compliance baseline for CVE-2021-27137.

suggestion.title: UPnP Service Requests to DD-WRT
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability lies in UPnP buffer handling; 'internal buffer used by UPnP' is the attack surface. No UC addresses anomalous UPnP traffic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect oversized or malformed UPnP requests to DD-WRT devices (SSDP, SOAP). Flag repeated SUBSCRIBE/NOTIFY with abnormal payload sizes or control characters.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Code Execution on DD-WRT
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'trigger a code execution vulnerability' as the impact; pipeline omits execution-phase detection despite RCE being the stated outcome.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected process spawning on DD-WRT devices post-exploitation (shell, wget, curl, nc). Correlate process creation with prior UPnP overflow attempts.

suggestion.title: CVE-2021-27137 Patch Compliance
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Federal patch due: 2026-07-24'; federal agencies required to remediate. No UC validates patch state or inventory closure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scan results and asset inventory for unpatched DD-WRT instances running versions vulnerable to CVE-2021-27137. Flag gaps between scan date and federal remediation deadline.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Service Access to DD-WRT UPnP
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'unauthenticated attacker' vector; no UC models or detects authentication bypass or lack of UPnP ACLs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound traffic to UPnP ports (1900, 5000) from untrusted networks. Flag absence of authentication headers or TLS in UPnP service responses from DD-WRT.

suggestion.title: Detect Exposed DD-WRT UPnP Service Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated attacker' can exploit DD-WRT via UPnP buffer overflow. Asset-exposure hunt template explicitly mentioned but pipeline generated no detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for external sources connecting to UPnP ports (UDP 1900, TCP 49152-49161) on DD-WRT instances. Correlate with device fingerprints indicating DD-WRT presence. Alert on any connection from non-whitelisted external IPs.

suggestion.title: Monitor for Suspicious Process Execution on DD-WRT Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'code execution vulnerability' triggered by stack-based buffer overflow. No use case captures post-exploitation activity on the compromised router.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of legitimate processes on DD-WRT (httpd, UPnP daemon). Alert on unexpected child processes spawned by UPnP service or unexpected binary execution with root/admin privileges on DD-WRT hosts.

suggestion.title: Detect Unexpected Incoming Connections After DD-WRT Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Successful code execution creates C2 opportunity. Article describes remote code execution but pipeline does not suggest hunting for command-and-control or lateral movement indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For confirmed or suspected DD-WRT compromises, monitor outbound connections from the router to unusual destinations (non-ISP DNS, high-entropy domains, known C2 infrastructure). Establish baseline of expected egress and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: CVE-2021-27137 Vulnerability Scanner Match — DD-WRT Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'match against your vulnerability scanner' for CVE-2021-27137. Pipeline generated no asset inventory or scanner integration use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2021-27137 against active asset inventory. Prioritize DD-WRT devices regardless of reported patch status (article notes 'patch lag is the silent killer'). Escalate any unpatched instances with external exposure.

suggestion.title: Detect Buffer Overflow Exploitation Attempts in UPnP Traffic
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'stack-based buffer overflow' in UPnP component. IDS/payload analysis rules needed but pipeline provided none.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Configure IDS signatures to detect oversized or malformed UPnP requests (SSDP, SOAP) targeting known buffer boundaries in DD-WRT UPnP handler. Flag payloads with NOP sleds or shellcode patterns in UPnP request bodies.

suggestion.title: Exposed DD-WRT UPnP Service Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies the attack surface: 'unauthenticated attacker to overflow an internal buffer used by UPnP'. Asset discovery of exposed UPnP services is the critical first hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify DD-WRT devices with UPnP service exposed. Search for inbound SSDP M-SEARCH traffic and responses from known DD-WRT user-agent strings. Inventory UPnP ports (UDP 1900, TCP 49152+) accessible from internet-facing subnets.

suggestion.title: Buffer Overflow Exploit Traffic on UPnP Ports
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploitation mechanism: 'stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability...trigger a code execution vulnerability'. Must detect malformed UPnP requests attempting to trigger overflow.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor UPnP service ports for malformed requests, oversized payloads, or known CVE-2021-27137 exploit signatures. Correlate large or anomalous UPnP packets with immediate process execution on the target device.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Command Execution on DD-WRT
suggestion.rationale: After buffer overflow succeeds, article states attacker gains ability to 'trigger a code execution vulnerability'. Hunt for unexpected shell/process execution post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In DD-WRT syslog or process accounting, detect shell invocation, binary execution from /tmp, or network utility spawning (wget, curl, nc) following UPnP traffic anomalies. Flag command execution with no user interaction baseline.

suggestion.title: CVE-2021-27137 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly instructs: 'CVE-2021-27137 — match against your vulnerability scanner'. Alert on scanner findings of this CVE across fleet.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scanner detections of CVE-2021-27137 on any asset. Correlate positive findings with device patch status, internet exposure, and CMDB criticality. Prioritize federal agency assets and contractors against 2026-07-24 remediation deadline.

suggestion.title: UPnP Reconnaissance and Device Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Prior to exploitation, attackers probe for vulnerable UPnP-enabled devices. Article surface is 'internal buffer used by UPnP' on exposed devices.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect hosts sending repeated SSDP discovery traffic (M-SEARCH) to multiple targets or subnets. Flag scanning patterns targeting UPnP ports across infrastructure blocks, consistent with automated vulnerability reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: UPnP Buffer Overflow Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability... used by UPnP... trigger a code execution'. Requires detection for craft UPnP packets targeting internal buffer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous UPnP requests (SSDP, SUBSCRIBE, NOTIFY) with unusually large payload or binary patterns from external sources to internal DD-WRT devices (typical ports 1900/udp, 5000/tcp). Focus on failed handshakes or immediate disconnects post-request.

suggestion.title: DD-WRT Device Exposure and UPnP Service Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability requires 'unauthenticated attacker' access to UPnP; must hunt for internet-facing DD-WRT routers with exposed UPnP. Article implies public-facing exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for UPnP service banners (M-SEARCH responses, UPNP device descriptions) on external-facing IPs tied to DD-WRT firmware versions. Correlate with CVE-2021-27137 patch version checks.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Code Execution via Compromised UPnP Daemon
suggestion.rationale: Article: buffer overflow 'trigger a code execution vulnerability'. After successful exploit, detect unexpected child processes, reverse shells, or firmware modifications spawned from UPnP daemon context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process children of UPnP daemon (upnpd, miniupnpd, etc.) with suspicious attributes: network connections to C2, shell spawning, firmware read/write operations. Flag deviations from baseline on DD-WRT systems.

suggestion.title: CVE-2021-27137 Vulnerability Scanner Hits
suggestion.rationale: Article in CISA KEV means active exploitation. Splunk/KQL pattern for standard vuln scanner detection of CVE-2021-27137 on internal assets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any vulnerability scanner result (Nessus, Qualys, etc.) reporting CVE-2021-27137 as exploitable on DD-WRT or similar embedded Linux router firmware. Cross-check patch version against vendor advisory.

suggestion.title: Exposed DD-WRT Inventory — Vulnerability Scan
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' is recommended, with template reference and CVE placeholder guidance. Pipeline generated zero UCs despite this clear directive and template-driven suggestion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify internet-exposed DD-WRT devices via asset inventory, vulnerability scanner, or external exposure scans. Prioritize instances running versions prior to patch. Cross-reference against internal netflow to confirm reachability from untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: UPnP Buffer Overflow Exploitation Attempt — Network Layer
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability triggers via 'UPnP' service and 'buffer overflow' mechanism. No network-layer detection suggested despite this being the exploitation vector before code execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor UPnP traffic (UDP 1900, TCP/UDP 5353) to DD-WRT devices for oversized payloads, malformed SOAP requests, or repeated exploitation attempts. Flag patterns consistent with buffer overflow probing or known POC traffic signatures.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Code Execution on DD-WRT
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'trigger a code execution vulnerability' — successful exploitation leads to RCE. No post-compromise monitoring UC exists to detect execution phase despite this being the impact statement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DD-WRT syslog and process execution logs for unexpected process spawning, especially from UPnP daemon context. Flag reverse shells, outbound connections from administrative processes, or unusual command sequences post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: GitHub Release Tag Reassignment to Orphaned Commit
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'The attacker deleted the original version tags and relocated them to the malicious commit' and 'had the attack commit orphaned from any branches, including the main branch.' This tag-manipulation + orphaning combination is the core obfuscation tactic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on GitHub release tags (v*) being reassigned to commits that are not on any active branch, or when tags are deleted and recreated in sequence. Flag scenarios affecting actions with >1k dependents.

suggestion.title: Encrypted Secrets Exposed in Public GitHub Actions Workflow Logs
suggestion.rationale: Core impact vector: 'An attacker with write privileges on the Action repo made a commit that caused encrypted secrets to appear in plaintext in the GitHub Action logs. This could lead to a devastating breach on a public repo where the Action logs are also public.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search GitHub Actions logs (regex: AWS_ACCESS_KEY|GITHUB_TOKEN|API_KEY) for secret patterns appearing after changes to widely-used action repos. Correlate with recent commits to tj-actions/* or similar Action repositories.

suggestion.title: External Code Pull During GitHub Actions Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The attack relied on making an external network call to pull down the attack code, which ultimately led to it being noticed by services that monitor anomalous network activity.' This is the actual detection mechanism that caught the compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests initiated from GitHub Actions runners to non-standard package repositories. Alert on curl/wget of shell scripts or executables from hosts outside githubusercontent.com, registry.npmjs.org, etc.

suggestion.title: Dependency Takeover: Compromise of High-Dependency GitHub Action
suggestion.rationale: Attack scope: 'About 23,000 GitHub repos use this Action... a malicious actor had write access to a repo that 23,000 other repos relied on.' This is textbook supply-chain compromise (T1195).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For GitHub Actions with >1000 forks or >5000 stars, flag: (1) new commits by unfamiliar maintainers, (2) changes to action.yml or run steps that introduce external dependencies, (3) unexpected branches or tags, (4) mass tag updates within 24 hours.

suggestion.title: Orphaned Commit Creation in Shared GitHub Action Repository
suggestion.rationale: Attack enabler: 'Having the attack commit orphaned from any branches, including the main branch' was a deliberate obfuscation step to hide the malicious code from normal branch inspection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In high-value repositories (Actions, widely-forked libs), alert on commits reachable only via direct SHA reference, not via any branch or tag. Escalate if such orphaned commits are subsequently assigned release tags.

suggestion.title: Repository Write Access to Popular Dependency Without MFA Enforcement
suggestion.rationale: Attack prerequisite (root cause unknown): 'As of this writing, it's unknown why the attacker had write permissions on the repo.' Detection should include audit of who holds write access and whether MFA/2FA is enforced.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit members with write/admin access to Action repos; alert if any lack 2FA. Monitor for rapid role changes (user promoted to maintainer, then commits made). Flag if write access is granted via OAuth app or personal access token rather than user account.

suggestion.title: CVE-2021-27137 Vulnerability Scanner Detection

Correlate scanner findings with active DD-WRT systems to prioritize remediation. Flag any systems showing vulnerable status despite claimed patches, as patch lag is noted as a material risk.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Code Execution from UPnP Service Context
