suggestion.title: UPnP Buffer Overflow Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability...used by UPnP.' Protocol-level attack surface (UDP 1900, 5353) must be hunted. 'Unauthenticated attacker' establishes zero-trust requirement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor UPnP multicast traffic (239.255.255.250:1900) to DD-WRT devices for malformed M-SEARCH requests, oversized payloads, or binary anomalies consistent with buffer-overflow exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: DD-WRT Post-Exploitation Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states buffer overflow 'could allow...to trigger a code execution vulnerability.' Pipeline must model post-exploitation behavior. Once buffer overflow succeeds, attacker gains arbitrary code execution on device.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DD-WRT syslog and telemetry for abnormal process spawning, reverse shell connections, web shell uploads to /www directory, or modifications to crontab/startup scripts post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: DD-WRT Asset Inventory and Exposure Mapping
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV is actively exploited. All DD-WRT instances must be discovered and their exposure posture known. 'Unauthenticated attacker' means any network-reachable device is vulnerable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory all DD-WRT devices via DHCP, ARP, subnet scanning. Cross-reference with firewall rules to identify inbound exposure vectors. Flag any internet-facing DD-WRT instances for immediate remediation before 2026-07-24.

suggestion.title: DD-WRT Firmware Patch Compliance Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Federal patch due date 2026-07-24 requires version tracking. Pipeline must correlate device firmware versions against CVE-affected versions and track remediation timeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query all DD-WRT devices for firmware version via management interface. Alert on any firmware version prior to the patched release. Escalate devices still running vulnerable firmware as deadline approaches.

suggestion.title: CVE-2021-27137 Patch Compliance — DD-WRT Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Federal patch due: 2026-07-24' and emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' — asset discovery and vulnerability scanner confirmation are the critical first hunt. Article explicitly references asset-exposure UC template.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners for CVE-2021-27137 matches on DD-WRT devices. Correlate network discovery of UPnP services on port 1900/udp and management interfaces (80, 443) with unpatched inventory. Flag for immediate remediation ahead of federal deadline.

suggestion.title: DD-WRT UPnP Buffer Overflow Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated attacker to overflow an internal buffer used by UPnP and trigger a code execution vulnerability' — direct network-observable exploitation path targeting UPnP daemon.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor UPnP traffic to DD-WRT devices (port 1900/udp, M-SEARCH requests). Hunt for oversized or malformed SSDP/UPnP packets, embedded shellcode patterns, or responses indicating buffer corruption. Correlate with network latency spikes or device reset events.

suggestion.title: DD-WRT UPnP Service Crash or Unexpected Restart
suggestion.rationale: Stack-based buffer overflow typically causes service crash or kernel panic before successful exploitation; article describes vulnerability mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DD-WRT syslog for UPnP daemon crashes, segmentation faults, or unexpected device reboots correlated with UPnP traffic spikes. Observe network perspective: UPnP service timeout followed by device unavailability and recovery.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation DD-WRT Management Interface Access
suggestion.rationale: Successful RCE via buffer overflow implies attacker gains command execution on device; article states 'code execution vulnerability' without specifying privilege context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-exploitation hunting: detect unexpected SSH logins (port 22) or HTTP/HTTPS web-admin panel access (port 80/443) to DD-WRT devices from non-standard sources. Correlate with failed UPnP exploitation events or device uptime resets.

suggestion.title: CVE-2021-27137 Exploit Delivery — Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'trigger a code execution vulnerability' via buffer overflow — payloads will contain shellcode or binary exploits delivered over UPnP protocol or embedded in M-SEARCH responses.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for binary artifacts (ELF/ARM payloads typical of DD-WRT exploits), known public exploits (PoC shellcode signatures), or obfuscated payloads in network captures targeting port 1900 or management interfaces. Correlate with DNS queries for command-and-control domains post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: DD-WRT UPnP Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated attacker can overflow an internal buffer used by UPnP'—search for exposed DD-WRT instances with UPnP service reachable from Internet.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search asset inventory for DD-WRT devices. Cross-reference with network scans showing UPnP service (SSDP port 1900/udp or HTTP on alternate ports) accessible from untrusted networks. Flag externally routable instances for immediate patching.

suggestion.title: UPnP Buffer Overflow Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability' and 'overflow an internal buffer used by UPnP'—detect malformed or oversized UPnP payloads targeting DD-WRT.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor network traffic to/from known DD-WRT devices on UPnP ports. Flag: (1) malformed SOAP requests with payloads exceeding typical device description limits, (2) rapid-fire UPnP discovery requests from single source, (3) HTTP requests with oversized headers or body to UPnP services.

suggestion.title: DD-WRT Post-Exploitation Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions vulnerability 'could trigger a code execution vulnerability'—monitor for unexpected shell/command execution following exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On DD-WRT devices, monitor for: (1) unexpected shell spawns (sh, bash) with suspicious parent processes, (2) invocation of binary executables from /tmp or /var/tmp, (3) execution of wget/curl pulling external payloads, (4) sudden elevation of process or network activity post-UPnP port scanning.

suggestion.title: CVE-2021-27137 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article is CISA KEV (known exploited in wild). Baseline hunt: detect CVE-2021-27137 in all vulnerability scans; federal patch due 2026-07-24.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vuln scanner results for any instances of CVE-2021-27137 on DD-WRT devices. High false-negative risk: scanners may not detect this CVE if running outdated vuln signatures. Flag all DD-WRT hosts regardless of scanner result; cross-reference with asset DB and recent scans.

suggestion.title: CVE-2021-27137 Asset Exposure — DD-WRT Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and cites this CVE as actively exploited in CISA KEV. Pipeline generated zero UCs despite article body stating 'Federal civilian agencies are required to remediate by the published due date'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search asset inventory and vulnerability scans for DD-WRT instances with version exposure to CVE-2021-27137. Prioritise by network exposure to untrusted networks (public-facing per T1190). Correlate with patch status; federal due-date is 2026-07-24.

suggestion.title: UPnP Buffer Overflow Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article body: 'stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability...used by UPnP...trigger a code execution vulnerability.' No UC generated for the actual exploitation technique despite clear description of attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor UPnP traffic (UDP port 1900, SSDP) and HTTP/TCP UPnP control paths for oversized payloads, malformed packets, or patterns targeting DD-WRT default ports (80/443). Alert on any UPnP stack exceptions or process crashes on DD-WRT systems.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Code Execution on DD-WRT
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'trigger a code execution vulnerability.' Pipeline has no execution-phase detection despite article explicitly confirming RCE outcome.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On DD-WRT systems post-exploitation, monitor for unexpected process spawning, shell invocations, or service restarts following UPnP service activity. Flag 'nobody' or 'root' spawning shells outside normal UPnP service lifecycle.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Network Access to DD-WRT UPnP
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated attacker to overflow...used by UPnP.' No discovery/lateral-movement UC for attacker reconnaissance of DD-WRT systems despite this being the attack's prerequisite.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unsolicited UPnP SSDP discovery probes (M-SEARCH on UDP 1900) from external/untrusted networks to DD-WRT subnets. Correlate with DD-WRT device inventory to identify exposed instances responding to discovery attempts.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: DD-WRT Devices (CVE-2021-27137)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and cites template reference. Must identify exposed DD-WRT instances vulnerable to unauthenticated buffer overflow.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory and correlate DD-WRT devices from network discovery, HTTP banners, UPnP device advertisements. Cross-reference against patched versions post 2026-07-24. Alert on port 80/443 HTTP responses containing DD-WRT version strings or UPnP service descriptions matching vulnerable firmware builds.

suggestion.title: UPnP Stack Overflow Attack Detection (CVE-2021-27137)
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies vulnerability as 'stack-based buffer overflow' in 'UPnP' service handled by DD-WRT. Requires signature/behavioral detection of oversized or malformed UPnP payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor UDP/TCP traffic to UPnP ports (typically 1900/5000) from external sources to DD-WRT devices. Flag packets with abnormally large UPnP SOAP payloads, repeated M-SEARCH requests with crafted bounds, or NOTIFY messages exceeding typical message sizes. Correlate with process spawns or network connections on affected routers post-packet receipt.

suggestion.title: CVE-2021-27137 Patch Compliance Verification
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes federal due-date 2026-07-24 and that 'patch lag is the silent killer.' Compliance hunting required to identify unpatched DD-WRT instances in fleet.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability management system and device inventory for DD-WRT instances with versions prior to known-patched builds. Cross-reference firmware release dates; alert on any device still running vulnerable branches after federal due-date. Correlate with network exposure (public IPs, exposed ports).

suggestion.title: DD-WRT UPnP Service Enumeration and Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated attacker' can exploit via 'internal buffer used by UPnP.' Active scanning and exploitation attempts will probe UPnP services; detection of such probes is critical.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for repeated UPnP M-SEARCH or SSDP requests originating from external IPs to DD-WRT devices. Detect anomalous UPnP request patterns (high request frequency, unusual headers, known exploit payloads). Alert on successful buffer-overflow indicators (device reboot, service crash, sudden port state changes post-UPnP interaction).

suggestion.title: DD-WRT Public Interface Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes 'unauthenticated attacker to overflow an internal buffer' — exposure is prerequisite for exploitation. Article explicitly references 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' but pipeline generated no corresponding UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for internet-routable DD-WRT instances responding to UPnP/SSDP discovery (UDP/1900) or HTTP management interfaces on standard ports. Correlate with CVE-2021-27137 firmware versions from inventory scans.

suggestion.title: UPnP Buffer Overflow Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability...used by UPnP' as the attack mechanism. This is the execution phase and requires IDS/packet-level detection absent from pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for IDS signatures matching CVE-2021-27137 buffer overflow, malformed SSDP/UPnP HTTP requests with oversized payloads, or exploit patterns from known POCs targeting affected DD-WRT firmware versions.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Callback Detection from Compromised DD-WRT
suggestion.rationale: Article outcome is 'code execution vulnerability' implying attacker gains device control. Post-compromise detection should monitor for unexpected outbound connections or command injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful UPnP exploit attempts (IDS alerts) with outbound HTTP/DNS queries to known malware C2 or suspicious external hosts from the DD-WRT device in the 5 minutes post-exploitation window.

suggestion.title: CVE-2021-27137 Patch Compliance — CISA KEV Due Date Tracking
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status + federal patch due date 2026-07-24 makes this a compliance-first detection. Pipeline should surface the deadline and operationalize inventory scans with urgency.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset DB for unpatched DD-WRT instances with firmware versions vulnerable to CVE-2021-27137. Flag any still unpatched after 2026-07-24 federal due date. Cross-reference against network exposure scans to identify public-facing instances.

suggestion.title: DD-WRT Asset Exposure Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated attacker' can exploit UPnP—no auth required, meaning any exposed DD-WRT device on the Internet or reachable subnets is at immediate risk. Pipeline must surface all instances. Cite: 'unauthenticated attacker to overflow an internal buffer used by UPnP and trigger a code execution vulnerability.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all DD-WRT devices by querying vulnerability scanners for CVE-2021-27137, scanning for UPnP service signatures on UDP/1900 and TCP/1900, and cross-checking device firmware versions against vendor advisory. Federal patch deadline is 2026-07-24; flag any unpatched instance.

suggestion.title: UPnP Buffer Overflow Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'stack-based buffer overflow' via 'internal buffer used by UPnP'—this is a protocol-level attack on the UPnP service itself. Detection must hunt for malformed or oversized UPnP payloads. Cite: 'contains a stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated attacker to overflow an internal buffer used by UPnP.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor UPnP protocol traffic (UDP/1900, TCP/1900) for payloads exceeding normal UPnP SSDP/SOAP message sizes, malformed M-SEARCH requests, or SOAP method calls with unusually large Content-Length headers or parameter values. Alert on any attempt to trigger stack overflow condition.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Child Process Spawning from UPnP Service
suggestion.rationale: Article states buffer overflow 'trigger[s] a code execution vulnerability'—successful exploitation will result in arbitrary code execution in the UPnP service context. Detection must catch new processes or network connections initiated from the UPnP daemon. Cite: 'trigger a code execution vulnerability.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DD-WRT devices for unexpected child processes spawned by the UPnP daemon (miniupnpd or equivalent) or unexpected network connections (DNS queries, outbound TCP/UDP) originating from the UPnP service context. Any such anomaly post-exploitation attempt indicates successful code execution.

suggestion.title: DD-WRT Firmware Patch Compliance
suggestion.rationale: Federal deadline is 2026-07-24 per article—organizations must verify remediation. Pipeline must generate compliance query to track patched vs. unpatched versions across inventory. Cite: 'Federal patch due: 2026-07-24.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for all DD-WRT instances, extract firmware version, and cross-reference against vendor security advisory for CVE-2021-27137. Flag any device with firmware version below the fixed build as non-compliant. Generate trending report of patch adoption rate leading up to and past the 2026-07-24 deadline.

suggestion.title: Suspicious DNS/C2 from DD-WRT Compromised Devices
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation, attacker will likely establish command-and-control or exfiltration from the compromised device. Detection should flag anomalous egress from DD-WRT. No explicit mention in article, but standard TTPs post-RCE. Cite: 'trigger a code execution vulnerability' implies attacker has code execution and will execute commands.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual DNS queries or outbound network connections from DD-WRT devices, especially to non-RFC1918 destinations or known malicious C2 infrastructure. Correlate with exploitation-attempt detections to identify successfully compromised devices initiating command retrieval or exfiltration.

suggestion.title: DD-WRT Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated attacker' and implies network-accessible devices; CISA KEV requires asset inventory and exposure validation. Phrase: 'could allow an unauthenticated attacker to overflow an internal buffer used by UPnP.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for internet-facing DD-WRT instances via network scanning (HTTP banner fingerprinting on port 80/443 for DD-WRT web interface), vulnerability scanner results matching CVE-2021-27137, and DNS/WHOIS correlation with known DD-WRT distributions. Prioritize devices with UPnP service enabled (UPnP listener on UDP 1900).

suggestion.title: UPnP Buffer Overflow Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability explicitly targets UPnP protocol. Phrase: 'buffer used by UPnP and trigger a code execution vulnerability.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for malformed UPnP M-SEARCH requests (UDP 1900) and SOAP/XML payloads with unusually long buffer fields or control characters. Flag POST requests to UPnP control URLs with payload sizes exceeding normal bounds or non-ASCII byte sequences indicating shellcode injection.

suggestion.title: DD-WRT Process Execution Anomalies Post-Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'trigger a code execution vulnerability'; post-exploitation should manifest as unexpected process spawning from router firmware contexts. Phrase: 'trigger a code execution vulnerability.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process spawning (fork/exec) originating from UPnP daemon processes (upnpd, miniupnp) or router web service processes. Correlate with unusual network outbound connections, DNS queries, or file modifications in /tmp or /var directories following UPnP traffic anomalies.

suggestion.title: CISA KEV Patch Compliance Validation
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entries carry federal remediation deadlines and audit implications. Phrase: 'Federal patch due: 2026-07-24.' Validate scanning infrastructure captures this deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Tenable/Qualys/OpenVAS results for unpatched DD-WRT instances matching CVE-2021-27137; cross-reference asset inventory for end-of-life devices unable to receive firmware updates. Escalate any findings to compliance team with patch deadline date (2026-07-24).

suggestion.title: UPnP Default Credential Brute-Force (Upstream Vector)
suggestion.rationale: UPnP vulnerability requires network access; prior compromise via default credentials is a common precursor in DD-WRT exploitation chains. Article implies network-exposed devices are already at risk; many are configured with defaults.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DD-WRT web interfaces (port 80/443) for rapid failed login attempts using common default credentials (admin/admin, root/12345, etc.). Correlate with subsequent UPnP protocol anomalies or process execution within 5 minutes of authentication success.

suggestion.title: DD-WRT Firmware Backdoor Persistence Check
suggestion.rationale: Once code execution achieved, attackers typically persist via firmware modification or scheduled tasks. Article describes stack-overflow leading to code execution; post-exploitation persistence is implied.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain cryptographic checksums of DD-WRT firmware files (/bin, /sbin, /usr/bin) and cron/at jobs. Alert on firmware file modifications, new cron entries creating reverse shells, or presence of known DD-WRT backdoor binaries (e.g., unauthorized telnet/SSH daemons).

suggestion.title: CVE-2021-27137 DD-WRT Asset Inventory and Patch Status
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names CVE-2021-27137 affecting DD-WRT; pipeline extracted zero IOCs. CISA KEV designation mandates asset discovery and remediation tracking against federal deadline 2026-07-24.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and asset management system for DD-WRT instances. Cross-reference patch management to identify systems not yet remediated by federal deadline. Correlate with network discovery data to identify internet-exposed instances.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated UPnP Buffer Overflow Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated attacker' can 'overflow an internal buffer used by UPnP.' Requires network-level detection for exploitation activity on UDP 1900.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for oversized, malformed, or anomalous SSDP (UPnP discovery) packets on UDP 1900. Alert on fuzzing patterns (rapid requests, increasing payloads, null bytes, format string attempts) consistent with buffer-overflow exploitation.

suggestion.title: Public-Facing DD-WRT UPnP Service Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article implies exploitation of 'public-facing' routers. UPnP on edge devices is critical exposure vector; pipeline missed network discovery UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan internet-facing interfaces for UPnP service responses (UDP 1900 SSDP advertisements). Flag any DD-WRT instances responding to UPnP discovery requests from untrusted networks or identified in external asset scans.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation RCE Artifacts from DD-WRT Buffer Overflow
suggestion.rationale: Article describes buffer overflow 'trigger[ing] a code execution vulnerability' — implies remote code execution capability. Need detection for execution artifacts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DD-WRT syslog for unexpected process spawning, shell invocation, or service restarts immediately following UPnP traffic anomalies. Correlate timing of exploitation attempts with system behavioral changes.
